TOP NEWS " Texas requests $10B in reimbursements from federal government for Operation Lone Star" via Jeff Bell \--- Gov. Greg Abbott is officially applying to get reimbursed for what Texas spent on border security during the Biden administration. The Texas governor said he submitted the paperwork to the federal government on Wednesday. Abbott said under the Biden administration, Texas spent $10 billion of taxpayer money on Operation Lone Star that included sending Texas National Guard soldiers and state troopers to the border and building border barriers. "In March 2021, I launched Operation Lone Star to fill in the dangerous gaps created by the Biden Administration's refusal to secure the border," Abbott said in a statement. "For four years under Biden, Texas spent more than $10 billion of taxpayer money to secure the border. I have formally submitted Texas' application to the Department of Homeland Security for reimbursement of costs Texas had to incur because President Biden refused to do his job." () " Hundreds of data centers are coming to Texas. Here's what you need to know." via Alejandra Martinez - In the span of a couple years, hundreds of massive electricity- and water-hungry data centers have proposed construction in Texas -- a veritable gold rush for those capitalizing on the sudden demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. There are at least 248 data center projects planned across the state, according to a Texas Tribune recent analysis. Experts and industry representatives say the Lone Star state is just the place for the data center revolution because of its friendliness to business and lax regulation. And while industry leaders promise economic gains, some Texans fear the pressure data centers could add to the state's already strained resources like water and energy. Gov. Greg Abbott recently moved from calling Texas an "epicenter" of AI development to announcing he would make regulating the industry a priority for state lawmakers during the 2027 legislative session. () " How history is guiding a U.S. attempt to beat screwworm again" via Jayme Lozano Carver -- The New World screwworm has entered the country, and if history is any indication, the parasite's devastating effects on the U.S. could last for decades. The screwworm re-emerged following years of warnings from Central America and Mexico officials of the impending outbreak. Then last year, the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) cut funds for screwworm monitoring in Central America. Government officials continue to work to pinpoint how screwworm entered the U.S. while cases continue to creep up. While the financial impact of this modern-day outbreak is still unknown, the USDA estimates the industry saved more than $900 million a year as a result of eradication in the past. () " Tensions with landowners rise as a raft of gas pipelines push through Texas properties" via Brandon Mulder - In 2022, Ty and Leslie Eggemeyer received a notice in the mail that would shape the next four years of their lives. Their nearly 4,000-acre wildlife resort in Lampasas County -- featuring everything from giraffes to wildebeests and gazelles -- was along the route of a planned pipeline project proposing to connect the Permian Basin to the Gulf Coast. Matterhorn Express, a pipeline entity majority-owned by the Austin-based infrastructure company WhiteWater Midstream, would transport Permian Basin gas 580 miles to the Houston area using the powers of eminent domain to sail through thousands of acres of private property. On Artemis Ranch, the 42-inch pipeline would clip through just a half-mile strip of the property. But it would create an eyesore near the ranch's entrance, visible to guests coming for wedding parties, corporate retreats and other events. "We've been pushing our ranch as an eco-tourism ranch. How does that fit with a 42-inch gas pipeline running through the front entrance?" Ty Eggemeyer said. () " UT Austin researchers develop jacket that pulls drinking water from the air" via Henrikson -- University of Texas at Austin researchers have developed a jacket that pulls drinking water directly from the air, a technology they said could help hikers, farm workers and emergency responders stay hydrated in harsh conditions. According to UT Austin, testing showed the jacket produced between 400 and 900 milliliters of drinking water per day, depending on humidity levels. "We designed these water harvesting jackets by engineering these very special textile fabrics," said Professor Guihua Yu with the Texas Materials Institute at UT Austin. The researchers published their work in the month's new issue of Science Advances. According to the researchers, the specially engineered fabric can capture water from the atmosphere across a wide range of environments, from arid regions to humid climates like Central Texas. The textile collects moisture from the air and funnels it into detachable harvesting units, where the water is released and collected for drinking. Traditionally, atmospheric water-harvesting systems have relied on large, stationary devices that collect moisture from the air. Researchers said the new wearable textile is designed to make the technology portable. () 2026 " Jasmine Crockett's silence could hurt James Talarico's U.S. Senate chances in November" via Andrew Schneider - The Democratic Party's state convention is set to open Thursday in Corpus Christi. One of the most notable absences among the roster of speakers is U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett. The Dallas congresswoman has declined so far to campaign on behalf of her erstwhile rival in Texas' Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate, Austin state Rep. James Talarico. Texas Southern University political scientist Michael Adams said that could hurt the voter turnout Talarico likely needs to have a chance of beating Attorney GeneralKen Paxton , the Republican nominee, in November's election. Texas Democrats are trying to break a three-decade losing streak in Senate campaigns. "Black women voters [have] been the staple or the buckle, as we like to say, of Black voters in particular [for] Democratic turnout," Adams said. () " 'I'd love to have his help': Paxton reveals what he told Cornyn after Senate runoff" via Eleanor Dearman - "By the way, did John Cornyn ever call and concede?" Lt. Gov.Dan Patrick posed the question to Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in an interview for the inaugural episode of the lieutenant governor's new Lt. Dan podcast. He sat at a wooden table fashioned with a microphone and branded mug, as Paxton responded from a video screen facing the head of the table. The episode was released about a month after Paxton defeated longtime Republican incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in a bruising primary runoff. Paxton faces state Rep. James Talarico , the Democratic nominee for the statewide seat, in the Nov. 3 general election. The interview touches on the theme of party unity that's being pushed by GOP leaders, as Cornyn voters weigh whether to support Paxton in the fall. "So he sent me a text," Paxton said. "I never saw a phone call from him, but I texted him back and I said, 'Thank you. You know, I appreciate your service to Texas and to the country and I'd love to get together and talk.'" () " Republican Representatives from AG Paxton's home turf originally campaigned against him, explain why they now back him" via Jack Fink - Two Republican members of the Texas House who have butted heads withKen Paxton and endorsed incumbent John Cornyn told CBS News Texas they are fully supporting the Attorney General in his race against Democratic State Representative James Talarico. Representatives Matt Shaheen of Prosper and Jeff Leach of Allen are from Collin County, Paxton's home turf. "I think the Republican voters spoke loud and clear that they preferred Ken Paxton," said Shaheen. "He won overwhelmingly in the primary. We need to motivate our base, make sure that the Republican base gets out. Ken Paxton has clearly demonstrated that he can get our Republican base out. So, we look forward to helping him out and doing everything we can to get him and all of our awesome Republican candidates across the goal line." "Primaries are a time for us to pick our roster, to pick our candidates, to kind of have our family fights if you will," said Leach. "But once the slate is chosen, which the voters of Texas have done, it's incumbent upon us and for all Republicans to get out and support the ticket from the top to the bottom. So, it's never a question for me. We know who our candidates are headed into November, and we're going to do everything we can to make sure every single one of them, from the top to the bottom, is elected." () " Texas Democrats leave convention united in effort to end GOP's 30-year hold on Texas" via Blaise Gainey - Thousands of people filled the stands of the Hilliard Center Arena in Corpus Christi for the Texas Democratic Convention's closing rally Saturday, where Sen. Bernie Sanders made the final keynote speech. "We know that when we stand together as one people, the oligarchs and all of their money will never defeat it," said Sanders, a Vermont Democrat. "Let's go out and do it." His message was met with loud roars and cheers from the crowd, and it echoed one overall theme stressed by the party throughout their convention: The state's Democratic leaders urged Texans to unite behind a common message and turn their energy into votes ahead of November's consequential midterm elections. Sander's speech capped the three-day convention where democratic delegates, volunteers, and elected officials urged activists to organize for the 2026 elections. Candidates and party leaders argued that winning political power in the state is essential for protecting public education, expanding health care access and safeguarding rights they say are under attack -- both in the Lone Star State and nationally. () " Senator Nathan Johnson campaigns for Texas attorney general, prioritizes consumer protection laws" via Norman - State Sen. Nathan Johnson is campaigning across Texas as he seeks the office of attorney general. State Senator Nathan Johnson of Dallas is seeking the office of Texas attorney general. Johnson has represented Senate District 16 since 2018 and continues to practice law while serving in the Texas Legislature. He earned his law degree from the University of Texas at Austin. During a campaign stop in the Crossroads, Johnson said his campaign is centered on restoring public trust in the attorney general's office and ensuring it serves all Texans. Johnson argued that the office should focus on enforcing laws that protect consumers rather than pursuing partisan political agendas. "Consumers are having their daily rights violated," Johnson said. "As a legislator, I've passed laws to protect people from that, but those laws have to be enforced. When you're using the attorney general's office as a diversionary tactic or a partisan tactic instead of something that actually protects consumers, you're not doing your job. People aren't getting what they're paying for with their tax dollars, and they don't have an office they can trust." () STATE GOVERNMENT " Texas Business Court Caseload Accelerates and Broadens After House Bill 40 Expands Jurisdiction" via Marisa Secco Giles , Aaron Lira & Olivia Landry -\- The Texas Business Court's second year is off to a faster start than its first, and the expansion of its jurisdictional reach through House Bill 40 appears to be contributing to the uptick in its caseload. As discussed in prior coverage of House Bill 40, which became effective Sept. 1, 2025, the jurisdiction-expanding legislation lowered the value threshold to qualify as a "qualified transaction" from $10 million to $5 million; lowered the related amount-in-controversy threshold from $10 million to $5 million; provided jurisdiction over a broad range of intellectual property disputes; provided jurisdiction to enforce arbitration agreements and review arbitral awards in most cases where the underlying claim would otherwise fall within the Business Court's jurisdiction; and allowed pre-Sept. 1, 2024 cases to be transferred to the Business Court when there is agreement between the parties and the Business Court. House Bill 40 also allows the amount in controversy threshold in certain types of cases to be met by aggregating the total amount of all joined parties' claims. From its inception Sept. 1, 2024, through the end of the first quarter of 2026, the Business Court received approximately 367 cases through either original filings or removals. Close to half of those cases were added after the effective date of House Bill 40. In the Eleventh (Houston) Division, the Business Court received nearly as many cases since House Bill 40 went into effect as it did during its entire first year. In the Third (Austin) Division, the Business Court received even more cases since House Bill 40 went into effect than it did during its first year of operation. () " Slot machines are "illegal," the AG says, but local prosecutors have final say." via Yamil Berard - The Fortune Club, a gameroom in Ben Wheeler, Texas, about 75 miles southeast of Dallas, offers a new generation slot machine that looks like the real thing, but its owners and a district judge in east Texas say is "skill based," not chance, and therefore legal. The bitter fight over what constitutes a gambling device in Texas has grown yet another layer of complexity. A new generation of bell-ringing slot machines has been popping up across Texas since a trial judge in east Texas deemed them perfectly legal roughly two years ago. So, even though the machines look and sound like the real thing, the decision by former 336th District Court Judge Laurine Blake determined they are games of skill, not games of chance. According to her ruling, they include memorization elements similar to the vintage Simon game that was a symbol of 1980s pop culture. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Dallas woos Morgan Stanley with incentives for billion-dollar development" via Wooten - The Dallas City Council on Wednesday approved an $18.5 million incentive package and additional tax abatements as Morgan Stanley seeks to expand its "Y'all Street" presence by occupying a high-rise at the corner of McKinney Avenue and Fairmount Street. Under the terms of the deal, Morgan Stanley would undertake a two-phase development project. Morgan Stanley would lease roughly 700,000 square feet in the new Uptown Tower for 16 years with an expected move-in date of 2031. While waiting for the high-rise, the banking giant would lease about 255,000 square feet at downtown's Fountain Place skyscraper at 1445 Ross Ave. for just over four years. Morgan Stanley plans to invest nearly $97 million and will bring 1,500 jobs to Fountain Place by 2031. The firm will invest over $684 million in the new Uptown building by 2031 and employ 3,800 people at the site by the end of 2035 with the possibility of additional relocations. The developer is expected to invest another $650 million to build Morgan Stanley's new office, bringing the value of the estimated development to more than $1.3 billion, city documents show. The Fountain Place skyscraper and the planned Uptown site will be designated as neighborhood empowerment zones. Morgan Stanley will receive a 90% tax abatement on its property at Fountain Place for five years. The bank will also receive a 90% tax abatement on its property at the new site for 10 years. The city estimates it will forgo $4.8 million in tax revenue. () " Council members demand meeting about how $75M in arena deal should be spent" via Iszler - A rendering shows the planned new Spurs arena downtown and the broader Project Marvel sports and entertainment district. As city officials prepare to hash out agreements for a new Spurs arena downtown, three City Council members are calling for a special meeting to discuss how $75 million from the NBA franchise should be spent. Teri Castillo , Marina Alderete Gavito and Sukh Kaur said in a memo that they want residents, business owners, artists and labor union representatives to have a chance to weigh in on how the money should be allocated. In a non-binding term sheet for financing the $1.3 billion arena, Spurs owners have pledged to give the city $2.5 million annually over 30 years for so-called "community benefits." It would be distributed during the term of the franchise's lease with the city for the arena, which could begin in 2028. There are no stipulations about what the money must be used for. () " Harris County immigrant legal services program paused by Texas Supreme Court" via Al-Shaikh -\- Funding for a Harris County program is now on hold after the Texas Supreme Court put the brakes on it. The Texas Supreme Court temporarily blocked the county's multi-million-dollar immigration legal assistance program after finding "serious doubt" about whether the county has the legal authority to operate it. The program offers free legal services to county residents facing deportation who qualify. The state supreme court said they have enough legal questions to put a temporary pause on funding. On Friday, the court temporarily blocked the county from spending money through its Immigrant Legal Services Fund while the case plays out. () " Advocates take aim at police spending in Austin budget" via Austin Sanders - A coalition of more than 30 community groups is calling on city leaders to restore millions in proposed cuts to social service contracts and fund additional programs by limiting growth in the Austin Police Department budget. The coalition this week released a "community investment budget" calling for roughly $36 million for programs including emergency rental assistance, violence prevention, homelessness services, mental health response and inclement weather sheltering. The proposal comes weeks before Austin City Manager T.C. Broadnax is expected to release an austerity budget proposal for the upcoming fiscal year that must account for a $25 million shortfall. Broadnax has already indicated he plans to achieve that by cutting $17 million from social service programs. The coalition is asking the City Council to reject that approach. () " SAISD board picks next superintendent as two trustees raise concerns" via Noah Alcala Bach - San Antonio ISD trustees selected Adrian Bustillos as the lone finalist for superintendent at a meeting Wednesday night. The San Antonio Independent School District board picked its next superintendent on Wednesday in a 5-2 vote. Adrian Bustillos, a chief transformation officer in a Houston-area district, is slated to take the top job in San Antonio's oldest school system, replacing outgoing Superintendent Jaime Aquino. Bustillos' career in public education began two decades ago in El Paso ISD, where he taught science. He rose through the district's ranks, becoming an assistant principal in 2009 and serving in two central office roles from 2018 to 2019. After 13 years in El Paso, Bustillos became the chief transformation officer at Aldine ISD, a largely suburban district just north of Houston that serves about 52,000 students across nearly 70 campuses. The two dissenting trustees -- on an often unified board -- who voted against the selection were Jacob Ramos and Stephanie Torres. () " Austin ISD is closer than ever to a state intervention. Here's what can happen" via Keri Heath and Tony Plohetski - When the Texas Education Agency announced in 2023 that it would seize control of the Houston Independent School District over the academic failings of one campus, many Austin families watched with deep concern about what it would mean for the state's largest public school district. Crystal Brothwell Hernandez , president of the Austin Council of PTAs who has nine children in Austin ISD schools, described seeing Texas' largest urban school district fall into the hands of the state as part of a conservative grab for public schools. She believes the state doesn't know what local schools need and fears takeovers turn learning into a cookie-cutter approach and rob parents of their voice in their child's education. Brothwell Hernandez is worried Austin ISD may be next on TEA's list of districts to take over, as the state has targeted the district in a number of recent investigations and flagged AISD for its academic struggles. () " Austin ISD slows boundary plan, pushes some changes to 2027-28 school year" via Brian Murray - Austin Independent School District (AISD) is slowing plans to realign its school district boundaries that impact which schools students attend. Originally, AISD was aiming to implement districtwide changes for the 2027-28 school year. But now, according to an email to families, the plan will be shifted into a two-phase approach. The first phase will address "urgent" boundary issues the district said 'cannot wait'; The second phase aims to be a comprehensive change to campuses' boundaries across the district. AISD said the new timeline would allow it to "make better, more sustainable long-term decisions along with the community." Below is a breakdown of the two-phase plan to address issues about staffing, overcrowded schools and the budget. Phase one includes "urgent" boundary realignment for select campuses with "projected growth that would otherwise require portables we cannot afford." It is unclear which schools will be impacted. The proposal for these changes will be announced next month, and the school board will vote on them in September. Phase one also includes defining Marshall Middle School's attendance area for the first time. AISD will begin planning phase two in January 2027 and is expected to bring school closures. The school board will vote on these changes in fall 2027. "Taking this extra time allows us to monitor enrollment trends following recent closures, analyze data from our October enrollment snapshot, and further progress our academic visioning," AISD Superintendent Matias Segura wrote in the email. "We want to ensure that future engagement opportunities take place during the school year when it is most convenient for families to participate." AISD cited concerns over the budget and enrollment efforts as some causes of the need for realigning boundaries. Under-enrolled schools financially strain the district. Sean Mooney , a real estate agent with Mooreland Properties, said affordability in the housing market has made it hard for young families with younger children to access some areas in Austin, leading to an aging population and underpopulated schools. () #TXLEGE " Texas leaders are asking data centers how much water they use. Most aren't responding" via Alejandra Martinez - Data centers use water to cool their massive arrays of computer servers. A state agency sent out a survey to figure out how much, but less than a third of the companies responded. Data centers need a lot of water and energy. State officials want to know how much, and they hoped a survey sent to data center companies would give them the answers. But at a legislative hearing Tuesday in Austin, they were told less than a third of the companies surveyed responded. "Bad data, bad study," said state Rep. Brad Buckley , R-Salado, a member of the House Natural Resources Committee. () " Texas Lawmakers Again Eye Regulation for Proxy Advisory Firms" via Holly Hansen - State lawmakers are considering bolstering a state transparency law and imposing further regulations for proxy advisory firms, and may subpoena two foreign-owned advisors over ongoing concerns about conflicts of interest -- and claims the firms advised companies against relocating to Texas. During the 89th Legislative Session, state lawmakers approved Senate Bill (SB) 2337 requiring proxy advisory firms to disclose when their recommendations are based on "non-financial factors" or "conflict with other proxy advisory services." Holly Hansen is a Senior Reporter for The Texan where she has written extensively on criminal justice, public corruption, politics, and property rights, and is one of the state's most recognized journalists covering Houston and Harris County. She is a frequent guest on radio and television shows, discussing local, state, and federal public affairs. She graduated from the University of Central Florida with a degree in History, has called Texas home for three decades, and now lives in the Austin area where she enjoys the outdoors and reading historic literature. () BUSINESS NEWS " Tesla's tiny robotaxi fleet could 'dramatically scale,' Texas official says" via Andrea Guzm an - Tesla Inc. officially began operating a robotaxi service in Austin a year ago. Now, leadership at the Texas Department of Transportation thinks its fleet could start to surge. TxDOT Executive DirectorMarc Williams experienced a production version of the Cybercab at the Texas Innovation Invitational and wrote on LinkedIn afterward that the purpose-built robotaxi will "dramatically scale" Tesla's cab operations over the coming months. "Observing this vehicle firsthand -- from its design and butterfly doors to the cargo trunk configuration -- provides a tangible example of how quickly our transportation system is evolving," Williams wrote. "Sitting inside the cabin, the complete absence of traditional driver controls underscores a significant shift in mobility and vehicle design. No steering wheel, no accelerator, no brake. Only a single touch-screen monitor." () " NRG Energy opens first power plant in 10 years to meet energy demand" via Srivastava - NRG Energy opened its first power plant in over a decade late last month, partly funded by the state's energy fund. The power plant, located off the Sam Houston Highway in Willowbrook, is a peaker plant -- a power plant that operates one to two hours each day, acting as a shock absorber to the power grid -- said Matt Pistner , the president of NRG Wholesale. As energy demand in Texas continues to surge, largely driven by new AI data centers, developers have looked toward Houston, the energy capital of the world, as a location for new sites. The TH Wharton generating station is one of three NRG power plants funded by the Texas Energy Fund, a state initiative established in 2023 that is managed by the Texas Public Utility Commission. Two others are expected online by 2028, both also in the Houston area. The TH Wharton plant is also one of 108 new gas power plants pitched between the beginning of 2024 and April 2025, according to a report by the Environmental Integrity Project. Approximately half of the projects listed were clustered in the Houston area, making Houston a hub for new power plant developments. () " Neugebauer wins expedited discovery; FRMI shareholders urged to vote (FRMI)" via - Toby R. Neugebauer , shareholder and co-founder of Fermi Inc., along with affiliated participants, filed definitive Schedule 14A proxy materials seeking agent designations to call a Special Meeting and urge shareholders to support their slate. The filing states the Texas Business Court granted Mr. Neugebauer's emergency motion for expedited discovery related to the Board's adoption of a 70% supermajority bylaw to expand the board. The participants say the court order requires Fermi to produce documents and testimony about the bylaw, federal-court actions, and the cancelled Special Meeting. The proxy materials state Mr. Neugebauer beneficially owns 146,516,035 shares of common stock, composed of 44,656,376 shares held by Vicksburg Investments Management LLC, 94,359,659 shares held by the Melissa A. Neugebauer 2020 Trust, and 7,500,000 shares underlying RSUs that vested. The court's order for expedited discovery, dated June 26, 2026, is described as requiring the company to produce documents and testimony about its adoption of a 70% supermajority bylaw and earlier litigation positions. The proxy states these materials are relevant to a Special Meeting effort led by the Fermi Founder Parties. The filing frames the development as material to shareholder rights and solicits agent designations to call a Special Meeting. Subsequent filings and produced discovery will determine whether the bylaw and related actions were procedurally justified; timing and scope of discovery are described but specific documents and deposition subjects are not listed in the excerpt. () " H-E-B to build $175M refrigerated facility on the East Side" via Lily O 'Neill - H-E-B wants to expand its manufacturing and distribution facilities on San Antonio's East Side. H-E-B plans to build a $175 million refrigerated facility at its East Side campus. The new property is part of the San Antonio-based grocer's largest-ever investment in its manufacturing and supply chain operations. H-E-B plans to construct a two-story, 675,000-square-foot facility with refrigeration space, as well as office and administration space, at 2045 South Foster Road, according to a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. Construction is expected to begin in August this year and be completed by March 2028. The grocer declined a request for comment on the new facility. The company also is working on building a $125 million bakery production facility at the campus, and said in a news release that it plans to add a transportation building and additional facilities. () " Vistra gets funding to expand Ward County power plant" via Mella McEwen - Plans to add two new natural gas units to a Ward County power plant have received approval for the eighth Texas Energy Fund loan from the Public Utility Commission of Texas under its In-ERCOT Generation Loan Program. Vistra Corp. plans to add 860 megawatts of new reliable power by building the two new natural gas units at its Permian Basin Power Plant, which would more than triple the site's current capacity. The additional 860 megawatts would be enough electricity to power about 215,000 Texas homes. The project is expected to begin generating power for the Electric Reliability Council of Texas power region in 2028. Vistra announced in September that it planned to move forward with the next phase of its capital plan to support grid reliability in Texas. In 2024, the company identified more than $1 billion worth of potential capital additions in generation capacity within the Texas power market operated by ERCOT by 2028 if market conditions were supportive. Citing customer demand and West Texas' growing power needs, particularly the state's expanding oil and natural gas industries, the company made a final investment decision to build the two new natural gas units. () " Casey's eyes Texas expansion by building on small-town legacy" via - Casey's is looking to Texas as a prime location to expand its small-town business model, which has thrived in Iowa and across the Midwest, CEODarren Rebelez says. "We love Texas," Rebelez said Wednesday, June 24, at Casey's investor day in New York City, where the company detailed its strategic plan for the next three years. Iowa small towns, where Casey's stores are a common fixture, launched the nearly 60-year-old convenience store chain that is now the nation's third largest. "When I think of growth prospects, this is the anecdote I like to give: In Iowa, our home state, we have 550 stores with a population of 3 million people," Rebelez said. "The population of Texas is 30 million people. So, are we going to put 5,500 stores in Texas? Probably not. But could you squint and see 1,000 stores, 2,000 stores? I don't see why not." Friends,
We’re taught that the best way to deal with bullies is to stand up to them and challenge their power. That’s true whether the bully is in the schoolyard or the Oval Office.
Which is why we’ve sued Donald Trump 73 times in the 17 months since he returned to the White House.
Our test is incredibly simple: Is the President following the law? Is he complying with the Constitution? If the answer is no — and far too often, it is — we take action. If he is harming California and those who call this state home, we will hold him accountable. Full stop.
I will never apologize for holding the most powerful man in the country accountable when he oversteps the bounds of his power.
He might not like it, but the truth is, his power isn’t limitless. He isn’t king.
When this administration breaks the law, tramples our rights, and attacks our democracy, we fight back and take them to court — again and again. And again and again, we win.
But I'm not naive about what's ahead. We've got a long way to go until Trump finally leaves office. That's a big part of why I'm running for re-election this November — California needs an Attorney General ready to keep fighting.
Trump continues to target this state. Our healthcare. Our schools. Our public safety. Our immigrant communities. None of us can sit back while the federal government attacks our rights, our neighbors, and our values.
We have to give this everything we've got.
A fight this big takes resources, and right now, we're up against a hard deadline. Our end-of-quarter filing deadline is at midnight, and my campaign is working toward an important fundraising benchmark. Coloradans deserved a choice in this primary race because in America, _we, the people_ — not establishment politics — choose our leaders.
**Tonight, you chose fresh, energetic, and bold leadership for Colorado.**
As your next governor, I’m ready to get corporate money out of our elections and ensure our political system stays focused on delivering for all Coloradans, not just the wealthy few.
I’m ready to take on the affordability crisis in health care, housing, and child care.
To protect our land, air, and water.
To invest in our economy and jobs, with infrastructure to support our growth.
To show up, listen, and work together — because tonight, we proved that that’s how we win.
I’m ready to keep _fighting like hell_ for our rights and freedoms. _And I will never bend the knee to lawless bullies like the Trump administration._
**If you’re with me, I’m ready to keep this energy going through November. Because we’re going to be up against a lot from the official Republican nominee.**

---
| | Dear Peter,
Working people across this country have been helping to build an all-out fight to elect Kshama Sawant to Congress, because workers everywhere understand that the outcome of this election has the potential to be an earth-shattering break with the savage status quo of politics in the United States. This campaign is a vehicle to build the mass movements that we need to win life-changing demands. Kshama is the only candidate fighting to end all military aid to Israel, to shut down ICE and the detention centers, and to shut down the AI data center juggernaut that is driving mass layoffs. She's the only one fighting for free health care for all funded by taxing the rich and a $25/hour minimum wage with automatic raises tied to inflation.
We know that the establishment will do everything in their power to stop Kshama from winning, because she is a proven fighter for the working class who won’t sell out. That’s why we need YOU (yes, you!) to join us in mobilizing tens of thousands of people to vote for Kshama Sawant.
---
| | [**Join us for one of our upcoming phonebanking shifts to get out the vote for Kshama**](https://us.list-manage.com/YAMWmYQVZPo?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
---
| | You can attend phone banking shifts that are held several times per week from now up until the primary election day on August 4th, 2026. With these calls we’ll reach voters in the district who may not have heard yet about Kshama’s pro-worker, antiwar campaign or about her unparalleled track record on the Seattle City Council. Phone banking is a crucial way to reach voters who we otherwise might not reach and to follow up with identified Kshama supporters from our on-the-ground canvassing work and ultimately ensure that they both vote and join the class-struggle movements we need to win our demands.
You don’t need any prior experience to join. Experienced campaign organizers will be leading each volunteer opportunity. We’ll provide training and support throughout the entire process to answer any questions that come up.
---
| | [**Join us for one of our upcoming phonebanking shifts to get out the vote for Kshama**](https://us.list-manage.com/OOh5lj_20G6?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)
---
| | I am one of many campaign volunteers both in Washington state and around the country actively fighting to elect Kshama Sawant to Congress because we know that this election represents the best chance we have to win breakthroughs for working people and to break with the political duopoly of the Democratic and Republican parties. Despite any differences they have, both parties represent the billionaire class. They have both voted to create and fund ICE, and they have both backed the genocide in Gaza. Working people need our own party, and we need independent candidates of our own who are willing to go to war against both the Democrats and Republicans to win things working people need.
Kshama's campaign is the most important campaign in this year’s midterm elections, because she is the ONLY one with a track record of defeating the billionaires to win historic victories for working people. She has led movements that resulted in millions of workers getting a raise and higher taxes on the rich to fund working people's basic needs. She is a revolutionary working class fighter who has both the temerity and skill to lead the working class in a battle to win exceptional victories for the working class, even in the face of opposition from billionaires and establishment politics.
This campaign is our chance to send a clear message to the world that socialist, independent, working-class politics can stand up to the power of the capitalist class and win. We do not have to accept poverty, genocide, climate collapse, unaffordable rent, and a political system bought by the rich.
I hope you’ll join us for an upcoming phonebanking shift. This week we have volunteer shifts scheduled on [Tuesday June 30th](https://us.list-manage.com/kEOjGBEISQO?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15), [Wednesday July 1st](https://us.list-manage.com/nVF1hJvnGbs?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15), and [Sunday July 5th](https://us.list-manage.com/1A6UPMOOTku?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15). If one of these days doesn't work for you then please email us that you want to get involved and we can help get you activated. We can only win if thousands of ordinary people get involved and help us fight for every vote in this historic campaign. Because when we fight, we can win!
Solidarity,Alberto OliartVolunteer with Kshama for Congress

body:
more details about the viral video
| Team,

Many of you have now seen the viral video of Senator Scott Wiener being harassed and bullied with antisemitic attacks at San Francisco Pride this weekend.

What you did not see in that video was Scott lashing out or escalating. Even during a scary attack, he stayed calm under pressure and kept his focus where it has always been: on doing the work.

At a time when politics is full of division, anger, and people trying to tear each other down, Scott is head down on progress.

As a California State Senator, Scott has become one of the most effective LGBTQ rights leaders in the nation. He’s fought to protect trans people, expand civil rights, strengthen access to gender-affirming care, and take on far-right bullies who have publicly threatened and targeted him for years, including Elon Musk, Megyn Kelly, and Fox News.

**Now Scott is running to become the first openly LGBTQ person ever elected to represent San Francisco in Congress. That would be groundbreaking.**

[And it would send a proven national leader on equality to Washington at a time when LGBTQ rights are under attack and progress has stalled. That’s why we’re asking you to split a donation between Voter Protection Project and Scott Wiener’s campaign today.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/115779?t=6&akid=25917%2E878179%2EpQZA_e) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Scott Weiner and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $7 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/115780?t=7&akid=25917%2E878179%2EpQZA_e)

name: INGOP
subject: Governor directs state to reimburse local governments for gas tax holiday revenue
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
ICYMI: Indiana Capital Chronicle No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-e-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-x/) **IN CASE YOU MISSED IT** [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-r/) **Governor directs state to reimburse local governments for gas tax holiday revenue** [Click Here to Read the Full Story](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-y/) Local communities will be spared revenue losses from Indiana's suspension of gas taxes. (Photo courtesy of Indiana Safe Zones) Niki Kelly
June 30, 2026
[https://indianacapitalchronicle.com/2026/06/30/governor-directs-state-to-reimburse-local-governments-for-gas-tax-holiday-revenue/](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-j/)Gov. Mike Braun's administration will make local governments whole for any gas tax revenues lost due to his suspension of Indiana's fuel taxes since May, according to a Tuesday news release.State Budget Director Chad Ranney will bring the formal request to transfer funds from the State Highway Fund for April and May to the Board of Finance on July 21. Once the transfer is approved, local governments are expected to receive distributions from the Comptroller's Office within five to seven business days, the news release said."This is only possible because Hoosiers demand commonsense fiscal management, and we've delivered," Braun said. "We are running government more efficiently and as a result, we have the resources to offer tax relief while supporting local partners."Hoosier drivers have been saving up to 62.5 cents per gallon in both sales and gas tax eliminations.Braun [first declared an energy emergency](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-t/) on April 8, temporarily lifting the state's sales tax on gasoline. He sought to offset the rapidly escalating cost of fuel after the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran, which closed the Strait of Hormuz -- a key transit hub for oil imports.The governor extended the suspension for another 30 days through a second executive order May 6, this time lifting the state's 36-cents-per-gallon excise tax too. In June, Braun [extended both](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-i/) another 30 days through July 7.The 30-day tax suspensions, combined, are expected to cost the state $104 million and local units $52 million. Braun's initial 30-day suspension of the 7% sales tax on gasoline came at a separate $50 million revenue hit.Braun indicated the state's energy emergency statute grants him the authority to extend both gas tax suspensions through early August, if needed, before legislative action is needed.The Board of Finance -- consisting of the state budget director, comptroller and treasurer -- can make budgetary transfers during the fiscal year."The Comptroller's Office is committed to serving as a trusted partner to Indiana's local governments by ensuring these distributions are processed accurately and without delay," Comptroller Elise Nieshalla said. "We understand the importance of timely revenue distributions, and we remain focused on delivering taxpayer dollars with the transparency, accountability and fiscal stewardship Hoosiers expect."Similar requests will be made at the August and September Board of Finance meetings, as needed. Local governments are expected to be made whole no later than November 1. [Click Here to Read the Full Story](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-d/) **INGOP Team: **Under Governor Mike Braun's leadership, state revenues have far outpaced projections, allowing Hoosiers to continue paying the lowest gas prices in the country while fully reimbursing our communities. That is the kind of conservative leadership that makes Indiana a model for the entire country. [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-h/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-k/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-u/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-o/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-b/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-n/) [Click Here to Support Your Indiana Republican Party](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fpiyky-hhlljjcji-p/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. Citizen Activist Promotes Massachusetts Alone, as Partisan Politics Hurts Massachusetts Once Again.
Washington, D.C. -- While Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey chose not to participate in the nation's 250th anniversary celebrations on the National Mall, one dedicated Massachusetts Republican stepped up to proudly showcase our Commonwealth to thousands of visitors from across the country.
Donna, a committed member of the Greenfield Republican Town Committee, has been a standout representative for Massachusetts at the historic event. Single-handedly flying the flag for the Bay State, Donna has manned the booth and even given out samples of Massachusetts maple syrup at her own expense.
Her efforts have earned widespread media coverage, including interviews with USA Today, The Boston Globe, The New York Times, The Washington Post, NPR, Real Clear Politics, Scripps News, CBS News, WCVB Boston, and FOX News.
The FOX segment in particular created a major rush to her booth, and her story has been picked up by wire services and numerous additional outlets.
Donna has already distributed all of the Chamber of Commerce flyers she brought with her: a testament to the strong interest in Massachusetts tourism and culture she has generated on the ground.
"The Massachusetts Republican Party is incredibly proud of Donna's initiative and hard work," said Amy Carnevale, Chairwoman of the Massachusetts Republican Party. "In the absence of official state participation, Donna has exemplified the grassroots spirit that makes our Commonwealth great. She is putting Massachusetts front and center at this once-in-a-generation national celebration."
The MassGOP is exploring ways to support Donna on short notice by arranging a rapid delivery of additional Massachusetts tourist brochures, promotional materials, and items to help sustain her momentum.
Donna's dedication reminds us that real leadership often comes from the grassroots. The Massachusetts Republican Party thanks her for carrying the torch for the Bay State when others would not.
For more information or to support these efforts, contact the Massachusetts Republican Party.

## Supreme Court Upholds Birthright Citizenship
The Supreme Court [struck down](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFvgzAQBeBfYzbQ-TCGDB66sKVrR0TsI77KYGQ7Qemvr-jS7t1OOuk9fe_jOl1nDrzd3-eVTFnitNGRA5VCabpxKj7x3RfLhb9oy553H4ObEFDX0NcgJzdzeE2qcmYhQmorMrIf8ALQ9VB5Y7FVqBZsYZHorNMtqb4jrbQcLHRQsTnToAcpAS44NN2s1dzJRYO96EFLoYAcl5iaz8hb8bSEV3xSamxcq2B8KXsW7ZvAUeB4HEdjb_lUnH-B43kKHPNjT7RSbeMjlfqXVv-x1SU91r12ZDlz3ASOVTJuPzgEzroXCu7rzOGnuPxrrafB7wAAAP__RWOAIg) President Trump's order to end birthright citizenship, ruling that nearly all children born on U.S. soil are citizens under the 14th Amendment. Chief Justice John Roberts wrote the [6-3 majority](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFvhDAMRn9N2ECOCQkMGbqwXdeOKIC5uAoEhdyh66-v6NLuXbxYep_e-7gNN8eBt_u7W8nmJQ4bnUegnCkNI6fsE999njjzF22H593HMA8IqEswJchhdhxegypmuxAh1QVZaVrsABoDhbeqrUdasKMGpZMaR2NA1YrkUoNskAq2Fw0MSAnQYVs1TivXyEXD1OlWS6GAZs4xVZ-Rt-xpCa_4pFRNcS2C9Tnvh6jfBPYC-_M8q2kbp-spsL_QAnu4Tg0C--OxJ1qpnOIj5fLXsPyjWKbHlaTyeQ1FsvN-cgh8aCMU3FfH4Wc5_yvX0-J3AAAA__8rhn33), finding little support in the Constitution for the administration's position. The order, signed on Trump's first day of his second term in 2025, never took effect. Justices Clarence Thomas, Neil Gorsuch, and Samuel Alito [filed dissents](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZB61DdgQOLiEbC69EBnc4D4ZjEwzo7mvP81usJtvXKoqvffnPt49JdrX335Dx0sed3yeCZmxjBMVjoXWyDMx_cP9jHTEnMKoQRsJVoIag6f0GpsquAVRY12hU7bTPUBroYrO9CYoZa3xajJ2qvsAdlZW4RQsKrQVufcaWFAKoNfdrfWm8a1aDMy96YwSDWAgzuX2N9POEZf0yg8stzlvVXKR-ThF_UvoQeiBI0ZK6Z0JPRRcr-SZ8i70MOersJw8c8JT6KHt67ZtOvmFKb9xyvM6Cm4oP2tcru2QquEo_YZ72HBnoYequHA8KSU6jRUNrJunj_OKf2Tz4fT_AAAA__-yJorY), with Alito warning the Court had made a serious mistake. Trump called [the ruling "too bad](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u2zAQBODTUB2N5Y8oqWARIFD3gnQpBZpcmRvQokCun-GcPnCapE89wGC--fGxfQQqdNy-hTt63ut24LMXZMa2XalxbnTLHInpFx4905lrSZsG7SRMEtSWApXXZofkd0SNZkCvplkvAOMEQ_bOOIN6nnaYx7AEO1u8uhDTuI8RdJoH8u82mEApgEXPlzE4G0a1O4iLm50SFjAR13b5WengjHt51U9sl1jvQ_GZ-ezCfBF6FXoN1_gWvDOh1--1EFPsQq_cHvdTXkOSPVZ-dPk4M5Yk_yLlP0p5PnrGLgveqJfAVA-h1861vYRZKQnzVRlr7AJqGppP55NKoe4mYeF2D1T-jOP_evTT698BAAD__08GjCE)" and urged Congress to restrict birthright citizenship through legislation.
## SCOTUS Upholds Transgender Sports Bans
The Supreme Court [upheld state bans](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO3CAQhJ8Gd5wWzsa-giKNuz9tSgubxWyEwYL9z7o8feS8QrqRRprR9_36Wr4cJcr7T3eg5VCWjFdLyIx1WalyrLRH3ojpD-YW6Ywl-UWDNhJGCWrxjtJn6TtvA6LGZ4dWjZN-AQwjdNGCD5N6QT-sQQWDgGrcnq6f-jCYMJmxI3uvwQhKAbz09Bic6d2ggoHtZSajRA_oiUt9_C6UOWJIn_LG-tjK0SUbmc8mnj-EnoWer-t6bGu7Ke5e6PmOQs_t-6x4oNzKd2XJ1eW2Y_ZYpeOYkLHJ1WV5YWP5prpTJifJu1iEnrtq_XlRStTMKHrYD0fp3z__l7S31X8DAAD__zJzgtg) on transgender athletes in girls' and women's sports, siding with West Virginia and Idaho in two closely watched cases. Justice Brett Kavanaugh, writing for the majority, said that states [may set eligibility requirements](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFvwyAUhH-NvWEBxsYZGLp4S9eOFoGH_SoMFrzESn99lYxdO55OOt33fV2Xq8WIaf20OxgKeUlw1ghEUJYbFtoKrhs5JPyBVDc8thz9IrkcGdeMi8VbjM9Ftd4EAAl9C0boSV44HzRvN-N7K3sdnBVByQBBcwUhSKl43_sh6BbNa41rLgTnFzl1gx2VHUQYubuM0ygaxcEj5dJ9Z0y0QYjP_IDSuby30WxER236j0bOjZzP8-zSzb0oXn0j5yNHJHS1kXO9HwV2YC7fC_3N7P5mq6ySJWBUbKorJA-F1SMXquxmU2XFJStH0U-qLcYfJ8aIddSN4utuMb5P0b9MPoz8DQAA___nNIr0) based on biological sex without violating Title IX or the Constitution's Equal Protection Clause. All nine justices agreed Title IX did not bar the bans, but they split 6-3 on the constitutional question, with the three liberal justices dissenting in part. The ruling reaches well beyond two states. Similar bans now stand on firmer ground [across much of the country](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOozAQRk9jOkdmAIMLF9vQZdstkcEDnpWxkT1JlD39KrnCX3_63pPen_tydxQpHb_diZb3vCR81YjMWJaVCodCR-CNmP5hqoGukKNfQIGWapSqXbyj-F76xtsdEbBr0LbjBEapYVRNsCtsvfGT9qvXA3inu9107TZ1DrU3q2vIfmhqVG2rlIHpNjjdu6HdtdqMnnQreoWeOJfb30yJA-7xnZ9Ybls-m2gD81VF90vALGDmgIFi_GwC5oLHIzqmnATMW34UlqtjjlgFzIPpBt2B5OJSPTB5LNJxiMgoV5eqrI-r4InyexQwN8X660UxUtWj6NVxOvqaGv5RuqeF_wEAAP__PsqETA).
## MLB Can Yell 'Play Ball,' But It Can't Own It
Major League Baseball [struck out](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAQRk9jMqOiwAYCB5uQ9aYbogIX7doxPzJWI-b0o545wsTfp6en9-8xPkiibM-_tLLLyz5ufJ2Rc-Y0TpJySPIMeZYsn7ydQY6wRz8ioNXQaqhGTxLvsSm8W5iR64Jd1XbYA5gWiuD80k2tsWYiM9VAdWOo6-YeOsB5BoOFuDcNWqgqgB670pBtyFSLhbm3na1UA-wl76n8v8uWAy_x3l-cynlfi-hCzsep6j8KB4XDdV0ln8f2HhUOa5wUDmfe061wGBUO4hUOTY9o66r_eWjPm7DXk3idE3leKX3oIyQ6WR-Rbj1RjEVy_rgkRjltqxp4riTx2yH_KtzL4VcAAAD__xbygKc) trying to trademark two of the most familiar words in sports when the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office denied the league's bid to register "Play Ball" as a trademark.

Baseball executives wanted to trademark the phrase to use on clothing, but the government ruled the phrase is too common in everyday use to belong to anyone. MLB, which first applied in 2022, can still appeal. But the rejection echoes Taco Bell's [successful fight](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQAL_GdEb2HthQuHgN3b02JTKwwF4WjMzm0OXro8svpB_NSPNx7--RmPblf9wwyJz6Ha-TUQRzP1CWNdOyykhC37ifKx1r4qkHA04br43tp0j86qtiCjMi4K3AYH0DrTG1N8UaIN7GqYHZe4feOhxag26swNmqbjw0BYW3zXhjrTEtNGUdXRVrOzsztq5xVlUGJ5KUy0eiXVac-ZWemMsxbQWHVeQ41e2fgk5Bd11XuWAecOd4vQkF3cBpUdB9nYcknfGBo5x64-HUUQS3Q7QkLTlOuMX8qQ-OLz1EZgVdkcN0XMRMp_OqMssWiX_D8qdbzwA_AQAA__8L4H9z) to free up "Taco Tuesday" from a taco competitor. Commonplace phrases are hard for any one company to own. Applauding the decision were a variety of small companies. A bubble-gum maker, a playground-surfacing firm, and a Rochester children's museum [already use](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ_GdEbGvzFQuEhD96dNiQys8UaLjey9Q5enj-7yCGmmGX2j0ffre_n2SJiOn_4ExyEvCe5KwAxlWbFwLHhE3pDxD6Qa8YqZ9kUrbaUapOqW3SO9FtPsLgBo-GrAdcOoJ6X6QTXR6WkD02m1WbOaIYy9De9-3cddmQHWBt17TQ2q65Sa9Nj23hrfd8GqbbKj7YRRsCPn0v7OmDhCoFd-Qmm3fDbkIvNVxdcPoWeh5_u-2_NR4XHmcJF_tbkcQs9XgVplAQJfQeiZI8jKJadDJs-Ykyf5D5M5yDdYPylXTyQPT14W4EdJVei5KW6_biTCagdh1HF6pM8b_i-FT6f_BgAA__-t6og1) the phrase.

## Trump Calls for Lower Gas Prices
President Donald Trump is pressing oil companies and gasoline retailers to cut prices faster, [urging retailers on Monday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ugzAUhZ_GbEbXhhgYPHRhS9eOyD8XclUTkH0Tkj59RV-hy1nO0Xek7-s6XR0lui-fbkXLr3mb7niUhMyYJ-f9xhwyMQX6wZIf55RdmjRoI6GToKboKL2ntorWQxxUhVZ1vR6g6QZT3WzfqkH72DY-oDGdjpfo4wyqVXgZdDQV2RMGHSiloFFtHQKEru8NRD9fTONECxiJt1zzDRlfrszpvT0x12Fbq2RvzHsRzYfQo9DjcRz1t-fXWQo9nmyhRzijAaFHzo91l8GlVOTiitwzBSxy2WTcjrukdcVIjjG9hR6rbON-UEpUTCdaWFZH6e-W_yfrafVvAAAA__9NSH2u) to target $2.50 a gallon as oil prices have dipped below $70 a barrel. "DROP YOUR PRICE FOR OUR GREAT AMERICAN PEOPLE!" [he wrote on Truth Social](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-O8yAQBPCnMV2iBZzFFBSf9MldrjrpSgvDJkbCwYLNv3v6k-8Vrp0Z_Yr5Ok9nn3K6XT_8So5flzLd6NkyMVOd_DwX5lATp5C-qdX7PmWfJwUKD2AOIKfoU35PvYhuhmilICfNoCxoY1EsziuLQUZEHW04WR21JGl0MKTJwIlEcjsGBqSUoGV_DAGCGQaEOF9OqH3XA8XEpR55IaaXb5f8Lg-qx1BWkd3CvLVO_-vU2KmR652XVkLyee_3sIdKPv8vN5_jZ72vW6fGrTRunRqlxEEjaNWjNsYiGlFd3J4p59TQdD1cV59-KcF_O-jh1E8AAAD__1_xeGw), accusing sellers of gouging and ordering a Justice Department probe into Big Oil. Last week, [Chevron's finance chief said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOrDAURFdjMqPrT_MJHLyErF86IbKNgSsZjOzb0D2rHzFbmKSSKp2SztdzfFqMuC__7RYMvec07uEqMRCFPFrnEpHPSOjxO5T8uqdk4yhBNhxaDmKcLMbPqKvJOJh6UQUj2k72oNq-qVYDzlplu9A3Sjlp9dwpPT-00EpJLWCu0NwwaEEIAUro2nvwbdc1MLn50SjLNIQJKeWa1kDhbcscP-kMufZpq6JZiY7C1D8mByaH67pqvzt_l0wON5vJAe6QDyYHv4Yzp50vtvAjow-FU35tB3e48ISxXmmLVTbTcWGMWJqWaVg2i_H3jv4m6TTyJwAA___-9Hpv) the major oil companies are "doing everything we can," but warned that there is a lag before falling crude prices reach the pump. Texas drivers are paying less than most Americans, with [the statewide average](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OgzAQhJ_GdI7WC7GhcHENXa69Ei22CZbMj-xNSO7pT-QVrppiRvNp5uc23CimuN6_aQmWX9M2rOEoKTCHPNA4bswuR44u_oaSH2eUKQ0IqCUYCWrwFNN7aCpvR_CdqoJVpsUOatPparbTlXBsnEHdadUgdpOGrjajbzsNZlJVtGcZGFBKQa2ai3PgTNtq8ON01TWJBoKPvOULz4HDi8qU3tsz5IvblirZmXkvov4S2Avs3VjoUTiupyuwP-cI7NPmKAnsOT-WXR60cpF3KpJY4hXkHHIo8jhFfhByz9GFIgvT6qts_X7ElGLRRjRwXyimD53_99nT4l8AAAD__252gdg) at $3.29 a gallon, down nine cents from a week earlier, versus $3.84 nationally, according to AAA.
## Texas Republicans Blast Supreme Court Ruling
Texas Republicans [sharply criticized](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuqzAQRL_GdKD1QgwULl5Dl9feEhnbxCs5GNmbkOTrr8gv3HpGc0bn5zpfDUXabv_N3Wt-rWne_FGiZ_Z5NsuSmG0mJksfX_LjrLKJMwKqGvoa5OwMxffcVU4v4EZZeS37AUdo-1FVQTsEbDt0ah1xcQusYyu9c9bBBa1FVZE-x6AHKSW0smusBdsPgwK3rBfVGtGBd8QpNxw8-5cpa3ynp8-NTfcq6sC8F9H-EzgJnI7jaGzIaTtTgdOe4nm_CJxMZrLRC5wWyhwy3QLXlpg-fiuB9rrYxI9Sfxk1You9HFSzh73K2u0HxUhF9aKD291Q_OL5b9KeGn8DAAD__xfLgxM) the U.S. Supreme Court's 6-3 decision Tuesday upholding birthright citizenship and rejecting President Trump's order to end it for children of illegal immigrants. Governor Greg Abbott called automatic citizenship "a powerful magnet for illegal immigration," and U.S. Rep. Chip Roy called the ruling "insane." Sen. John Cornyn pointed to his bill targeting "birth tourism" by countries like China and Russia as a possible next step. Texas has one of the nation's largest illegal immigrant populations. The [Migration Policy Institute](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI48hgAuXGxD97bdEhl7CCMZjMZDXl6-fpX9ha3v1dHR-fM1fwXKdDx-hx29vNYyH_hdM4ogz2FZikhkEor0xsrX5yohz9bYXptBG5hToPwzd03yi0kOGvQwjNaZdnB9s3mXQj9EXNvo7jCYcHcB7D31aw_juAI05D8wMxgAMC10txhNHMaxN2lZ730bVGcwkRS-yYaCr1DX_FOeyLdY9ib7TeSsqv2l7KTsFJYI7WdRdjpLFWWnep2MO-pYLhbNV0YtfO1n1fjCeAk9URdOyJqxClMUOh56IZaN6bGJjiT0xqNudCo7gevAjQaUnRr26fymnKn2g-rMYw-U_2nJ_8V8evs3AAD__1o_izs) estimates Trump's order would have affected millions of Texans. Texas Democrats welcomed the outcome, with the Asian American Democrats of Texas calling citizenship "not a political bargaining chip." Trump urged Congress to limit citizenship by [legislation](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE9jOtCzzWIoXKSh27QpkX8eixWDkf1YdnP6iFwhzTQz-kb6vu7T3YQYtsenWVHTa07ThmeJSIR5MtYmIpcDBRd-sOTjmpKJkwDR1aBq4JM3Ib6ntvLagh94hZqrXgwg1dBVi0apjOiFsb0fZudkf3OtNUoK5Dc5zH0V9AUDBZxzkLxtnAOn-r4Db-dbJw1rAX2glBtakPBlyhzf6Ym5cWmtol6I9sLkBxMjE-N5ns23pddVMjFebCZGuEICE2M59owr1i4dmepjX1L0peYtLbVZcfMrbsTEWGXt9zPEGEqnWAuP1YT4d0j_0_TU4jcAAP__jkd7ig).
## San Marcos Data Center Ban Faces Challenge
San Marcos [became the first Texas city](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGP4yAQBeBfgzsiGHsBFxTXuNtrr7SG8ThBwiaCud3kfv0p-Qtbv6dPT-_P5_qJueTz-hsPjvLY63rydy8swm3FlKoItSyZ8j_u7e-rKlhWMOC08drYdcNcnus0bDGZbbYDR-sDzGb0sxtucSYL6cMF9CkEInCB7O5pYkgW5pCGHF-Y8cZaa0Y7XYgM-RCc2dL-4UZUk-EtS20XubHwA_tenvWL24XqMZR4E7l3Nf5SsChYMJEdX4mC5V67KFg6nvrARrXrxFQP7nrPrYumLE_9FnXCU28oqIlP4da1cJd8XnWphEVTPaXVomCx8wQwW6dgGVrc7t-5lNydV5O5HpjLe5T87MqvCP8DAAD__61HiVg) to ban data centers, with its city council [voting 4-3 on June 16](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S2zAMhJ-G6ughKZ4kFyrSqLu0KTUQCNuY8MdDQr6Tnz6jdKnToPrwze7--lw_gSPn-09INMv3rayZvlokEaorbFsRwcrCyG9qdT9Rgbg64wZtRm3sGoDjsfouzJsJV9vRbMfJXU0_XofuMU_-9kGI1PsejCXve-ectb43DizC1PF8ysxorLWmt_6CaHCcpsGE7fYx9KC8ocBS6kUeJPQN7RaP8qJ6wZK6OD9Enk31P5RblFuwpLRnloPTE1BORrkF9iaclVsaZJ2gYml62wPo30ck5Zb76cuJsii3nHmUW8x57PjvE5Y9I0f9KkJNS9HPWh68segAAhopC9WmOWuIUb9L5nzXgZtURmnKLV2dw_OLY-Q2jMqbewKOf5vI_-3_mt2fAAAA___AK5yF) to bar the facilities from every zoning district. Council members cited the strain data centers put on local water and power as Texas races to become the nation's top data-center market. No projects are proposed within the city, but [at least two are planned](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUD2PnDAU_DWmM7INa6BwkYbu0qZEj-fHYp2xkf1y7ObXR6RLfeVoPjQzvz6WDwgxpOdPOMjxa8tLoqtGYqaywLpmZiyBA4Y_VMvvW8oQF6OMlWqQSi8eQnwvfePdqvykG3J6GM2kumGyze7MRAaRsN-Msto8aPP9psHo0Vr90H0T3B2mBqW1Vp3uW0SFwzha5dftYTsQvSIfOJeWd2J6Qd3iO39RaTEfTXQ781lF90OYWZj5uq728wXpJoWZ7zXCzDEjRGHmCkkeUDDX_4A0SknAQtIDg0RKTEWeEZKsJ5TPKhOF577mIjEnpJJuf1OcP68QY6h2EL16HhDiv1L8vSu_nPkbAAD__5nRiek) in surrounding Hays County. Republican state Sen. Paul Bettencourt said he will challenge the ban, arguing it violates state limits on local moratoriums. "_They should not use zoning to ban anything everywhere in the city, because that's not lawful_ ," he said. San Marcos' state senator, Judith Zaffirini, a Democrat, said the council acted "decisively and appropriately," and officials in other Texas cities say they are watching the case closely.

| 2026 is a make or break election year for democracy.
All of the talking heads are talking about the House and Senate elections, and yes, those will be consequential. But here's the truth most political pundits and election analysts are missing:
The fate of Democracy will also hinge on often overlooked and underappreciated state Supreme Courts races.
As MAGA witnessed the formation of a massive blue wave in 2025, they started working on desperate countermeasures, launching an all-out blitz of anti-democratic election rigging efforts at the state level--rewriting elections laws to make it harder for Democrats to vote and gerrymandering maps.
The constitutionality of their actions will ultimately be decided by state Supreme Courts. That means whoever controls these courts will control the fate of our Democracy:

The national party is going to be stretched thin. With dozens of competitive House and Senate races, state court elections will risk being ignored. We can't let that happen, not when the entire guardrail of democracy is on the line.

| | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE July 1, 2026
Oakland County Sheriff Mike Bouchard Endorses Doug Lloyd to be Michigan's Next Attorney General
LANSING, MI - Oakland County Sheriff Mike Bouchard announced today he is endorsing Eaton County Prosecutor Doug Lloyd to be Michigan's next Attorney General.
"The choice for Michigan's next Attorney General could not be more clear. Doug Lloyd has dedicated his career to holding criminals accountable and standing up for victims," Sheriff Bouchard said in his statement announcing the endorsement. "Eli Savit has repeatedly embraced an approach that has allowed dangerous offenders to receive reduced or zero consequences and return to our communities and hurt more people."
Sheriff Bouchard has witnessed the dangers of Eli Savit's radical agenda firsthand following the shooting of a woman during a carjacking in Oakland County in late May. Thanks to Savit's role as Washtenaw County prosecutor, the suspect in the Oakland County case was out on probation for hog-tying, duct taping and suffocating a woman with a plastic bag as he threatened sexual assault.
The police agency who arrested the criminal in the Washtenaw County case requested he be charged with assault with the intent to murder, which is punishable by up to life in prison, but Savit's office charged him with a lesser crime with a far more lenient sentence.
Sheriff Bouchard blasted Savit after the Oakland County shooting, [saying prosecutors have to "do their damn job."](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Xj2QKR9qvTNadq1ssNBVrkdEjzQ7vaRtN4FW91FWB-IBHFd9S4WCsD4_dSW0iNP9nOou_iXY0yM3eCMxBROa-v3cFC45zxDg4T-kL3-pr5ry3mzYr25w4uPg2cpRwVakxhFkBIYeaCg74j0nhXT9SdGJfc-yNcyCpI_XWk7MVpq5e-tjHSJRtJ1Htcc5fCrlqrE000Q3Tg_bAJlAj_GCAblgR3T0qq5d-YrNLTrXQMDKkRv5R2MDFMqEKHX0jqOy&c=hggSFc49HjLsVGP8NmGKQpugaZ_bdUfSjtfRGNz9xhiK4asOmi-DRw==&ch=98NLKcZnuV-xKZ-7gcgYGWG5caKNhSg_VQ6qZ8vSHcG_8WNfBpIyxA==)
"This election is about one simple question: Do we want an Attorney General who puts public safety and victims first, or one whose record reflects a philosophy of little or no consequences for serious offenders?" Sheriff Bouchard continued in his endorsement of Doug Lloyd. "For me, that choice is clear."
Sheriff Bouchard joins the Fraternal Order of Police State Lodge of Michigan, Police Officers Association of Michigan, and the Michigan Association of Police Officers in supporting Doug Lloyd to be Michigan's next Attorney General.
"I am honored to have Sheriff Bouchard's trust and endorsement in this race for Attorney General," Eaton County Prosecutor Doug Lloyd said. "What he is going through in Oakland County because of my opponent's policies is a travesty and we can't allow it to spread across our state. Law enforcement knows my record and knows I will never waver on holding criminals accountable. As Attorney General, we will support our police by prosecuting criminals and bringing justice for victims."
###
For more information about Doug Lloyd's campaign for Attorney General, visit [www.votedouglloyd.com](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Xj2QKR9qvTNadq1ssNBVrkdEjzQ7vaRtN4FW91FWB-IBHFd9S4WCsAjzLiTmQgAmdqdQqC_RtoEOl25UGTPzCYSFoRR5q80_DounQkZcmCwWAW-XaSmBFkQJrFjm7Shts_iym2-ppPpHkSYbaE3Em-92NuKUiuTUcmmkjtGjl0Y=&c=hggSFc49HjLsVGP8NmGKQpugaZ_bdUfSjtfRGNz9xhiK4asOmi-DRw==&ch=98NLKcZnuV-xKZ-7gcgYGWG5caKNhSg_VQ6qZ8vSHcG_8WNfBpIyxA==).

Sheriff Bouchard blasted Savit after the Oakland County shooting, == "This election is about one simple question: Do we want an Attorney General who puts public safety and victims first, or one whose record reflects a philosophy of little or no consequences for serious offenders?" Sheriff Bouchard continued in his endorsement of Doug Lloyd. "For me, that choice is clear." Sheriff Bouchard joins the Fraternal Order of Police State Lodge of Michigan, Police Officers Association of Michigan, and the Michigan Association of Police Officers in supporting Doug Lloyd to be Michigan's next Attorney General. "I am honored to have Sheriff Bouchard's trust and endorsement in this race for Attorney General," Eaton County Prosecutor Doug Lloyd said. "What he is going through in Oakland County because of my opponent's policies is a travesty and we can't allow it to spread across our state. Law enforcement knows my record and knows I will never waver on holding criminals accountable. As Attorney General, we will support our police by prosecuting criminals and bringing justice for victims." > _**One of the most encouraging things I have seen during this campaign season is the number of accomplished community leaders stepping forward to serve. They are not career politicians. They are people who have built successful careers, raised families, volunteered in their communities, and decided Connecticut deserves better.**_
**[Ken Astarita](https://substack.com/redirect/14b31268-6490-409d-a1cc-39a15b28f4ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** is one of those leaders.
As the Republican candidate for Connecticut's 134th House District, representing **Fairfield and Trumbull** , Ken brings decades of financial experience, service on Fairfield's Representative Town Meeting, and a practical understanding of how government should work. He understands that taxpayers deserve accountability, transparency, and leaders who put their communities first.
**A Practical Leader for Fairfield and Trumbull**
Ken's campaign is centered on the issues that matter most: affordability, economic growth, strong schools, public safety, responsible government, and restoring local control. He believes government should empower communities--not dictate to them.
His experience in financial services and local government gives him a unique perspective on how policy decisions affect families, businesses, and taxpayers. He understands that every government dollar comes from the people, and every decision should reflect that responsibility.
**Ground Zero for Connecticut 's Housing Debate**
That message is especially important because Fairfield has become ground zero for Connecticut's housing debate.
> As one of the few municipalities to earn an 8-30g affordable housing moratorium, Fairfield has already shouldered a significant share of the responsibility under state housing law. Now, with Public Act 25-2 (formerly House Bill 8002) taking effect, communities like Fairfield and Trumbull face even greater pressure from Hartford mandates that often fail to account for local infrastructure, traffic, parking, schools, sewer capacity, emergency services, and neighborhood character.
Ken understands that affordable housing and responsible planning are not mutually exclusive. We need housing solutions that are developed with local communities, not imposed on them. The people who live in Fairfield and Trumbull know their communities best, and their voices deserve to be heard.
**Making Connecticut Affordable Again**
Ken also understands that the only lasting solution to Connecticut's affordability crisis is creating an environment where businesses want to invest, jobs can grow, and families can build their futures here.
Economic opportunity--not bigger government--is what keeps young families in Connecticut, allows seniors to remain in the communities they love, and gives the next generation a reason to stay and build their futures here.
**A Movement Built from the Ground Up**
During his campaign kickoff, Ken reminded supporters that success will require everyone working together.
_**" This is going to take all of us."**_
He's absolutely right.
> _**Federal solutions often begin with local ideas, and many local priorities require state and federal partners working together. Politics is local, but its consequences reach Hartford and Washington. Building a stronger Connecticut starts by electing leaders who understand their communities and are willing to fight for practical solutions instead of accepting the status quo.**_
Ken Astarita is part of that growing movement.
**My Endorsement**
> _I am proud to support Kenneth Astarita because I believe he will bring common sense, financial discipline, and a commitment to local control to the Connecticut General Assembly._
> _If you live in Connecticut 's 134th House District, I encourage you to meet Ken, hear his vision, volunteer, and support his campaign._
Learn more at **[www.voteastarita.com](https://substack.com/redirect/4198ca0c-ed48-4e8d-933c-b59b5600f66b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
_**Together, we can build a more affordable, more accountable, and more prosperous Connecticut --one community at a time.**_

They are people who have built successful careers, raised families, volunteered in their communities, and decided Connecticut deserves better. is one of those leaders. As the Republican candidate for Connecticut's 134th House District, representing Fairfield and Trumbull , Ken brings decades of financial experience, service on Fairfield's Representative Town Meeting, and a practical understanding of how government should work. He understands that taxpayers deserve accountability, transparency, and leaders who put their communities first. A Practical Leader for Fairfield and Trumbull Ken's campaign is centered on the issues that matter most: affordability, economic growth, strong schools, public safety, responsible government, and restoring local control. He believes government should empower communities--not dictate to them. His experience in financial services and local government gives him a unique perspective on how policy decisions affect families, businesses, and taxpayers. He understands that every government dollar comes from the people, and every decision should reflect that responsibility. As one of the few municipalities to earn an 8-30g affordable housing moratorium, Fairfield has already shouldered a significant share of the responsibility under state housing law. Ken understands that affordable housing and responsible planning are not mutually exclusive. We need housing solutions that are developed with local communities, not imposed on them. The people who live in Fairfield and Trumbull know their communities best, and their voices deserve to be heard. Peter,
Yesterday, the Supreme Court officially ended its 2026 term, leaving a bloody trail in their wake with a slate of disastrous and history-altering decisions that will be felt for decades to come if nothing is done about it.
In just a single term, the MAGA justices on the court:

* Gave Trump the power to fire independent-agency officials without cause, overturning a 91-year-old precedent and tearing down a wall that kept the presidency from seizing control of agencies Congress built to be independent. The branches were meant to be coequal. This Court is making the president a king.

* Gutted the Voting Rights Act, clearing the way for Republican legislatures across the South to redraw maps and erase majority-Black districts.

* Struck down decades-old campaign spending limits, unleashing unlimited party-coordinated money into our elections and making it even easier for oligarchs to buy politicians.

* Banned transgender girls from school sports, a decision that is only enforceable by conducting genital checks on children and teenagers.

* Ended Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians, and stripped the courts of the power to review most challenges, clearing the way to tear families apart with no judicial check.

* Slammed the door on asylum seekers, ruling that people fleeing persecution who present themselves at our border have not legally "arrived" and can be turned away before they ever set foot on U.S. soil.

This term, MAGA's justices worked their way straight down the far-right's wish list:

For nearly 30 years, right-wing extremists ran a multi-billion dollar campaign to capture the Court. This term, MAGA's justices fully exposed themselves for who they really are--partisan activists using the court to impose MAGA initiatives on our nation that they know would never have a chance to pass in Congress.

Defend Our Courts is building the political pressure to make court reform a litmus test for Democrats, winning key House and Senate elections, and laying the groundwork for Supreme Court reform by 2028.

name: Steve Kerrigan
subject: Showing up after Pride Month

body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Peter,
Pride Month has always meant a great deal to me, not just as Chair of our Democratic party, but as a proud, openly gay man who understands firsthand what this month represents.
At its core, Pride is about the simple but radical idea that every person deserves to live openly and with dignity. It's rooted in resistance, in the bravery of those at Stonewall in 1969 who stood up against injustice when the world told them to stay silent. Their courage is the reason we gather each June, and it's a reminder that the rights we celebrate were never given to us. They were fought for.
Here in Massachusetts, we have a lot to be proud of. We led the nation on marriage equality. We continue to work hard to protect transgender residents and LGBTQ+ youth. And we have built a Democratic Party that doesn't just talk about inclusion; we live it. We cannot take any of that for granted.
At the same time, I want to be candid with you. The political attacks on LGBTQ+ Americans, and particularly on transgender individuals, are serious and they are intensifying. These aren't distant policy debates. They are affecting real families in real communities and as Massachusetts Democrats, we have both a responsibility and an opportunity to push back, and I know this party is up to that challenge.
Even though Pride Month is over, continue to show up, because that's what this community has always done.
Happy Pride, and thank you for standing with us.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Steve%20K%27s%20Signature.png]
Steve Kerrigan
Chair, Massachusetts Democratic Party

Dear Peter,
For the first time ever, the Republican Party will hold a Midterm Convention -- a historic, one-of-a-kind event. President Donald J. Trump, Vice President J.D. Vance, the Republican National Committee and Republicans from around the country will come together in Dallas for a national celebration heading into the 2026 midterms -- a moment to unite our Party, energize our grassroots, and showcase our candidates on the national stage, all while celebrating our nation, our achievements, and our bright future.
"We are going to celebrate the GREAT AMERICAN COMEBACK, and the incredible successes of the American People who transformed our Country through the America First Agenda. . . . It will be a RALLY like none other!" - President Donald J. Trump
If you're even considering going, apply to join the Massachuestts delegation right away. More information below.
To Victory in November!
---
|
---
Amy Carnevale Chair, Massachusetts Republican Party
---
The Great American Comeback Midterm Convention September 9-10, 2026 | American Airlines Center | Dallas, Texas

## What We're Celebrating
* The America First Agenda: No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security, stronger borders, the safest communities in our history, lower costs, and real affordability for American families.
* More jobs, American energy dominance, and the hardworking Americans, innovators, entrepreneurs, manufacturers, first responders, and job creators powering our nation's Golden Age.
* America's 250th Birthday -- together, we are building the foundation for the next 250 years of American Greatness.

## What This Event Is
* A special ceremonial national gathering -- not a nominating convention.
* A celebration of our Party's vision and candidates, built to mobilize voters ahead of November.

## Key Distinctions from Conventions
* No nominating delegates. There is no credentialing process, as this is not a delegate or alternate event associated with a nomination.
* Tickets, not credentials. Each state party will receive and distribute a set allocation of tickets. The MassGOP will accept applications for tickets and applicants are subject to vetting at both the state and national level.

## Logistics at a Glance
* Dates: Wednesday, September 9 - Thursday, September 10, 2026
* Venue: American Airlines Center, 2500 Victory Ave, Dallas, TX 75219
* Ticket allocations: The allocation process will move quickly. There is a $20 processing fee per application.
* Dues: If selected, you must pay your dues within 48 hours, which are expected to increase from the 2024 Convention Dues of $500.
* Hotels: The MassGOP will reserve an allocation of hotel rooms for ticket holders once the official hotels are released by the RNC.
* Transportation: Transportation to and from Dallas will be on your own. Transportation to and from the RNC hotels to the American Airlines Center will be provided to all official ticket holders.
* Overall Costs: Upwards of $4,000
* Questions: Contact the MassGOP at [info@massgop.com](mailto:info@massgop.com)
