_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2590%2E259176%2EyghPlt) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2590%2E259176%2EyghPlt)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13919?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.01_McBride-Reelection_B1_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=4&akid=2590%2E259176%2EyghPlt) It's official, Peter. **The paperwork has been filed, and I’m running for re-election to continue representing Delaware in the House of Representatives.** My first term in Congress has been eventful to say the least. Elon Musk’s DOGE ransacked the federal government, Republicans slashed funding for Medicaid, food assistance, and other critical programs working families rely on, and Donald Trump started a reckless, illegal war that has caused even more pain for Americans as gas prices rose in response. But every step of the way, I’ve been proud to stand up and fight for what’s right for Delaware. Now, this November, we have a chance to take back the majority and start passing an agenda that will put working families first for a change. When I was first elected last year, I said that **I believe small states can do big things** — and there is no limit to what we can accomplish when we work together to make people’s lives better. That holds true now more than ever. If we’re going to flip the House in this year’s midterms so that we can hold this administration accountable and pass a budget that centers the needs of regular Delawareans over Trump and his billionaire allies, **it has to start by keeping this seat blue.** Republicans would love nothing more than to flip Delaware red, and I’m going to do everything I can to make sure that doesn’t happen. That’s why I just finished visiting all 57 of Delaware’s municipalities in just 57 hours — to talk to our neighbors across the state and remind them why they trusted me to represent them in Congress: to deliver lower costs, expand access to healthcare, and protect our fundamental rights. I’m going to keep going every single day between now and November, and I’m going to need your help along the way. **Peter, our campaign is powered by everyday people.**[**Which is why today, I’m asking you to split a donation of $20.26 between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help us flip the House on Election Day.**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13919?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.01_McBride-Reelection_B1_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=5&akid=2590%2E259176%2EyghPlt) _If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Sarah McBride and Blue Amp Action will go through immediately:_ | | [RUSH $20.26 →](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13920?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.01_McBride-Reelection_B1_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=6&akid=2590%2E259176%2EyghPlt)

He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | A security camera caught an ordinary man filling up his tank. | Hi PPeter,

I’m Stefany Shaheen, and I’m proud to be running for Congress in New Hampshire’s 1st District.

This district is my home. It’s where I grew up, raised my family, and built my business. It’s where I learned what it means to care, serve, and fight for what matters.

My daughter, Elle, was just eight years old when she was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. Her life has revolved around needles and blood sugar checks, 24-7—with too many sleepless nights and constant worry that the wrong amount of insulin could kill her. That experience changed me—for more than 15 years, I’ve fought for medical research and innovation in health care to help people like my daughter and millions more who are battling chronic, life-threatening diseases.

Now, Trump and MAGA Republicans are crushing medical research while Republicans in Congress slash Medicaid, and health care for kids, seniors, and veterans—all to give big tax breaks to billionaires and corporations—it’s time to turn outrage into action. I’ve got to fight.

I’m running for Congress to fight for New Hampshire families and the values that make us strong. There’s no one who fights harder than a mom for her kids, and that’s how I’ll fight for your family, too. In New Hampshire, we stand up for each other.

BREAKING, Peter: Justice Democrat
Melat Kiros has officially won the primary for Colorado’s 1st
congressional district, beating 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260701-1.e7boUC&refcode=em20260701-37979&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=37979%2E1203867%2E6Rv2Sk ]Graphic with a photo of Melat Kiros that reads: Congratulations CO-01
Primary 2026 winner Justice Democrat Melat Kiros

This is yet another monumental win for our progressive movement, just one
week after we swept two races in New York. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260701-1.e7boUC&refcode=em20260701-37979&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37979%2E1203867%2E6Rv2Sk ]But we can’t let this
momentum end: will you rush $5 now to help us win our final
3 primaries of the cycle this summer?

Melat’s opponent served in Congress for 15 terms, taking campaign checks
from Big Pharma, the military-industrial complex, and the real estate
lobby, while delivering next to nothing for working-class families in
Denver.

Those same lobbies dropped over $2 million in the final weeks of this race
when polls showed Melat up by five points, and they realized they could
lose their puppet.

Most of that money came from AIPAC: the pro-Israel lobby group played a
pernicious role in this primary, using vaguely-named shell PACs like
Pro-Choice Majority Action to support DeGette and attack Melat, just like
they did in other 2026 primary races.

But their last-minute attempts to buy this seat failed after Melat built a
movement that inspired Denverites to remember they themselves have the
power to transform what kind of Democratic Party they want to be
represented by.

Melat sacrificed her career as an attorney to stand up for pro-Palestinian
protesters being fired by law firms and moved back to the district to work
part-time as a barista and pursue a PhD — before deciding to launch her
campaign to deliver leadership unbought by corporate influence to CO-01.

Justice Democrats was the first national organization to endorse Melat
back in December, and with our support, we made sure her message reached
voters across the district, while her campaign knocked on more than
100,000 doors and generated the turnout needed to win.

DeGette has been in office longer than Melat has been alive. For the first
time since 1997, Denver will finally have bold new representation in
Washington willing to fight for workers.

Melat and our candidates continue winning this cycle because Democratic
voters are finally getting leaders acting on their demands to bring the

Friend, **** I'm Tim Lanier, and I'm a common sense Democrat running for US Congress. I need you to remember the number 4. I'm running in the 4th District. I had 4 and a half days to put this campaign together. I'm listed 4th on the ballot. And I have 4 things I will fight for in Washington. I have spent years working in construction. As a carpenter and small business owner, I have seen firsthand how difficult it has become to build the homes and communities people need. Most people think we have an affordable housing problem. What I saw was a worker pipeline problem. The construction industry could hire 500,000 people right now and close to 2 million over the next decade. Major projects are delayed because there are not enough skilled workers to do the job. That affects every family looking for a home and every community trying to grow. **That is why I developed the B4, the Big Beautiful Building Bill.** The plan starts with oversight of federal construction projects to make sure budgets and estimates are in place before work begins. It invests in workforce development by training and certifying people to operate equipment like cranes and dozers. It creates a clear pathway for people who want to become General Contractors. It continues to develop sustainable housing designs and adapt those plans for communities across the country. I believe we can build our way out of the housing crisis if we build smarter. I have also watched people lose confidence that their voices are being heard. **That is why voting rights matter.** I have watched women strengthen the businesses, organizations, and campaigns they help lead. **That is why women's rights matter.** I have watched violence continue in Ukraine while Russia attempts to annex territory and test what the world will tolerate. **That is why standing up to aggression matters.** These are not issues I learned about from a distance. They are things I have watched, experienced, and thought deeply about. They are the reason I am running. Now I want to hear from you. If you could fix one broken system in this country, what would it be? Supreme Court Ends Its Term With a Bang 5-minute read · 4 stories Lead Story · The Supreme Court SCOTUS CLOSES TERM: BIRTHRIGHT ORDER STRUCK DOWN, GIRLS' SPORTS PROTECTED, PARTY SPENDING CAPS GONE What's HappeningOn the final opinion day of its term Tuesday, the Supreme Court handed down three of the year's biggest decisions at once — a split verdict that gave conservatives two clear wins and one hard loss.The Situation
* **Birthright citizenship — struck down.** By 6–3 in _Trump v. Barbara_ , the Court blocked the president's Day One executive order and reaffirmed that the 14th Amendment grants citizenship to nearly all children born on U.S. soil. Chief Justice Roberts, calling citizenship "the right to have rights," wrote the opinion — joined by the three liberal justices and, from the right, **only Justice Barrett**.
* **Girls' and women's sports — protected.** In a separate 6–3 ruling, the Court upheld West Virginia and Idaho laws requiring athletes to compete by their sex at birth.
* **Party spending caps — gone.** The Court also struck down a Watergate-era limit on how much a national party can spend in coordination with its own candidates, in a challenge brought by **Vice President JD Vance**. Justice Kagan dissented sharply.

The PerspectiveTwo out of three isn't a bad day. States can now keep men out of women's sports, and the parties are free to spend on their candidates without a 1970s-era muzzle. The birthright ruling stings — but note that Justice Kavanaugh flagged the door Congress left open, and that the president's position pulled a vote it was told it never had a decade ago. This fight moves to the Capitol, not the grave.[Read the full story at NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/yETiddLsbEfWTdnkbrEloyl%2F8QBkOLqsw7%2FpX%2BBh2Ty045iHsXPc9ggjR%2Frp%0ARbLk%2BZGxNwZZeAYyCua2Kr6rbctemxsyaO5b5OYVV%2FUOFobkKXLQLGdP7eH6%0AwZV0HHi%2FlXCM9YxGM30r7rujU%2FLWhRUQ%2F6ymZcYGD2d15VwCEO3SATZFQ%2Bd7%0ABbpxGei3tTUH8CQOY5%2FHIRZcIlbqXtSHFg%3D%3D%0A/165abe3b025167e3)The 2026 Map DEMOCRATS EAT THEIR OWN IN COLORADO — A DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST TOPPLES A 30-YEAR INCUMBENT What HappenedIn the only statewide primary Tuesday, Colorado Democrats swung hard left. In Denver's 1st District, **democratic socialist Melat Kiros, 29** , ousted 30-year Rep. Diana DeGette — a first-time candidate backed by Bernie Sanders and the DSA unseating one of the state's most senior members of Congress. The AP called it just after 10 p.m.The Situation
* Kiros campaigned on **abolishing ICE** and Medicare for All, and made opposition to Israel a centerpiece; she'll be heavily favored in the deep-blue seat in November
* In the governor's race, Attorney General **Phil Weiser upset sitting Sen. Michael Bennet** in the Democratic primary — a contest that turned largely on who would fight the Trump administration harder
* Sen. John Hickenlooper survived his own primary challenge from the left
* It follows last week's progressive wins in New York City — part of a national pattern of insurgents knocking off the Democratic establishment

The PerspectiveThe party that spends its days warning about "extremism" just handed a safe seat to a candidate who wants to abolish a federal law-enforcement agency — and pushed out a governor's-race frontrunner for not being anti-Trump enough. Whatever you think of DeGette, this is a Democratic Party being pulled to its left flank in real time. In a midterm year, that's a contrast Republicans will happily run against.[Read the full story at NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/GucORO9S3nAHk9NmruKyCqLF6c3wxDJIp4usEg3IlcxGxkZIcO%2Bhs7BzlYFK%0AbMMiBTojT3iyX1mdGhMwxvO8uBxujQK2jcBebXZYVao7N9FLvwv1JTkVSKdT%0A4DU3KQ1U7L2giBjamvWK7HMGHbDOZGGpzBoUNIv6ilWATFt7DNDhpDDN6dmC%0AOoySGQ%2Fm1fsBOD4eEeqcifQcglmxH6Lfdw%3D%3D%0A/1e7f053f0ddeca0c)Foreign Policy IRAN LASHES OUT AT HORMUZ AS THE U.S. AND OMAN BUILD A WAY AROUND IT What's HappeningWeeks after the ceasefire reopened the Strait of Hormuz, Iran is reportedly straining to keep its grip on the chokepoint. Analysts say Tehran allegedly targeted commercial shipping in the strait — an apparent bid to undercut a **new southern shipping corridor** the United States and Oman have been developing to route cargo around Iranian pressure.The Situation
* Hormuz normally carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, giving Tehran outsized leverage every time it rattles the waterway
* The U.S.–Oman corridor is designed to give Gulf exporters an alternative that Iran can't simply throttle
* The reported attacks suggest Iran sees that workaround as a genuine threat to its leverage

The PerspectiveBack in June this newsletter led with the strait reopening under American pressure. This is the sequel: when you build an off-ramp around a bully's roadblock, the bully gets nervous. Iran lashing out isn't a sign the strategy failed — it's a sign it's working. The details here are still "analysts say," so we'll watch the shipping data, not just the threats.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/AZHpnAdyblE%2Fs%2BxOASelnLvKHAqWs%2BW1ZWkQHX%2BaTXygHH6ag7A6YaH1IKmS%0AB7XXAIQ5bT0i3iX6dbuklWCdTx5cqE8fUxLAbJTIac1YItxY1H4ieyyqmxQy%0A4Kt5PHWbhm5ksZbmBRl%2FRJxA9lKpVbWua3KTZmhS%2BEsBHx0G2W4umI%2BRZKRZ%0Ar7p%2FTJaa33XZJGqNbhF5rvkjC93142ecFA%3D%3D%0A/b3eea079a951dc37)The Economy CALIFORNIA'S GAS TAX CLIMBS AGAIN ON JULY 1 — NOW THE HIGHEST IN THE NATION What's HappeningRight as holiday travel ramps up, California's gasoline excise tax rose again Wednesday — up 2.2 cents to **63.4 cents per gallon** , keeping it the highest state gas tax in the country. The increase is automatic, tied to inflation under **Senate Bill 1** , the 2017 law that raises the tax every July without a vote of the legislature.The Situation
* Average regular gas in California runs about **$5.58 a gallon** per AAA — the highest in the nation and roughly **$1.65 above the national average**
* Counting sales tax and other fees, the total government surcharge comes to roughly **$1.15 per gallon** at California pumps
* The state's GOP congressional delegation, led by Rep. David Valadao, urged Gov. Gavin Newsom to **suspend the hike**
* Newsom's office pushed back, noting the increase is automatic — enacted in 2017 and upheld by voters in 2018, before he took office
* Diesel taxes also rose, climbing to 48.2 cents per gallon

The PerspectiveHere's the split screen: an Iran ceasefire is finally nudging pump prices down nationally, and in California an automatic tax hike claws part of that relief right back — no vote required. Defenders are right that voters approved the mechanism years ago. But "you signed off in 2018" is cold comfort at $5.58 a gallon on the way to the Fourth of July. When relief shows up, Sacramento's autopilot quietly takes its cut.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/khDqgYtHCklXZ0uqSXyxe%2FlldQKn2b2JX9q410OHNncSyEgVDVBxKUX0oy%2Bw%0AR8Mz94AYSSDjJx5IbWxGdQ3RoVm1GE1i6aGRqNUHvuHa1IHqe0EClIops%2B9Y%0AUJxE6QaYfNA0QvmB4NJStniUHRZSIIvOHiyIlI7AGmZskN9kc6xBTh3%2F18zh%0AKBweURnC%2F%2BgH85tqzsLrbhoMrEDFewqjIQ%3D%3D%0A/c08a2d777e2149fa) ⚡ The Bottom Line The Supreme Court gave conservatives a split decision — girls' sports and party speech protected, the birthright fight kicked to Congress. Colorado Democrats answered by lurching left and torching a 30-year incumbent. Iran is rattling Hormuz precisely because America built a way around it. And in California, pump prices ticked up again on July 1 — an automatic tax hike no one had to vote for. **Two wins at the Court, a Democratic Party at war with itself, and leverage holding abroad even as Sacramento reaches deeper into drivers' pockets. | | **June 7, 2026**

The protein boom is alive and well. Unless you live under a rock, you’ve likely seen protein being marketed on almost every food item you buy. [Doritos](https://us.list-manage.com/92oNFpV32Tx?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), your [coffee](https://us.list-manage.com/ACKLjtmToTF?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), and even your [ice cream](https://us.list-manage.com/KvfjeVFbs38?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) now trumpet their protein content. And it’s not just a marketing story; consumers are demanding more protein. [A majority of Americans](https://us.list-manage.com/7VmMds2f8U4?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) say they’re actively trying to eat more of it. Meat snacks alone have become a [$5.5 billion juggernaut](https://us.list-manage.com/19QcdXbymil?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), and #protein[ has millions of posts on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube](https://us.list-manage.com/4YBsoYxxxYM?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586). These days, the word “protein” on a package is almost as important as the price.
Food fads are not new, and while I believe the protein story isn’t a fleeting phenomenon, it’s not unreasonable to question the sustainability of the boom. After all, before protein, American consumers were infatuated with hydration. Remember when Liquid I.V. suddenly appeared everywhere? When everyone started carrying water bottles and Stanley cups became a status symbol?
It seems to me there’s a pattern here. First, a real health concept goes mainstream, social media amplifies interest in the topic, the food industry builds an empire with brands and products to help consumers achieve their goals, our culture changes to incorporate the new desires, and suddenly it’s in every aisle of your grocery store...

| | **June 14, 2026**

History may not repeat itself, but it often does rhyme. As resources become valuable, major powers scramble to secure access to them. But it’s not just the resources that matter, it’s the ability to get (to) them; inevitably, chokepoints emerge, and great powers start jockeying for position. In many cases, success in securing materials or trade routes is enough to reorient global power dynamics.
Rome conquered the Mediterranean in the 2nd century BC because it meant control of trade. For a thousand years (or so), the Silk Road drove empires from the Han Dynasty to the Mongols to battle for control of Central Asian corridors. The spice trade led the Portuguese and the Dutch into conflict over nutmeg in the 1500s and 1600s. The 1908 discovery of oil in Persia redrew the map of the Middle East, and we’re still fighting over those lines today. And Britain and Russia spent the entire 19th century playing what [Kipling called the “Great Game” across Central Asia, with India as the grand prize](https://us.list-manage.com/cR886dZeUWU?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586). Battles over resources and trading routes is nothing new.

Today, another Great Game is underway in the north. As I have written before, I believe the next couple of decades will see a Great Power contest for the Arctic, and it is already heating up....

| | **June 21, 2026**

Last weekend, my family headed north to watch my 15-year-old son Kai deliver a speech to the Rotary Club in Orford, Quebec. As someone who has been a professional speaker for more than 15 years, I was genuinely impressed by both his message and delivery. I could not have been more proud.
I hope you’ll indulge me on this Father’s Day and take 6 minutes to watch (or at least listen to) his speech. Yes, I’m a proud father who wants to brag about his son. But I’m also a concerned citizen and want his powerful message of hope and optimism to be shared and spread as widely as possible. He offers a path towards a more compassionate and peaceful politics.
And if you like his speech, please consider [subscribing to his podcast, The Kai Guy Show, on Apple Podcasts](https://us.list-manage.com/3GogiaKjR6M?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) where he regularly shares his thoughts. | | **May 24, 2026**

[4,316,233 babies were born in the United States](https://us.list-manage.com/eP48zqjZm8l?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) during 2007, the most in American history. The fertility rate, a measure of how many children are born per woman, stood at 2.12, almost exactly at the level needed to keep the population stable.
All of that seemed to change in 2008. When Lehman Brothers collapsed on September 15, 2008, the birth rate collapsed along with it. The number of births in America had already started slipping earlier in 2008 (~68,000 fewer babies than the year before) but by 2009, births had [dropped to 4,131,000](https://us.list-manage.com/jaeK7Zo7ORk?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) (~185,000 below the 2007 peak.) And it just kept falling. Through the recovery, through the bull market, through the lowest unemployment in half a century. Year after year after year.
Last year, [3.6 million babies were born](https://us.list-manage.com/uU2YngIohro?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586); that’s **700,000 fewer than the 2007 peak**. The fertility rate hit [another record low: 1.6 children per woman](https://us.list-manage.com/xCMIr1aPI3E?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), well below the replacement rate, and government demographers believe it will stay near 1.6 [through 2055](https://us.list-manage.com/mPvN_1ZGvij?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586)....

**Peter, I'm Troy Downing.** I bet you've never heard of me, but that's OK. I never thought in a million years I'd be sending you this final message pleading for your help.
I'm a combat veteran. A God-fearing Christian. A husband & a proud dad.

**I'll always tell the truth. ****
****I'll always put America First. ****
****I'll always have a backbone.**

# _Virginians Need A Representative With Grit_
---
| |
### _We’re tired of the status quo...are you?_
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
Washington has taught too many people that elections in our political system are won behind closed doors with wealthy donors and endless fundraising calls.
**Elizabeth Dempsey Beggs knows America was built differently.**
Most politicians ask Americans to trust a polished campaign with a bottomless financing pot, or a provocative and expensive television ad. Instead, Elizabeth is earning voters’ trust one mile at a time by running every mile of Virginia's First District, proving that no town is too small or too far off the map to matter.
For 250 years, Americans have endured through challenge upon challenge, emerging every time with greater strength and resolve. And there's something deeply American about the resilience of getting up and putting in the work, even when you’re tired and constantly busy. About showing up instead of making excuses. About believing that if you want the privilege of representing your community, you should be willing to push yourself to your limits for it._That’s what this run represents_.
Every mile Elizabeth runs is more than a campaign stop. It's a reminder that **democracy works best when leaders know the people they're asking to represent.**
That's the grit, determination, and work ethic she'll bring to Congress.If you're ready for a representative who believes trust is earned, not bought, help keep Elizabeth moving. Sponsor the next mile with a donation of $20 and help power another conversation with the people of Virginia's First District.

name: Anika Page
subject: What Do You Really Pay? The most complete picture of taxes ever built for Mississippi
body:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/dome-dispatch-12853883?e=5703353baa)
Good morning Friend,

Taxes have a way of hiding in plain sight.

Most of us know roughly what we pay in federal income taxes. If you've bought a vehicle recently, you probably remember what it cost to register it. Every time you stop to fill up at the gas station or pay your utility bill, you're paying taxes there, too.

But if someone asked you a fairly simple question—"How much do you actually pay in taxes each year?"—most of us would struggle to answer it.

That's not because the information isn't available. It's because it's scattered. Federal taxes are in one place. State taxes in another. Local taxes somewhere else. If you wanted the complete picture, you'd spend more time hunting for information than actually learning anything from it.

That struck us as odd.

Taxpayers deserve a simpler way to understand where their money goes. So over the past several months, that's exactly what we've been building.

Today, we're excited to introduce TaxToolMS.com, a free public resource from the Mississippi Center for Public Policy designed to help Mississippians better understand the taxes they pay and the government that spends them.

** Start With Your Household
------------------------------------------------------------

The first thing you'll notice is just how easy the site is to use.

Enter your household income and your ZIP code, and within a few seconds you'll receive a personalized estimate of your tax bill. There's no account to create, no email address to enter, and nothing is stored. Everything runs in your browser, so your information stays private.

It's simple by design because understanding your taxes shouldn't require creating another online account.

** Seeing the Whole Picture
------------------------------------------------------------

Most tax calculators focus on just one piece of the puzzle.

TaxToolMS was built differently.

For the first time, federal, state, and local taxes are brought together into one estimate so you can see what your household is actually paying across all three levels of government.

Even more importantly, the site doesn't stop at calculating your tax bill. It begins to answer the next question almost every taxpayer asks:

Where does all of that money actually go?

Interactive charts break spending into categories that are easy to understand, making government finances feel a little less like a spreadsheet and a little more like a conversation.
Federal + State + Local—all in one estimate.

** Ever Wondered Why Your Car Tag Costs So Much?
------------------------------------------------------------

It's one of those questions almost every Mississippian has asked.

Now there's an easy way to find out.

The Car Tag Calculator estimates your first-year registration costs, annual renewals, shows where those dollars go, and even lets you compare what the same vehicle would cost to register in neighboring states like Alabama and Tennessee.

Whether you're buying a new vehicle or simply renewing your tag, it removes much of the guesswork.
Compare Mississippi with Tennessee and Alabama.

** The Taxes You Probably Don't Think About
------------------------------------------------------------

When people talk about taxes, they're usually talking about income taxes.

But those aren't the only taxes we pay.

Every trip to the gas station, every utility bill, every vehicle registration—and even some everyday purchases—carry taxes or fees that often go unnoticed.

Individually, they may seem small, but added together, and they're an important part of your overall tax burden.

TaxToolMS brings those hidden taxes together so you can finally see the complete picture.

** Following the Money
------------------------------------------------------------

Transparency doesn't stop with your tax bill.

One of the newest additions to TaxToolMS is Mississippi DOGE, a searchable database that makes it easier to explore government spending. You can browse spending by agency, contractor, university, county, or vendor and see how taxpayer dollars are being distributed across state government.

Government spending has always been public information.

Now it's just much easier to explore.
Explore 110,000+ spending line items.

** How Does Mississippi Compare?
------------------------------------------------------------

Mississippi's tax system doesn't exist in a vacuum.

One feature of TaxToolMS allows you to estimate what your state and local tax burden would look like in every other state. It's an interesting way to compare Mississippi with the rest of the country and better understand how different tax systems affect families.

Whether you're simply curious or interested in public policy, it's a fascinating comparison.

** Built on Facts, Not Guesswork
------------------------------------------------------------

One question we've already been asked is, "Where do the numbers come from?"

That's an important question.

Everything you'll find on TaxToolMS comes from official sources, including the U.S. Treasury, the Mississippi Department of Revenue, the Legislative Budget Office, and the Tax Foundation.

We didn't create the data. We simply gathered it, organized it, and made it easier to understand.

** Why We Built This Tool
------------------------------------------------------------

TaxToolMS wasn't built for accountants or policy experts. It was built for Mississippi taxpayers.

Whether you spend five minutes exploring the site or an hour clicking through every feature, we think you'll come away with a better understanding of what you pay, where your money goes, and how Mississippi compares with the rest of the country.

After all, they're your tax dollars; you should be able to see where they go.
Visit TaxToolMS.com (https://taxtoolms.com/)

Warmest regards,

Anika Page
Director of Operations

# When We Count
# Voter Registration Training Series

---
| |
Building a blue electorate starts from the ground up, and expanding our voter base is the single most effective way to secure Democratic victories.
This month, the DNC is launching [**Voter Registration Best Practices**](https://us.list-manage.com/YA8nTLZGZks?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e), an exclusive four-part virtual training series designed to equip our partners with the data-driven strategies, resources, and refined tactics developed through our premier _When We Count_ program.

---

President Trump delivered a historic victory for our country in 2024 -- and he did it by ensuring every Republican had a plan to vote. It's up to us to do it again.
That's why we're proud to launch [Vote.MassGOP.com](https://qgzxgy5ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_H18Spzzh6aZUr9g-ye4fURPFDDHLJBKauP2Pm3u1d0R3W6-Q6vfw4YRt5Hjx5x4cVSajtYHJFlaTuigEMM8rbKUOSA8GosE51my4A4LITwSmNpn7ZZjqjBUyhiNmpVkShx0T8xGP8RG-AzjWoE8CQ==&c=6CqNoIWZgW0Nkd0EYkaUKiObDGaS1jUbxzpGpQuOGuDoiZuEBtgcxw==&ch=tJlkDPp13zWgbqi4LYwEdqdZ2Ifg3CmrH_cOCb_D5UmfWjdnJdehUA==) \- your election hub for:

As I reflect on our country's founding and this incredible 250-year journey, I want to hear from YOU!

I put together this quick poll to hear directly from you:

Have a wonderful and safe 4th of July!

Jen Kiggans 🇺🇸

Peter,

Lately, I've been thinking about my Dad a lot and how he taught me so much. He showed me how to fish. How to mow grass. How to drive a tractor. We would drive around our town for hours and talk while he showed me the roads, culverts, and other things he helped to build.

**I credit him with teaching me the value of hard work and just how much pride there is in building something from the ground up.** I have met so many parents in Iowa who work hard and sacrifice to take care of their families, just like my Mom and Dad did. My dream is to make sure we have a government that rewards their hard work, that ensures they don't just get by, but get ahead. _Yesterday showed me once again that I am not alone in this fight and that hard work runs in the very veins of our movement._

June marked one year since we launched this campaign, and June 30th marked our first end-of-quarter deadline since the primary. Yesterday, I asked for your help to deliver a strong fundraising report to show Mariannette Miller-Meeks and everyone watching that we have what it takes to win in November. **I'm so excited to report that not only did we reach our goal, but we exceeded it and had the BEST end-of-quarter fundraising performance since we launched!**

We didn't get here from nowhere, Peter. Each month since last June has brought a steady stream of hard work from our entire team to get our message out and make sure our campaign has all the resources we need to build a strong campaign. None of this would be possible without your support. Whether you've donated, signed a petition, knocked on doors for us, or even read just one email — I can't thank you enough for showing up.

Thank you,

Christina

# Iran and Ceasefire
* **Indirect technical talks in Doha:** Indirect negotiations between the United States and Iran continued in Doha on Wednesday, with Qatari and Pakistani mediators facilitating technical discussions on implementing the interim memorandum of understanding.
* Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani met U.S. negotiators, Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner on Wednesday, with the Emir's office saying they discussed the "progress of the negotiations" between Washington and Tehran as well as the situation in Lebanon and the "importance of consolidating the ceasefire."
* Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters the talks are going "very well" and described the meetings as "very good."
* Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi participated in a trilateral meeting with Qatar and Pakistan, and said the Doha meetings were focused on implementing the interim agreement rather than negotiating a new deal.
* **Iran will discuss frozen assets with Qatar, not the U.S.:** Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f0b17cd4-3859-4fe6-8ea2-e28ab796bdf3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that Iran will hold talks with Qatar in Doha on Wednesday to discuss implementing its memorandum of understanding with the United States, particularly the release of its frozen assets, but that the Iranian delegation has no plans to meet the American delegation "in the coming days."
* Baghaei said the talks would focus on Paragraph 11 of the MOU, which covers unfreezing Iran's restricted funds, stressing that what matters to Tehran is "gaining access to its funds and using them as it sees fit."
* Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson, Majed Al-Ansari, officially confirmed today that the $6 billion in frozen Iranian funds has not yet been transferred to Tehran; Qatari and U.S. officials have maintained that the frozen funds remain in Qatari accounts.
* Separately, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said recent agreements have enabled continued Iranian oil exports, eased some financial and foreign exchange restrictions, and created new opportunities for economic cooperation.
* **Iran and Oman proceed with fee-collection plan for Strait of Hormuz:** Iran and Oman are [moving forward ](https://substack.com/redirect/c36d72bc-104a-4b5e-a60c-6361a78ae4c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with a proposal to collect fees from ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, despite U.S. objections, the New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing Iranian and diplomatic officials.
* Oman reportedly proposed a system modeled on the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, where shipping companies "voluntarily" contribute to navigation and safety services. Iranian officials, however, say the payments would be mandatory.
* U.S. officials have received and are reviewing the Omani proposal, and are expected to offer revisions rather than rejecting the deal outright.
* The current U.S.-Iran framework agreement only guarantees free passage through the Strait for 60 days, after which Iran and Oman are expected to negotiate a longer-term arrangement for shipping through the Strait.
* Iran's Parliament Speaker and diplomat Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/38cf4d23-574a-4fb4-a2ff-dadbf506ca7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) later on Tuesday that Tehran had reached an agreement "on all legal and service-related matters" governing maritime services in the Strait, while insisting Iran would not cede its sovereignty over the waterway, which he called a "divine gift" given to the country during its recent conflict with Israel and the United States.

* **Araghchi warns Israel after Katz says Khamenei is "marked for death": **Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned Wednesday that "any threat against our People and Leadership will receive Immediate Powerful Response" after Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, was "marked for death." In a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/cd934c15-eb2d-411b-b6d8-56963c6cae20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, Araghchi said the terms of the Islamabad MOU were "crystal clear and public for all to see," adding that U.S. President Donald Trump had committed Washington to "muzzling its pets in Tel Aviv" and warning that "if they ignore their master, Iran will school them." Katz [said](https://substack.com/redirect/df9c5ba9-ab91-43dd-8757-da1de1cb4cf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that Israel could find itself at war with Iran "tomorrow," adding that the Israeli military had been instructed to prepare for an independent operation against Iran if necessary.
* **Report: President Trump considered reviving war with Iran:** President Trump [weighed](https://substack.com/redirect/e1293555-8aed-441b-8e5a-74fd88ba33b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) resuming full-scale war with Iran, holding multiple discussions with War Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine on new military strikes, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, but decided to continue diplomatic talks for now.
* **Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf talks Lebanon, oil, nuclear deal:** In a wide-ranging interview with Iranian state media on Tuesday, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf discussed the progress of the deal, its consequences for the region's energy industries, and gave additional details concerning the Iranian delegation's priorities ahead of a second round of negotiations.
* Ghalibaf [reiterated](https://substack.com/redirect/da6f9d54-984f-4f8b-a22a-872b9f6776c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Iran would not negotiate a final deal with the U.S. until Washington delivers on the core commitments it made under the MOU, pointing particularly to Washington's failure to secure a total ceasefire in Lebanon, Iran's demands that it allow for the sanction-free export of its oil and petroleum products, and the release of its frozen funds.
* Ghalibaf [stressed](https://substack.com/redirect/862c9ab8-e4fb-4d06-bf0b-173647b4dc3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Lebanon in particular, saying that the memorandum "seeks Lebanon's independence," whereas the framework agreement between Lebanon and Israel, mediated by the U.S., "seeks to normalize Lebanon's relations with the Zionist regime," and that it would put the Lebanese army "in service of the Zionist regime" by making it responsible for Israel's security.
* Ghalibaf also [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/862c9ab8-e4fb-4d06-bf0b-173647b4dc3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of working to undermine the memorandum of understanding during his recent tour of the Gulf, and of attempting to rally Gulf states against Iran.
* Ghalibaf [emphasized](https://substack.com/redirect/399c94b3-5a96-41d9-95b7-348c16fa8774?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that nuclear enrichment is Iran's "legitimate right," adding that Iran would continue to abide by the Non-Proliferation Treaty. He also argued that "domestic strength and a strong position on the ground" would be the country's only guarantees of safety, and that it would not negotiate its missile capabilities.
* In the interview, Ghalibaf [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/d5e85bbd-93c1-42a1-8c82-b85f24516ef7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that in the "10-12 days" since Iran had lifted its blockade, it had exported more than 40 million barrels of oil.
* **Vance claims U.S. is using Iran deal to "refill" the oil market: **Vice President JD Vance said the Trump administration is using the memorandum that ended the war with Iran "to sort of refill" the world's oil supply during an appearance on the Michael Knowles Show on Monday.
* Vance [said](https://substack.com/redirect/37e787b2-61c8-4136-ba77-0cf6a26e8c86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the U.S. has two options going forward: either a long-term deal requiring "a significant change" in Iranian behavior or banking its gains from its military campaign against the country while keeping renewed strikes on the table. Both options, he said, remain "very much in play."
* The vice president also claimed that oil traffic through the Strait had "reached its pre-war height." "We're seeing more oil come out of the Strait of Hormuz, and some days actually more oil coming out of the Strait than came out before the war even started," he said.

* **UN says evacuation of stranded Hormuz seafarers remains suspended:** The evacuation of roughly 8,500 seafarers [stranded](https://substack.com/redirect/21273f3b-7472-4c06-a3f2-7265975844a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in and around the Strait of Hormuz remains suspended until security guarantees are in place, according to International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez.
* Dominguez said on Tuesday that 2,500 seafarers were evacuated before operations were paused.
* Dominguez also came out [against](https://substack.com/redirect/ed447ba3-4b42-424f-94bc-e67b8f9e22b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) mandatory tolls on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, calling the arrangement unlawful, but proposed a voluntary funding system--like that which governs the Strait of Malacca--as an alternative.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli shelling and demolitions in southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire": **An Israeli drone [dropped](https://substack.com/redirect/e2b26bdc-34ea-4802-b683-d3744b59a140?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three stun grenades over the southern Lebanese town of Yater on Wednesday afternoon, while Israeli forces also opened fire at a civilian vehicle near the spring of Ibl al-Saqi, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. In Sour (Tyre), Israeli artillery shelling targeted the outskirts of Beit Yahoun. Israeli forces also [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/1eb158ac-6e6e-4280-80cd-d41ec9869904?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) overnight demolitions of several homes in the Beit Yahoun-Hadatha area and in the town of Tayri in Bint Jbeil district.
* **Israel claims it killed a Hezbollah fighter in southern Lebanon as it delays withdrawal:** The Israeli military [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/016d5403-583d-4933-89bd-94f310f4d499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it killed a Hezbollah fighter in southern Lebanon on Tuesday, as Israeli media reported that Israel's withdrawal from two "pilot zones," in Zawtar and the Froun-Ghandourieh area, has been delayed pending agreement on a U.S. oversight mechanism.
* Israeli officials told Lebanon that leaving the zones "will take time," a Lebanese military official told The National.
* On Wednesday morning, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz vowed to keep Israeli troops "indefinitely" within its "security zones" in Gaza, Syria, and Lebanon. "We will not withdraw from the security zones," Katz said.
* **Lebanese President defends Washington "framework" amid widespread criticism: **Lebanese President**** Joseph Aoun [defended](https://substack.com/redirect/38e76294-1b6b-431f-97d9-87c13dc79c22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Washington framework signed with Israel on Tuesday, saying it is "not an agreement but a framework" that includes provisions for an Israeli withdrawal, the return of displaced people and prisoners, and the repatriation of the remains of Lebanese held in Israel, NNA reported. Aoun argued Lebanon "did not compromise its judicial, political or field principles," and called on critics to present alternatives.
* He also urged opponents not to take the dispute to the streets or portray the outcome as "surrender and humiliation." Aoun praised Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri for establishing two "red lines" during the negotiations--preventing sectarian strife and protecting the Lebanese army; Berri had denounced the framework on Monday, calling it a set of "diktats."

# Palestine
* **Israeli strike kills two in Al-Mawasi:** An Israeli strike on the Al-Mawasi refugee camp in Khan Younis overnight Wednesday [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/4ef750d4-8775-41bf-9ec7-5823d8fe3118?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two people, and injured several others, according to WAFA.
* **Israeli forces detain 20 Palestinians in West Bank, including five women and a journalist:** Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/78e34a51-e167-400f-8d92-c752a8434910?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 20 Palestinians across the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, between Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Society. Those detained included five women and a Palestinian journalist from Bethlehem.
* The group said Israeli authorities have intensified raids since the start of the war on Gaza, with more than 24,000 arrests recorded in the occupied West Bank during that period. It added that the number of Palestinian women held in Israeli prisons has risen to 99, while the number of detained journalists has reached 42, including two held under enforced disappearance.
* Separately, Israeli police [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/fc4d3919-88ed-4052-8697-70d4c7a9e9c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) mourners at a funeral near Bab Al-Asbat in Jerusalem, according to WAFA, firing tear-gas canisters and rubber-coated metal bullets at the protesters.
* **Israeli police kill Palestinian man in Lydd, sixth this year:** Israeli police shot and [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/811b11a6-e1e6-4274-99a3-3ee8947ef31a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man in his twenties, in the city of Lydd, inside the 1948 territories on Wednesday, WAFA reported.
* The man, who was identified as Sami Ahmed Ja'sous, was the sixth person killed by police in the city since the start of the year, amid growing reports of excessive force by Israeli police in Palestinian towns.
* Separately on Wednesday, two more young men were killed in Basma and Shfaram, bringing the total number of killings in Palestinian communities inside Israel since the beginning of the year to 139.
* **Report: Israeli plan to herd Palestinians in Gaza into controlled "shelters" set to begin within weeks: **Israel is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/e04b0d98-480e-4eda-a828-b95a1e61bafc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to push Palestinians into fenced "humanitarian shelters" in areas outside Hamas governance, policed by a foreign force, while its military deepens its occupation of the rest of Gaza, according to the Likud-aligned Israeli outlet Israel Hayom.
* Under the plan, unarmed civilians would be directed to a zone in Tel Al-Sultan, near Rafah. A multinational force, the ISF proposed by Trump's "Board of Peace," would deploy to the area from a newly built base, equipped to police the zones, while the Israeli military would "continue to maintain and deepen its hold" beyond the "Yellow Line."
* The camp/base for the force "has already been built," the report claims, and the board has "begun identifying sites" for logistics warehouses. Buildup in the area was also apparent in an image posted by the board, which showed tactical vehicles arriving at an area logistics base on June 30.
* A political source told Israel Hayom: "We are maneuvering within the American constraints, increasing the pace of targeted killings while remaining below the threshold of international criticism--and this will continue as long as Hamas is unwilling to disarm."
* The plan matches what Drop Site has previously exposed through leaked documents: a surveilled, checkpoint-controlled "planned community" in Rafah designed to force Palestinians into what amounts to an Israeli panopticon, tracked and screened as a condition of receiving aid. **Drop Site 's full report on that buildup is available [here](https://substack.com/redirect/4f307242-1b1f-49c0-a5a0-d231af7e77b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

* **Guterres calls on countries to cover $100 million UNRWA funding gap:** UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres [called on](https://substack.com/redirect/f3b1c024-7bdc-4cbe-95e7-ffa1f7107361?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) countries Tuesday to cover a $100 million funding gap for UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, warning that millions of people are at risk due to the shortfall. _By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at[ Julian@dropsitenews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/6d36c26a-0ec8-4935-b821-528cca2bfa17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
* **Primary results:**
* Progressive and democratic socialist **Melat Kiros** [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/48f46702-aba4-4a8c-b2e6-f7413a9542f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) incumbent **Rep. Diana DeGette** in Tuesday's Democratic primary to represent the state's 1st congressional district, which covers much of the Denver area. The 29-year-old Kiros, an attorney and doctoral student, was born in the same year DeGette was first elected to Congress, and was able to overcome the incumbent despite a last-minute infusion of cash into DeGette's campaign from Big Tech and pro-Israel interests (reported on by Drop Site, **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/f29303bd-bbff-4916-969e-75116bad0a45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**). * Colorado Attorney General **Phil Weiser** upset U.S. Sen. **Michael Bennet** in the state's Democratic gubernatorial primary. The state has been represented by a Democratic governor since 2007, making Weiser the heavy favorite to succeed Governor **Jared Polis**. Bennet's campaign received millions of dollars in donations from former New York City mayor Michael Bloomberg, and he was initially favored to win the race. Weiser, who initially showed little difference in his platform from Bennet, pivoted left toward the end of the campaign, which may have helped secure his victory.
* Former governor and current Sen. **John Hickenlooper** defeated a challenge from progressive State Senator **Julie Gonzales** in the Democratic Senate primary, a race in which Gonzales was outspent 8 to 1. Gonzales campaigned on housing affordability, immigrants' rights, climate protection and securing universal healthcare. She called for abolishing ICE. Hickenlooper will now face Republican state Sen. **Mark Baisley** in November's general election.
* **Supreme Court issues more decisions:**
* **Strikes down Trump 's bid to end birthright citizenship: **The Supreme Court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/a35e6adf-2822-448d-b453-72cde899cb3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 6-3 Tuesday that President Donald Trump's executive order attempting to deny automatic citizenship to children born in the U.S. to foreign nationals violates the 14th Amendment. Chief Justice **John Roberts** wrote for the majority, joined by Justices **Amy Coney Barrett** , **Elena Kagan** and **Ketanji Brown Jackson** , that children born to parents unlawfully or temporarily present are "subject to the jurisdiction" of the U.S. and are citizens at birth under the Citizenship Clause. Justice **Brett Kavanaugh** concurred in part but disagreed that the order violated the 14th Amendment, while Justices **Samuel Alito** , **Neil Gorsuch** , and**Clarence Thomas** dissented. Drop Site's **Julian Andreone** **[asked](https://substack.com/redirect/2106ff30-c3ce-4928-85f7-ae0dced9ca75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** members of Congress about the ruling.
* **Lifts limits on party campaign spending:** The Supreme Court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/d24d530f-79ef-4eb1-a2de-969b0f2ee45a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 6-3 along ideological lines Tuesday that federal limits on coordinated party expenditures violate the First Amendment, striking down caps on party spending in National Republican Senatorial Committee v. Federal Election Commission. The ruling overruled a 2001 precedent and is expected to help Republicans in the midterm elections by undercutting an advantage Democrats have in using their small-dollar donations to reduce television advertising rates.
* **Rules states can ban trans girls from girls ' school sports: **The Supreme Court [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/b515aff5-8a2a-4a69-97b8-91e27444b1e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday that states can ban transgender girls from girls' school sports teams, upholding West Virginia's ban in West Virginia v. B.P.J. and a similar Idaho law in Little v. Hecox. The ruling is expected to empower the anti-transgender political movement in its fights over bathrooms, IDs, and gender-affirming care.

* **Trump earned nearly $1.2 billion from crypto businesses last year, filing shows:** President Donald Trump [took in](https://substack.com/redirect/c0983906-199e-423c-9f1e-1ccdb12c2c92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nearly $1.2 billion from his crypto businesses last year, according to a federal disclosure filing released Tuesday with the Office of Government Ethics, with more than $500 million from World Liberty Financial's token sales and more than $600 million from CIC Digital LLC's sale of Trump-branded meme coins. * **House Republicans block amendments targeting U.S. arms transfers to Israel:** The Republican-led House Rules Committee [blocked](https://substack.com/redirect/9cc1a3b1-cb19-4b4e-bfbd-01e763b0fe00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an amendment to the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act from Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** (D-N.Y.), ruling it not "in order"; as a result, it will not reach the House floor for a vote.

That bipartisan amendment sought to strike Section 219 (formerly Section 224), which would create a "United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative" merging the two countries' defense technology, intelligence, and research, an integration critics say no other U.S. ally has.
* Rep. **Thomas Massie 's** amendment, which would [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/706edf6f-40bc-456e-9563-a7c81755225f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $3.3 billion in foreign aid to Israel from the State Department's 2027 bill, was ruled in order. Other members discussed the amendment with Drop Site Capitol Hill correspondent Julian Andreone;**see their responses[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/2efee9b1-aa8a-4274-8003-7e1a6fda45ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

# Other International News
* **Amnesty report finds that Sudan 's RSF committed ethnic cleansing in El-Fasher**: A new report by Amnesty International found that Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing during its 2024-2025 campaign to seize the city of El-Fasher in northern Darfur.
* The group said it interviewed 247 victims and witnesses and found that RSF forces systematically attacked settlements around El-Fasher housing the Zaghawa community, with fighters burning homes after residents fled.
* During the final RSF offensive on El-Fasher in October 2025, Amnesty stated that "hundreds were executed, and many others were tortured or detained" as they attempted to flee, noting that human rights violations were systematic and that "those in positions of authority knew, or should have known, what was occurring, and failed to stop it or hold anyone accountable."
* Separately, a report from the Yale School of Public Health's Humanitarian Research Lab published on Tuesday [found](https://substack.com/redirect/662d92d5-96ee-4953-882c-74010917220b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Rapid Support Forces have intensified attacks on civilian infrastructure in El Obeid, worsening an already severe humanitarian crisis. Researchers identified damage consistent with aerial bombardment at at least eight fuel stations and new damage to the city's electrical substation between May 25 and June 25, triggering a citywide blackout of at least four days, shutting down water pumps, and forcing the closure of emergency departments and a kidney dialysis center due to fuel shortages.
* The report also found more than 700 new temporary shelters at displacement camps over the past month, pointing to a sharp influx of displaced civilians, and warned that El Obeid, a city of more than 500,000 people, faces worsening food and water shortages as RSF forces tighten their siege.
* **Russia shuts down rail crossings with EU border states** : Russia suspended rail traffic through some of its last remaining border crossings with the European Union, halting the movement of people, vehicles, goods and cargo by rail with Finland, Estonia and Latvia as of July 1.
* Moscow described the closures as "temporary" in a public statement but gave no explanation or timeline for reopening, while formally notifying the Baltic states of the move.
* The decision to halt crossings comes amid an increasing campaign of Ukrainian strikes targeting major urban areas in Russia and as Russia expands military infrastructure near NATO's northeastern flank, including reported new barracks, ammunition depots and logistics hubs near Finland, Norway and the Baltic states.
* **Cuba says U.S. talks show "no progress" amid new threats**: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez [said](https://substack.com/redirect/7260ff02-edb6-49a9-9682-812289baa861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) negotiations with Washington have hit a wall, accusing U.S. officials of pairing "generally respectful" talks with "constant threats," coercive measures, and attacks on Cuba's sovereignty.
* Rodriguez said the U.S. was also trying to derail a UN debate over Washington's decades-long trade embargo, which has been in place since the 1960s, as the Trump administration escalates its current energy blockade on the country.
* **New EU report says world 's oceans hit hottest June on record**: The world's oceans [recorded](https://substack.com/redirect/e446418d-6ded-4cf8-8406-f0b8220b1c79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their warmest June ever observed, with average global sea-surface temperatures reaching 21°C, according to the European Union's Copernicus Marine Service.
* The agency said June's temperatures surpassed the previous records set in 2023 and 2024, capping a first half of 2026 marked by "persistently elevated" sea-surface temperatures and widespread marine heatwaves. Copernicus said marine heatwaves expanded through the first six months of the year, eventually affecting roughly 82 percent of the global ocean, with the Mediterranean, central North Atlantic, and equatorial Pacific among the key hotspots.
* **Syria names lawmakers for new transitional parliament:** Syrian authorities [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/c37175ba-a21d-4fb1-ad66-9c7c7ee9cb8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 70 new lawmakers appointed by interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa to complete a 210-member transitional parliament, clearing the way for the parliament to convene its first session next week.
* The chamber will have limited powers under the presidential system Sharaa has established since ousting Bashar al-Assad in 2024; two-thirds of its members were chosen last year through regional electoral colleges formed under a committee appointed by Sharaa.
* A temporary constitution introduced in March 2025 granted parliament limited powers under the system put in place following the collapse of the previous government and the new parliament temporarily excludes representation from the Druze-majority area of Sweida which has remained outside the control of Damascus since clashes last year.
* **Taliban says it struck Pakistani territory as border conflict escalates:** Afghanistan's Taliban government [said](https://substack.com/redirect/1da35891-486c-43c5-9571-992313b419fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday it launched air strikes on Pakistani territory in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces, targeting what it said were members of an ISIL affiliate, while Pakistan's military said it intercepted four "rudimentary drones" launched by Taliban forces into Balochistan.
* Pakistan warned that continued provocation from the Afghan Taliban "would receive a befitting response which would cost them heavily," and the Taliban's defense ministry posted on X describing the strikes as retaliation for deadly Pakistani air attacks on eastern Afghanistan earlier in the week.
* **Firebombings target homes linked to Greece 's governing party**: Unknown attackers [firebombed](https://substack.com/redirect/f8299b30-75e2-4ab3-9b5f-3e0cd952d942?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three residential buildings tied to Greece's ruling center-right New Democracy party in Thessaloniki before dawn Wednesday, wounding five people, police said. A New Democracy parliamentary candidate and her mother were among those injured, both suffering burns after gas canisters were set alight outside the buildings.
* A spokesman for the party said that the bombings "were a proper terrorist attack on the homes of New Democracy members," adding that "those who carried it out aimed to kill."
* **Cepeda says he won 't recognize de la Espriella as president over sovereignty concerns: **Colombian presidential candidate Ivan Cepeda [said](https://substack.com/redirect/509e5d10-d713-4fe8-9d41-b3920cec119a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday he will not recognize fellow candidate Abelardo de la Espriella as president unless de la Espriella renounces his U.S. citizenship and clarifies whether he has collaborated with U.S. security or intelligence agencies.
* Cepeda also noted in his statement de la Espriella's past work for disgraced businessman and convicted money launderer Alex Saab and his support from President Donald Trump.
* He demanded that de la Espriella respect Colombian judicial sovereignty and halt any effort to extradite President Gustavo Petro, warning he would call for peaceful civil disobedience if those conditions go unmet.
