Hi Peter,
I was 16 the first time I spoke to my taipo , or my great grandmother. I have been lucky to know her for my entire life, as she is 109 years old and lives in California. She is smart, resilient, and full of strong opinions, and she loves our family fiercely.
But she doesn’t speak English. My taipo speaks Mandarin, Russian, and Japanese. So for most of my life, I haven’t been able to speak with her directly. For years, my grandparents or my mother translated for us. They connected us, acting as a bridge, when we were not able to communicate with each other directly.
I grew up in Delaware, across the country from my grandparents and over an hour away from the closest Chinese school. My parents would have loved to give me the opportunity to learn Mandarin earlier, but that kind of commute just didn’t work for my working parents. It was out of our reach. I didn’t start learning Mandarin until I was in high school. It was only after studying Chinese for two whole years that I was able to have a real conversation with my taipo.
I was nervous the first time we spoke, but I was giddy with excitement upon the realization that I could speak to her. She made me laugh. My family had always told me she was funny, but as she complained about the construction of women’s clothing, I got to learn first-hand that she is hilarious, and that her turn of phrase is so unique she basically has her own dialect.
Learning Mandarin allowed me to connect to my great grandmother, and to my community as part of the Chinese diaspora in America. Being able to speak multiple languages with some fluency means that I am able to help my community here. I can use my ability to connect with people to inform my neighbors of what is happening locally. I can empower people with knowledge that is often only available in English so that they can take action and advocate for the future that our communities want to see in the world. I can act as a bridge for my community.
Keep reading to learn how you can take action.
In solidarity,
Sophia Liston
Operations & Language Justice Coordinator
Asian Pacific Islander Political Alliance
Protecting Philly Small Businesses
Members and volunteers visiting City Council to talk to elected leaders about taxes. [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AV001/1/82704/images/06.09.2026%20Philadelphia%20Visit%20to%20City%20Hall-2.jpg]
Members and volunteers visiting City Council to talk to elected leaders about taxes.
A few months ago, I was in a laundromat in West Philadelphia. I was the first person who was able to tell the manager about this year’s changes to the local tax codes that many small businesses would be paying the Business Income & Receipts Tax (BIRT) for the first time. No one had told him. There was some outreach in the city in English, but barely any in the other languages spoken by the people of Philadelphia. He showed me his water bill and the new occupancy taxes he paid. These tax changes are a huge burden on his livelihood, but nobody had given him the information he needed to prepare for it.
Before I left that day, I made sure he signed our petition so that the City Council can know how these changes are impacting our communities and that we’re not happy about it. Signing the petition also means that we are able to go back to him with more in-language information whenever there is news to share.
If you want to be a part of creating a city where we protect our small businesses and everyone pays their fair share in taxes, sign the petition and get involved! [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/small-business?contactdata=QjrRH86tsnwUwxJqrJyl+mnM+sEAouN2xVlVAgeBz2SWuT+7Gl+O61xVRiX0NB1fS0+opvRweR65PKWk4dQ2l9GqYNrRtJqv+FpEDrMXs0EnoJLvbUkCY4hemzYiFdUrGUw/3CWrOBqbufCFlrRoOpZXtB9Uy+tnrS/jh6UQ49U=]
Sign the Petition [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/small-business?contactdata=QjrRH86tsnwUwxJqrJyl+mnM+sEAouN2xVlVAgeBz2SWuT+7Gl+O61xVRiX0NB1fS0+opvRweR65PKWk4dQ2l9GqYNrRtJqv+FpEDrMXs0EnoJLvbUkCY4hemzYiFdUrGUw/3CWrOBqbufCFlrRoOpZXtB9Uy+tnrS/jh6UQ49U=]
Ending collaboration with ICE in Dauphin County
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AV001/1/82704/images/06.04.2026%20Harrisburg%20Press%20Conference-2.jpg]
Everyone deserves to feel safe seeking help when they need it. Whether it's enrolling a child in school, visiting a doctor, accessing county services, or reporting a crime, no one should have to worry that doing so could put their family at risk.
For many immigrant and refugee families, language access is a critical part of keeping their families safe. When people can access information and services in the languages they speak, they are better able to get the support they need, understand their rights, and fully participate in their communities.
That's why we're organizing for a Welcoming County Resolution in Dauphin County. This policy would require language access for county services, and protect residents' privacy by preventing county officials from assisting ICE, CBP, or other immigration agencies without a warrant signed by a judge.
Sign the petition to make Dauphin County a place where everyone can access services with dignity, regardless of where they were born or what language they speak at home. [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/welcoming-dauphin?contactdata=QjrRH86tsnwUwxJqrJyl+mnM+sEAouN2xVlVAgeBz2SWuT+7Gl+O61xVRiX0NB1fS0+opvRweR65PKWk4dQ2l9GqYNrRtJqv+FpEDrMXs0EnoJLvbUkCY4hemzYiFdUrGUw/3CWrOBqbufCFlrRoOpZXtB9Uy+tnrS/jh6UQ49U=]

* * *
For nearly four months, a sitting member of Congress -- representing one of the most competitive battleground districts in the country, in the middle of an illegal war and an economic gut-punch -- simply vanished. No explanation. No public schedule. No votes. Tom Kean, New Jersey's 7th District, last cast a vote on March 5th. He missed well over 140 votes after that. And almost nobody in Washington or the corporate press seemed to give a damn.
Now he's back. And the explanation is that his doctors recommended hospitalization for depression.
Let me be very clear about something before I say anything else: depression is real. I've lived it. It took real work to climb out of that hole, and I know exactly how it wrecks you -- mentally, physically, all of it. I'm genuinely glad Kean got care. I mean that. Nobody should be shamed for getting treatment for a mental illness, and the more public officials who are honest about that struggle, the better -- it opens the door for other people to get help too.
But here's the thing. Kean isn't just some guy. He's a member of Congress. And that comes with a different standard.
You do not get to disappear for four months, with no explanation to your constituents, while the country is dealing with an illegal war and an economic calamity, and just expect everyone to shrug it off when you resurface. If you didn't show up to your job for four months with zero explanation, you'd be fired. And good luck finding another job after that. That's not partisanship. That's the two-tier system in this country in one clean example -- the people who are supposed to answer to us operate by a completely different set of rules than the rest of us do.
And I want to be honest about something else: I'm skeptical. Not of depression as a diagnosis -- of these people's honesty in general. This crowd lies about everything, constantly, reflexively. I hope this story is exactly what he says it is. But given the track record of the people currently running this country, forgive me for not taking anything at face value anymore.

* * *
I should also note that dealing with depression didn't stop Kean from abusing his office to do more insider trading. Apparently nothing will stop these guys from profiteering off taxpayers. And that's become one of the defining features of American politics: the people with the most power have convinced themselves the rules simply don't apply to them. They disappear. They enrich themselves. They lie. They abuse public office. And then they act genuinely offended when anyone suggests there should be consequences.
Here's what actually disqualifies Tom Kean: It isn't that he got depressed. It's that he wasn't honest with the people who elected him, that he disappeared during one of the most consequential stretches in recent American history, and that the entire time he was getting taxpayer-funded care, he was voting to gut the exact system that gives regular people access to that same care. Kean voted for the so-called "One Big Beautiful Bill" -- the one that guts Medicaid, the single largest funder of mental health services in this country, and that let ACA tax credits expire, sending premiums up more than a hundred percent for millions of families. He voted to make it harder for his own constituents to get the kind of help he needed and received. The people writing the rules rarely have to live under them themselves.
So no -- he shouldn't lose in November because he had depression. He should lose because he wasn't honest, because he was absent when his district needed him most, and because he spent his career voting to strip away the very safety net he leaned on himself. Forget party for a second. That's disqualifying on its own.
And this isn't just a Kean problem. This is a Washington problem. We have a generational leadership crisis in this country -- a Congress full of people clinging to power well past the point they should've handed it off, members literally dying in office because nobody will step aside, and almost total silence about the health of the people running the country. Joe Biden's inner circle lying to the public about his decline for a year and a half is a huge reason Donald Trump is sitting in the White House again right now. And right now, Trump himself is visibly, obviously declining -- medical experts have said as much -- while his people trot out comparisons to NFL players and lie about his weight and his cognitive state like we're all supposed to just believe it. That boy ain't right, and everyone around him knows it.
It's the same mindset you hear when Mike Johnson defends members of Congress trading stocks because they have to "support their families." Members of Congress already make far more than the median American household. Millions of families survive on forty or fifty thousand dollars a year without access to insider information. The problem isn't that Congress can't support itself. The problem is that too many people in Congress have forgotten they're public servants, not a protected class.
We need real transparency about the health of the people who hold power over our lives. Not because getting sick is shameful -- it isn't -- but because these are people with enormous responsibility, who are susceptible to manipulation and burnout just like anyone else, and the public has a right to know if the person making decisions about war and the economy is actually capable of doing the job. The same standard should apply to every abuse of public trust. If you misuse power, lie to the people you represent, or use public office for private gain, there should be consequences. And this isn't about vengeance. It's about making sure no one is above the standards everyone else is expected to live by. Without that, power just keeps rewarding itself.
And this can't just be a Democratic talking point. Republicans need to hold their own accountable here too, or nothing changes.
If you're reading this and you're struggling -- with depression, anxiety, whatever it is -- I mean this sincerely: reach out. I've been in that hole. I know how dark it gets. You are not alone, and getting help is never something to be ashamed of.
But getting help and being honest with the people who trusted you with power are two different things. Tom Kean failed at the second one. That's why he should lose.

name: Michael Baumgartner
subject: Happy 250th Birthday America! A Message from Our Family
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vote Baumgartner for Congress | www
body:
Join us in celebrating 250 years of American liberty this 4th of July!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/15rE3H8h8aI?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# 250 Years of Freedom:
# A 4th of July Message
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/xYO_KRVtPAm?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| |
As we celebrate the 250th anniversary of our nation’s independence this 4th of July, we are so grateful for the enduring blessings of liberty that our Founders secured for us and the generations that have followed. Two hundred and fifty years ago, brave patriots declared that we are endowed by our Creator with unalienable rights: Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness. Their bold vision still guides us today as we work to protect freedom and the American Dream right here in Eastern Washington.
This tremendous milestone reminds us that our Republic thrives when we remain united in defending the principles that make America exceptional. In Congress, I remain committed to fighting for the hardworking families and communities of the 5th District — through strong national security, economic opportunity, and preserving the cherished way of life in our rural communities.
A highlight of serving in Washington DC is walking through the US Capitol Rotunda and seeing the spectacular paintings that tell the story of our nation’s history through some of our most decisive moments - an experience that I’ve been so pleased to be able to share with many of you visiting from back home.
Eleanor and I, along with our children, wish you and your families a safe and meaningful Independence Day. Whether you’re gathered with loved ones for a parade, fireworks, or a backyard barbecue, may this celebration renew our shared appreciation for the greatest country on earth. From our family to yours—Happy 250th Birthday, America! God bless you, and God bless the United States of America.
---
|
---
| |
# Standing Tall for Washington at the Great American State Fair
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/nGDwBdr_F2N?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| | Because Governor Bob Ferguson chose not to have Washington officially participate in the Great American State Fair (one of the main events of our nation’s 250th birthday celebration on the National Mall), I decided to step up and personally represent our state at the booth. What I found was a bare and stripped-down display, minimal compared to the lively and engaging pavilions from states like Idaho and Texas.
Still, I was proud to represent the Evergreen State. I stamped the “passports” for fairgoers, and showed visitors that Washingtonians know how to celebrate America. It’s disappointing when partisan politics get in the way of honoring our country. We should ALWAYS put pride in America above politics.

---

---
| |

This event features local entries, music, and family activities.

This event features a 5k, chalk contest, fishing derby, parade and so much more![T](https://us.list-manage.com/16G6ew5LG1k?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)hank you for all your encouragement and support!Happy 4th July!-Michael

name: Susan Collins
subject: A lesson from my mom to you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Collins for Senator
body:
From the potato farms to Washington

| [](https://trk.email.goprelease.)
---
"Susan, you cannot let the farmers down; they are counting on you."
When my mom sat me down and told me those words, I was just a young girl working on the potato farms. This was a large responsibility at such a young age.
It taught me a profound lesson about accountability, community, and leadership. The farmers relied on us to protect their livelihoods. If we didn't show up and work hard, an entire family's year of labor would be lost.

For 250 years, America has been the greatest nation on Earth - not because government made us great, but because freedom did.
We became a magnet for the most talented, hardworking people in the world. We rewarded innovation. We celebrated success. We believed that if you worked hard and played by the rules, you could build a better life for yourself and your family.
That's the America I grew up believing in.
Unfortunately, there are people today who want to take us in a different direction.

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: A clear winner.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
The results are in for Team Karen. We WON this Forum!

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| |

Friends,**What. A. Night.** Last night's Johnson County Post Candidate Forum was exactly what this campaign has been building toward. For over an hour, Kyle Palmer asked tough questions of all three candidates, including questions submitted by Johnson County residents. I came ready. You can listen to the forum here: [JOCO Post Facebook Live Video](https://us.list-manage.com/xABdWSuXyAz?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)I came prepared with facts and solutions._And yes, I came prepared to challenge the record of the current County Chair._ For too long, Johnson County government has grown without enough accountability. Spending has exploded. Property taxes continue to climb. The government keeps getting bigger while too many families are asking how they're going to afford to stay in the county they love.Those questions deserved answers. Instead, much of the evening became a defense of the status quo.The differentiation was stark:Mike Kelly defended the last four years and made no acknowledgement that there is a problem.I challenged the status quo.Months of studying budgets, reading commission packets, researching county policies, and listening to residents showed. This campaign isn't built on slogans. It's built on doing the homework and having the courage to ask the questions others won't.Johnson County deserves leadership that isn't satisfied with "good enough."We deserve a County Chair who asks hard questions before spending your money, who measures results, who believes transparency isn't optional, and who remembers every dollar in the county budget belongs to you.Thank you to everyone who watched, attended, volunteered, donated, and encouraged me along the way.We're building something special.If last night confirmed for you that it's time for new leadership, I need your help now more than ever.
* **Volunteer.**[**I want to join #teamKC**](https://us.list-manage.com/ut8boW0ldef?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
* **Put up a yard sign - sign up here:**[**YES! I want a sign!**](https://us.list-manage.com/1nEY12oZVVb?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
* **Make a contribution:**[**DONATE**](https://us.list-manage.com/E_sxiu5XXUQ?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
* **Tell your neighbors why you're supporting this campaign.**

The momentum is real, and together we're going to bring common-sense leadership back to Johnson County.Let's finish this.Karen CrnkovichCandidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

Friend of Life, It’s July and this time of year often causes us to reflect. We celebrate our country. We remember the foundation it was built on. We talk about freedom, about life, and about the generations that will be shaped by what we do right now. But for many women across our country, those ideas feel very far away at the moment they need them most. Right now, a woman is facing an unexpected pregnancy and being told that abortion is the easiest way forward. Not because it’s what she truly wants, but because she believes she has no other option. That’s the moment PreBorn! exists to meet. At a PreBorn! Network Clinic, a woman is welcomed with compassion and offered a free ultrasound. She sees her baby, often for the first time, and is given the space to truly consider what she’s about to do. And in that same appointment, she hears something many have never truly heard—that she is not alone, that her life has value, that her baby’s life has value, and that she is deeply loved by Jesus.

body:
Summer is officially here and I'm so excited!

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
### Summer is officially here and I’m so excited. I love Colorado summers. The farmer’s markets, the patriotism, the county fairs... all of it. It’s also always meant young kids are out of school and older kids are home. I’m excited to spend some time with family in July, but want to recap all that kept this campaign busy in June first!
---
| |
### Best, Eileen.

|
---
| | June was packed, in the best way. We were able to visit seven counties this month for various events and meet and greets. But I think one of the most impactful events of the month fell on the 16th. **Congressman Jason Crow and I hosted a roundtable in Windsor with over 60 veterans.** We discussed so many important topics including VA and healthcare issues, after service care, support groups, deployment, the current war in Iran, and national security. It’s so important that we talk _with_ our veterans, and not just about them.
Another event that left a dramatic impression on me was the Wheat Field Days event in Akron hosted by the USDA and Colorado State’s Department of Agricultural Sciences. **85% of Colorado’s wheat crop comes from CO-04 and this year has been incredibly difficult for our famers with the drought**. We need a comprehensive and supportive Farm Bill — it’s now three years overdue and Lauren Boebert still hasn’t done anything about it.
I was also able to visit another rural hospital in Kiowa County. **Weisbrod Memorial County Hospital faces unsustainable operating margins and aging infrastructure on top of the looming federal Medicaid funding threats.** The town of Eads and all of Kiowa County rely on Weisbrod and we must find ways to support these crucial facilities.
With the Colorado primaries yesterday, **my family and I also cast our ballots!** I loved practicing my civic duty with Chris and the kids!
One last thing I am always buoyed by every month is the **many gatherings of community around the district and June** , being the start of summer, was a month to remember with many picnics, festival kickoffs, and start-of-summer activities. I’m looking forward to more in July!

clean_body: Summer is officially here and I'm so excited! | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Summer is officially here and I’m so excited. I love Colorado summers. The farmer’s markets, the patriotism, the county fairs... all of it. It’s also always meant young kids are out of school and older kids are home. I’m excited to spend some time with family in July, but want to recap all that kept this campaign busy in June first! | | Best, Eileen. | | | | | | | | June was packed, in the best way. We were able to visit seven counties this month for various events and meet and greets. But I think one of the most impactful events of the month fell on the 16th. Congressman Jason Crow and I hosted a roundtable in Windsor with over 60 veterans. We discussed so many important topics including VA and healthcare issues, after service care, support groups, deployment, the current war in Iran, and national security. It’s so important that we talk with our veterans, and not just about them. Another event that left a dramatic impression on me was the Wheat Field Days event in Akron hosted by the USDA and Colorado State’s Department of Agricultural Sciences. 85% of Colorado’s wheat crop comes from CO-04 and this year has been incredibly difficult for our famers with the drought. We need a comprehensive and supportive Farm Bill — it’s now three years overdue and Lauren Boebert still hasn’t done anything about it. I was also able to visit another rural hospital in Kiowa County. Weisbrod Memorial County Hospital faces unsustainable operating margins and aging infrastructure on top of the looming federal Medicaid funding threats. The town of Eads and all of Kiowa County rely on Weisbrod and we must find ways to support these crucial facilities. With the Colorado primaries yesterday, my family and I also cast our ballots! I loved practicing my civic duty with Chris and the kids! One last thing I am always buoyed by every month is the many gatherings of community around the district and June , being the start of summer, was a month to remember with many picnics, festival kickoffs, and start-of-summer activities. name: Tom Fitton
subject: We Wont Stop Fighting For Clean Elections
body:
The U.S. Supreme Court has just issued an astonishing 5-4 decision which declined to require states to reject ballots that arrive after Election Day. While this wasn’t the outcome we hoped for... ...our resolve to fight for fair and honest elections is stronger than ever.
| [ ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=14409&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8b1ea2406c2235a7e72abe41770202fd3fe922e3a9843b295763736d5e3f2fd4)
---
Dear Fellow American, The U.S. Supreme Court has just issued an _astonishing_ 5-4 decision which declined to require states to reject ballots that arrive after Election Day. While this wasn't the outcome we hoped for... **... our resolve to fight for fair and honest elections is stronger than ever. ** | [Fuel Our Fight For Clean Elections ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
As Justice Alito noted in his dissent, this week's decision "creates a serious risk of further undermining public confidence in our elections" by inviting significant voter fraud. With the notion of a unified Election Day eviscerated, enforcing federal law and **ensuring states have _clean and accurate rolls_ is one of the most important firewalls left against stolen elections. ** | [We're Not Backing Down ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
Fortunately, _no organization has done more to clean voter rolls_ than your Judicial Watch. Our litigation has already led to the **removal of nearly 7 million ineligible names nationwide** and we'll be _redoubling our efforts_ in light of this decision. In fact, federal judges have just allowed Judicial Watch's **new voter roll lawsuits** to proceed in **California** and **Illinois** with _[more to come with your support](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_. | [Will You Stand With Us? ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
Thanks to the support of our loyal members, Judicial Watch scored a **landmark victory** at the Supreme Court earlier this year affirming the right of federal candidates to challenge election laws in their states. And,, our army of supporters just helped our team bring the fight for Election Day all the way to the High Court for a second time. And, _[with YOUR contribution we will keep fighting](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ for clean voter rolls, common sense voter ID laws, and upholding other laws protecting American voters. | [Fund The Next Battle ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
Each of our battles for election integrity requires great cost and years of litigation. Our resolve is limitless, but our resources aren't. If you're in a position to do so, please _[refuel our resources with a special contribution](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ to help Judicial Watch fight for the fair and honest elections Americans deserve. With your partnership, we will NEVER back down. Sincerely, Thomas Fitton
President P.S. The Supreme Court's astonishing decision threatens to make a mess of our nation's already stressed federal elections, but _[with contributions from supporters like you Judicial Watch will never stop fighting](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ for clean elections This is the perfect time to stand with us and [refuel our fight.](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83840&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ | Judicial Watch, Inc.

Peter, I’ve spent my career standing up to powerful special interests
that care more about making money than protecting people, communities, and the

subject: Defend the forests that make Oregon home
body:
https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2?am=20&amtOpts=&recurringAm=20&recurringAmtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=MjOtRA1SResbBXy7nhAlX/Ht0mOj2TYprZTmGnFrpt2CGHSTIDpFUwQTHbel0wYDUV8yDw1JDpAdi9Y2toDgda1E1YurqTkNnWvQpqan+ROK+4/unDib66L5JR8OdbfU [https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2?am=20&amtOpts=&recurringAm=20&recurringAmtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=MjOtRA1SResbBXy7nhAlX/Ht0mOj2TYprZTmGnFrpt2CGHSTIDpFUwQTHbel0wYDUV8yDw1JDpAdi9Y2toDgda1E1YurqTkNnWvQpqan+ROK+4/unDib66L5JR8OdbfU]
Hi Peter,
This holiday weekend, thousands of Oregonians will head into the forests we love most, pitching tents beneath towering trees, hiking familiar trails, cooling off beside mountain streams, and making memories in the public lands that belong to all of us.
But while we celebrate these places, they’re facing some of the biggest threats we’ve seen in generations.
From Mount Hood National Forest to the Columbia River Gorge, nearly 2 million acres of Oregon’s forests are at risk if the Trump administration moves forward with plans to repeal the Roadless Area Conservation Rule: one of the strongest protections our national forests have ever had ( read more [https://morethanjustparks.substack.com/p/trump-admin-targets-five-of-oregons?utm_source=post-email-title&publication_id=1594349&post_id=195273529&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=5ksrax&triedRedirect=true] ).
The Roadless Rule protects these wild places from industrial logging and road construction, preserving clean water, wildlife habitat, and the forests that communities across Oregon depend on. Oregonians have made their voices clear: when the Roadless Rule was opened for public comment, more than 99% of comments opposed the administration’s plan to eliminate these protections.
But now, instead of listening to the public, Senate Republicans are trying to repeal the Roadless Rule through Congress.
Senator Mike Lee has been one of the leading voices behind efforts to roll back conservation protections under Trump 2.0, putting our public lands at risk for the benefit of corporate polluters and logging interests.
Meanwhile, Oregon Congresswoman Andrea Salinas is fighting back with the Roadless Area Conservation Act (RACA), legislation that would permanently protect these treasured landscapes. OLCV and LCV are proud to support her work, but defending Oregon’s forests requires a strong grassroots movement behind it.
These forests aren’t just lines on a map. They’re the places where we go to reconnect, recharge, and remember why Oregon is worth protecting.
This summer and holiday, while you’re gathering outside to enjoy the beauty of Oregon’s public lands, I hope you’re reminded that these places belong to all of us. It’s up to all of us to defend them and protect them for generations to come.
Will you give a generous gift to OLCV today to power our work defending Oregon’s forests, holding decision-makers accountable, and protecting the places that make our state special? [https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2]
Protect Oregon's Forests [https://secure.everyaction.com/YnnBhNxoe0-gdDf_E1iL8Q2?am=20&amtOpts=&recurringAm=20&recurringAmtOpts=&is_optimized_ask=true&contactdata=MjOtRA1SResbBXy7nhAlX/Ht0mOj2TYprZTmGnFrpt2CGHSTIDpFUwQTHbel0wYDUV8yDw1JDpAdi9Y2toDgda1E1YurqTkNnWvQpqan+ROK+4/unDib66L5JR8OdbfU]
The fight to protect our forests won’t happen without people like you standing up.
Thank you for helping protect Oregon’s forests today and for generations to come.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Sarah%20Signature.png]

Trump’s cruel attacks failed — SCOTUS reaffirmed birthright citizenship is the law of the land.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260701-6421-footer&t=1&akid=6421%2E420207%2ESfLR70)
Peter,
Yesterday, the Supreme Court reaffirmed that birthright citizenship is exactly what we’ve always known it to be: **a constitutional right, not a privilege that the Trump administration gets to revoke with the stroke of a pen.**
I’m an immigrant myself. I came to this country when I was just 16 years old, and it took me 17 long years to get my US citizenship. I know exactly what it means when this country keeps its promises — and I know exactly how devastating the cost is when those promises are broken.
Since Trump launched this cruel, xenophobic attack on birthright citizenship, families across the country have lived under a cloud of fear that their children could be born without a country to call their home.
**That fear never should’ve existed.** It was manufactured entirely by an administration obsessed with cruelty and division. This ruling should settle this issue once and for all — but we know who we’re dealing with.
Trump and his MAGA allies have shown us _exactly_ who they are. They won’t stop trying to rewrite the rules of our democracy. **And I refuse to let that happen.**
I’m going to continue fighting in Congress to protect our families and make sure the promise of this ruling — and the promise of the Constitution — is protected.
**If you’re born in America, you’re an American._Full stop._**
[**If you’re able, will you pitch in $3, or whatever is meaningful to you today, to keep me in Congress fighting to protect our democracy and our Constitution?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260701.nzKIgE&refcode=em20260701-6421&amount=3&t=2&akid=6421%2E420207%2ESfLR70)

Yesterday, the Supreme Court agreed to hear two cases on the constitutionality of assault weapons bans – likely deciding if weapons of war are allowed on our streets.
This is a big deal. Here’s what you need to know:
In 2012, our country experienced one of the deadliest school shootings in U.S. history. A gunman entered Sandy Hook Elementary School and used his semi-automatic rifle to fire off 154 bullets in less than five minutes. Twenty first-graders and six educators were killed.
Enough was enough. Connecticut lawmakers took action to ban dangerous weapons like AR-15’s in their state. 9 other states and D.C. followed suit, banning assault weapons. This was a massive win for public safety.
**The gun lobby wants to get rid of those bans.**
If the gun lobby gets their wish, we could see even more weapons of war flooded into our neighborhoods — and there’s nothing your state or local government could do to stop it.

body:
Right now, a woman is facing an unexpected pregnancy and being told that abortion is the easiest way forward.

| | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkc-OnDAMxp_G3GYUEgjkwKES4lBpq3bVP0dkjIdJm4QoCbvq21dUMw-wR3_-9LN-8q-X-QWts2H7gp6HVG5zyjNheOfESPc7JxuK9TxLIfVFdBdRn426WoeVVqyp4qHuemlUI1td3Qe9NOtCtNKtXbRZjGFBpjU9YXvrm66u7HCiRCfq2ijRNldt-rYxihpVc9-jgEag41SuieOxOEsYCuY_tz0RX2n3lRvupcQM6hPICeS02Te-xsTLnsJZADk9JpATxsjoMqgpE6jx849RaKm_voLU6AuoUfYg9ZZBjRhA6qP4Oe9HIgY1xrTnyFRs2B4rz6s9PKiRPVr3CAl9RLsFUOPvw_19pnsoHM4TP-X8rbu8fp8uT_UqDWt8t87ZrDtoxHbS_suVjzzhbZD_AgAA__94OpFG)
---
Friend of Life, It’s July and this time of year often causes us to reflect. We celebrate our country. We remember the foundation it was built on. We talk about freedom, about life, and about the generations that will be shaped by what we do right now. But for many women across our country, those ideas feel very far away at the moment they need them most. Right now, a woman is facing an unexpected pregnancy and being told that abortion is the easiest way forward. Not because it’s what she truly wants, but because she believes she has no other option. That’s the moment PreBorn! exists to meet. At a PreBorn! Network Clinic, a woman is welcomed with compassion and offered a free ultrasound. She sees her baby, often for the first time, and is given the space to truly consider what she’s about to do. And in that same appointment, she hears something many have never truly heard—that she is not alone, that her life has value, that her baby’s life has value, and that she is deeply loved by Jesus.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkc-OnDAMxp_G3GYUEgjkwKES4lBpq3bVP0dkjIdJm4QoCbvq21dUMw-wR3_-9LN-8q-X-QWts2H7gp6HVG5zyjNheOfESPc7JxuK9TxLIfVFdBdRn426WoeVVqyp4qHuemlUI1td3Qe9NOtCtNKtXbRZjGFBpjU9YXvrm66u7HCiRCfq2ijRNldt-rYxihpVc9-jgEag41SuieOxOEsYCuY_tz0RX2n3lRvupcQM6hPICeS02Te-xsTLnsJZADk9JpATxsjoMqgpE6jx849RaKm_voLU6AuoUfYg9ZZBjRhA6qP4Oe9HIgY1xrTnyFRs2B4rz6s9PKiRPVr3CAl9RLsFUOPvw_19pnsoHM4TP-X8rbu8fp8uT_UqDWt8t87ZrDtoxHbS_suVjzzhbZD_AgAA__94OpFG)
---
This is how babies are saved and this is how the gospel is shared. **[That’s why, this July, we’ve set a clear goal: to provide 250 ultrasounds each day for mothers facing this decision across our country.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkc-OnDAMxp_G3GYUEgjkwKES4lBpq3bVP0dkjIdJm4QoCbvq21dUMw-wR3_-9LN-8q-X-QWts2H7gp6HVG5zyjNheOfESPc7JxuK9TxLIfVFdBdRn426WoeVVqyp4qHuemlUI1td3Qe9NOtCtNKtXbRZjGFBpjU9YXvrm66u7HCiRCfq2ijRNldt-rYxihpVc9-jgEag41SuieOxOEsYCuY_tz0RX2n3lRvupcQM6hPICeS02Te-xsTLnsJZADk9JpATxsjoMqgpE6jx849RaKm_voLU6AuoUfYg9ZZBjRhA6qP4Oe9HIgY1xrTnyFRs2B4rz6s9PKiRPVr3CAl9RLsFUOPvw_19pnsoHM4TP-X8rbu8fp8uT_UqDWt8t87ZrDtoxHbS_suVjzzhbZD_AgAA__94OpFG)** Because these decisions are happening right now. And these moments cannot be missed. **$28 provides one ultrasound.** One opportunity for a mother to see her baby and a life can be protected.
One moment where fear gives way to a different future.
One moment where the gospel is shared and a life is changed. This is how babies are saved and this is how the gospel is shared. Because these decisions are happening right now. And these moments cannot be missed. $28 provides one ultrasound. A full summary (so far) of yesterday's primary election
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey folks,
There was a lot to unpack from last night's primary election, and plenty of headlines, hot takes, and numbers flying around. We'll have much deeper analysis in the coming days, but if you're looking for the quick and easy version, here's what you need to know about the biggest races, the surprises, and what they could mean heading into November.
Last night's Colorado's primary election reshaped both parties' November ticket, with the biggest stories so far emerging on the Democrat side.
Attorney General **_Phil Weiser defeated U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet_** in the governor's race, while 29-year-old democratic socialist **_Melat Kiros unseated longtime Denver Congresswoman Diana DeGette_** in one of the night's biggest upsets. Progressive candidates also captured Democrat nominations for secretary of state and attorney general, signaling continued momentum for the party's activist wing.
On the Republican side, the _**governor's race remains too close to call**_ as Barb Kirkmeyer and Victor Marx traded a razor-thin lead, while Michael J. Allen secured the GOP nomination for attorney general and Mark Baisley advanced unopposed for U.S. Senate.
Turnout reached about _**36% of Colorado's active voters**_ , with more than 1.4 million ballots returned. **_Democrat ballots outnumbered Republican by roughly 62% to 38%_** , a gap driven largely by unaffiliated voters, who chose the Democrat ballot by about a _**70-30 margin**_. Results remain unofficial as counties finalize their counts.
As results come in, especially for the GOP nomination for Governor, we'll keep you updated on social media.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, July 1, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[How one volunteer connected the dots at RMV’s Freedom Fest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
After Freedom Fest ended, Pueblo resident Randy Thurston was still talking his way through the weekend. Not in order. One speaker reminded him of another, and a story from Saturday connected to something he had heard Friday. He was not replaying the event. He was still putting it together.
“I still don’t know how she pulled it off,” he said, meaning Rocky Mountain Voice founder Heidi Ganahl. “I don’t know how she even had that vision and then the ability to manifest it. Do you know what it took to get everybody there on the weekend before the Fourth of July? That in itself was impossible.”
A little later, after talking through several of the presentations, he came back to it again. “Any one of these speakers, I would’ve driven a thousand miles to see,” he said. “But to have all of them here under one roof ... it was the most incredible experience or opportunity you can ever imagine.”
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Energy Secretary Chris Wright makes the case for data centers, and admits they’re not for everyone](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Wright criticized Colorado's energy policies by name, arguing that "climate cult" ideology has made energy more expensive and driven businesses out of the state — and warned that the same fear-mongering now targeting data centers once nearly killed the fracking industry that transformed America from the world's largest oil importer into its largest exporter.
* Making a national security case, Wright argued that AI dominance will determine the global superpower of the 21st century, and that allowing China to win that race carries dire military consequences — framing data center construction as a strategic imperative, not a local zoning fight.
* Wright pointed to American nuclear power — especially small modular reactors — as the answer to powering the AI economy, noting communities that host data centers benefit from frozen electricity rates and new generation paid for by developers, not ratepayers.

******[Pride changed. I didn’t.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY VALDAMAR ARCHULETA | COMMENTARY | JUNE 30** _As the world wraps up another June, filled with rainbows and unicorns, I, as a gay Republican, reflect on 30 days of what always ends up being unproductive conflict. And once again, I prepare to face the inevitable question: “How can you be a gay Republican?"_
____
**[An open letter to Elon Musk](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | JUNE 30** _Dear Elon, You do not know me. I am one of millions of Americans who will likely never meet you, never stand on a launch pad, never design a rocket engine, never build a global company, and never appear in the history books. Yet I owe you a debt of gratitude._
**[Volunteers bring America’s 250th birthday party to Grand Junction’s fairgrounds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | JUNE 30**
_July 4 has always meant fireworks in Grand Junction. This year, a group of local volunteers think it should mean something more. Liberty on the Lawn – America 250 comes to Mesa County Fairgrounds/Lions Club Park on July 4, noon to 7 p.m. It’s free. Bring a chair, a cooler and the kids._
**[They almost stayed home: What a Douglas County couple took away from RMV’s Freedom Fest](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JUNE 29** _By Saturday morning, Russ and Deb Minary were home, a refrigerator due to be delivered and an ordinary weekend resuming around them. They couldn’t stop replaying the day before. They almost hadn’t gone. Their Friday had cleared at the last minute, and they drove over for day one of Rocky Mountain Voice’s two-day Freedom Festival, marking America’s 250th birthday and Colorado’s 150th._

Fellow American - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington.

**I grew up in the back of a bar.**
Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill.

After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves.

That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake.

The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today.

clean_body: I was the first in my family to go to college. | Fellow American - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington. I grew up in the back of a bar. Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did. I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13. I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb. That's the South Carolina way. That's the American way. After law school, I put on the uniform. I became a U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate - military prosecutor, defense attorney. Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves. That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake. The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today. And the folks on the other side of the aisle? They're perfectly happy to hand your neighborhood over to open borders, pile new taxes on your paycheck, and tell you to be grateful for it. I won't stand for it. Not for a second. We are in a fight for the future of this country, and it is not a time to sit on the sidelines. I didn't come from money. I came from a bar in South Carolina, a mother who worked hard, and a faith that hard work still means something in America. It still does. Thank you for standing with me. God bless you, and God bless South Carolina. July 4th—but in a liberal way

# The Fight Continues
---
| |
## _Join us this week_
---
| | **Peter,****An exciting week awaits us. After a week filled with candidate forums and events with high-profile Democratic elected officials, we are hearing the same thing over and over: our message is resonating with people. From the Northern Neck to the Richmond suburbs, people are demanding bold, progressive leadership to meet this moment and restore accountability in Washington. But we cannot do that without your help.**
**Election day is five weeks from tomorrow, and we must maximize every opportunity to reach voters over the phone, through the mail, and at their doorstep. We are asking you to be a part of this effort.**
**We are hosting**[**two phone banks this week: Tuesday, 6/30, from 5:30-6:30pm; and Thursday, 7/2, from 6:45-8:00pm.**](https://us.list-manage.com/j_NTzo8QHPw?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)****
[**On Friday, July 3rd, we are knocking doors in Glen Allen from 4:00pm-6:15**](https://us.list-manage.com/12RKXmXB182?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**. Our field operations team will be present for training and guidance.**
**We will be traveling throughout the district to celebrate July 4th.**[**From 8:00am-11:00am, we will be in Chesterfield to march in their July 4th parade**](https://us.list-manage.com/jrRHy_npTwF?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**. We will be handing out flags, celebrating our country, and sharing Elizabeth’s vision with voters.**
**The afternoon will take us to**[**Colonial Williamsburg, where we will be from 1:45-4:00pm.**](https://us.list-manage.com/fItNscL8FGn?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**Stop by at any time, say hi, and ask Elizabeth anything!**
**To conclude July 4th, we will be in**[**Historic Williamsburg from 5:00-9:00**](https://us.list-manage.com/wc7dVp1H6wA?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**. There will be a concert, food, fireworks, and a community full of patriots committed to restoring the promise of our founders.**
[**On Sunday, we are hosting a postcard writing and pool party in Mechanicsville from 10am-noon**](https://us.list-manage.com/18y5jH4ueQ_?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)**. Bring a swimsuit, sunscreen, and your passion for democracy.**
**On Sunday night at 7:00, Elizabeth will be conducting her weekly volunteer briefing on Instagram Live. Make sure to follow @elizabethforvirginia and tune in!**
**For most of this campaign, our grassroots movement was considered a long shot. But now, experienced leaders and organizations are acknowledging the momentum we are building. Every phone call made, every door knocked, and every postcard mailed could be the difference between winning and losing this election. Join us this week to contribute to this movement and build community!**
**—Team Elizabeth.**

#
Peter,
Colorado's primary results are in, and the battle for November is set.
**We have a massive opportunity to flip two critical congressional seats, defeat two extreme, anti-family Republicans, and build a firewall for the House majority.**
[**If you’re ready to help Voto Latino register, mobilize, and turn out Latino voters across Colorado’s key battlegrounds, will you rush a contribution of $3 right now?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260701-1.dsOvC7&amount=3&refcode=em20260701-332&t=1&akid=332%2E1366028%2EF93FjS)

**CO-08:** Colorado's most heavily Latino district, and a dead-heat tossup. Republican incumbent Gabe Evans voted to gut Medicaid for 176,000 constituents, blocked health care tax credits, and backed tariffs that spiked costs. Democratic nominee Manny Rutinel is a Spanish-speaking son of a single immigrant mom, grew up on Medicaid himself, and has passed legislation lowering health care costs and expanding affordable housing.
**CO-03:** A vast rural district with a decisive Latino population. Republican incumbent Jeff Hurd voted to slash SNAP for 110,000 constituents, gut Medicaid by nearly $1 trillion to protect billionaire tax loopholes, and hand $70 billion to hostile immigration enforcement targeting local neighborhoods. Democratic nominee Dwayne Romero is ready to lead — but winning this massive territory takes an aggressive ground game, starting now.
Evans and Hurd chose their party's extreme agenda over their constituents. Both are vulnerable — but only if we build the turnout to beat them.

body:
Please forgive the lengthy letter

| | | | [](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)
---
| | | Dear Fellow Conservative, Please forgive the lengthy letter, but we're celebrating an emotional moment in our nation's history, _and every word I 've written comes straight from the heart_. 250 years ago, the greatest, freest, and most prosperous nation in history was born. Our Founding Fathers boldly took on the world's largest empire to declare our independence and proclaim that our rights and freedoms do not come from government - but from _Almighty God Himself_. When Benjamin Franklin was asked what sort of government America has, he said... **_" A Republic, if you can keep it..."_** Those words send a shiver down my spine every time I read them. You and I both know firsthand how hard we must work to keep it. We've all witnessed how close our Republic has come to the brink. How many times have we seen our freedoms get trampled on? ...Our freedom of speech, our Second Amendment rights, our religious liberties, our right to privacy, our right to make medical choices, our right to leave our home during the COVID lockdowns, our right to run a business, our right to private property - and so many more - have all been challenged time and time again by those who wish to see our Republic fail. But every single time there's been even the smallest encroachment on our freedom, patriots like YOU have recalled the courage and resilience of our Founding Fathers and stood up in the name of liberty. **And by God, America has survived 250 years as a Free Republic.** As we celebrate this incredible milestone in not just American history but _world history_ , we cannot forget that the enemies of freedom are still hard at work. So my question to you is this: **_will you do your part to keep it?_** **So if you can, and only if you can - I really mean it - [please make a contribution of _$17.76_ to ensure that America survives another 250 years](https://trk.email.tedcruz.). [[LINK]](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)** In liberty,

clean_body: Please forgive the lengthy letter | | | | | | | Dear Fellow Conservative, Please forgive the lengthy letter, but we're celebrating an emotional moment in our nation's history, and every word I 've written comes straight from the heart. 250 years ago, the greatest, freest, and most prosperous nation in history was born. Our Founding Fathers boldly took on the world's largest empire to declare our independence and proclaim that our rights and freedoms do not come from government - but from Almighty God Himself. When Benjamin Franklin was asked what sort of government America has, he said... " A Republic, if you can keep it..." Those words send a shiver down my spine every time I read them. You and I both know firsthand how hard we must work to keep it. We've all witnessed how close our Republic has come to the brink. How many times have we seen our freedoms get trampled on? ...Our freedom of speech, our Second Amendment rights, our religious liberties, our right to privacy, our right to make medical choices, our right to leave our home during the COVID lockdowns, our right to run a business, our right to private property - and so many more - have all been challenged time and time again by those who wish to see our Republic fail. But every single time there's been even the smallest encroachment on our freedom, patriots like YOU have recalled the courage and resilience of our Founding Fathers and stood up in the name of liberty. And by God, America has survived 250 years as a Free Republic. As we celebrate this incredible milestone in not just American history but world history , we cannot forget that the enemies of freedom are still hard at work. So my question to you is this: will you do your part to keep it? So if you can, and only if you can - I really mean it - . Dear friend,
I wanted to reach out to say thank you.
Yesterday, I spoke with Phil Weiser – to congratulate him on his victory and to commit to continuing our partnership in service of Colorado when he becomes governor.

While the results are not what we hoped for, I’m proud of what we built together.
We chose to fight for a Colorado where working families can afford to get ahead, where young people can build their futures here and where we take on big challenges with big ideas instead of accepting the status quo. Sometimes the harder path is the right one, even when it doesn't lead where you hoped.
Thank you to everyone who knocked on doors, made phone calls, hosted events, volunteered your time, contributed what you could, and had conversations with friends and neighbors – all in support of our shared belief that Colorado can become the best place in America to build a life. I am also endlessly grateful to my incredible campaign team and to Susan and our girls, whose love and support have made every step of this journey possible.
**None of this would have been possible without you.**
I still believe Colorado's best days are ahead of us, and I remain committed to fighting for affordable housing, lower health care costs, stronger schools, our public lands, greater opportunity, and the values and freedoms that define our state.
It remains the privilege of my life to serve Colorado in the United States Senate, and I will continue showing up every day to do that work. I'll continue standing up for Colorado whenever our values, our freedoms or our democracy are threatened, and I'll always work to ensure the next generation has every opportunity to build their lives here.
**Thank you for believing in this campaign, for believing in Colorado and for believing in me. It’s been an honor to fight alongside you.**
With gratitude,

Michael

name: Justice Democrats
subject: At least 6 new Justice Democrats are going to Congress
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

After democratic socialists swept the New York primaries last week,
establishment Democrats panicked and claimed this was a fluke limited to
NYC. They were wrong.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260701-2.8OM6Rb&refcode=em20260701-37981&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37981%2E1203867%2EXLf7x- ]Google news screenshot of Fox News headline: "Melat Kiros becomes 28th
far-left candidate to win a Democratic primary this year as socialists
amass power"; preheader: "Melat Kiros, backed by Democratic Socialists of
America and Justice Democrats, won the Colorado 1st congressional district
Democratic..."

Justice Democrats and the progressive movement are WINNING more than ever
before, including yesterday’s heated primary for Colorado’s 1st
congressional district.

JD-endorsed democratic socialist Melat Kiros beat a 30-year incumbent and
more than $2 million in super PAC spending, defeating Rep. Diana DeGette
by 10 points in yet another massive upset for the corporate and
AIPAC-backed establishment.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260701-2.8OM6Rb&refcode=em20260701-37981&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37981%2E1203867%2EXLf7x- ]Screenshot of primary results for Melat Kiros and Diana DeGette. It
shows Melat as the projected winner: "Melat Kiros Wins the Colorado
Primary" with her image on the right of the title. The graph shows Melat
with 67,959 votes, 51.3% of the vote, while Diana DeGette (Incumbent)
secured 55,179 votes, 41.7% of the vote

This is Justice Democrats’ most successful primary cycle EVER. In the last
week alone, we took out 40 years of incumbency across 3 races. So far,
we’re sending at least 6 new Justice Democrats to join our bloc in
Congress, with another two candidates advancing to the general election in
November.

But we’re not done winning yet. We have three more 2026 primary elections
to go:

→ Donavan McKinney vs. Shri Thanedar in Michigan’s 3rd district on Aug.
4th.
→ Cori Bush vs. Wesley Bell in Missouri’s 1st district on Aug. 4th.
→ Justin J. Pearson for the open seat in Tennessee’s 9th district on Aug.
6th.

These final races are our chance to unseat two more Do-Nothing Democratic
incumbents, defeat AIPAC and corporate super PACs, and send three more
bold progressive fighters with moral conviction to fight for workers and
against fascism in Washington. And make the establishment cry some more.

Primary by primary, we’re doing what we set out to do: transforming the
Democratic Party and unseating the out-of-touch incumbents who refuse to
get out of the way.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260701-2.8OM6Rb&refcode=em20260701-37981&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37981%2E1203867%2EXLf7x- ]Let’s do it again (and again, and again) next month: fuel our work now
to get out the vote for Donavan, Cori, and Justin and win these final
primary fights →

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260701-2.8OM6Rb&refcode=em20260701-37981&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=37981%2E1203867%2EXLf7x- ]Contribute $5

Let’s keep this momentum going and show the country that this is a
movement, not a moment. With your support, this is only the beginning.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260701-37981-footer&t=1024&refcode2=37981_1203867_XLf7x-&akid=37981%2E1203867%2EXLf7x-

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe: https://go.justicedemocrats.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=1025&akid=37981%2E1203867%2EXLf7x-

| | | Peter, **I'll get straight to the point because there isn't time to waste.** A brand-new poll from the _New York Times_ and Siena College just dropped -- and it shows me and my far-left Democrat opponent, James Talarico, tied at 47% each in the race for U.S. Senate in Texas. _This is a blaring alarm warning for all conservatives!_ Texas hasn't sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in almost 40 years -- since 1988. And right now, the liberal media and Democrat donors smell blood in the water. They think this is their year to **flip Texas blue** with Talarico... _Here's what the poll found that should alarm every conservative in this state:_ **Talarico is leading me by 27 points among independents, and he is up 18 points with women voters overall ...****** This is a man who stood on the floor of the Texas House and declared "God is nonbinary," and who has argued that there are "six biological sexes." * * *
_**by Dana DuBois**_
I nearly missed the fourth anniversary of _Dobbs v. Jackson Women 's Health Organization_ -- the day the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade and handed the states permission to do whatever they wanted with our bodies.
It was last week. June 24, 2026. Substack reminded me (_thanks, Substack_).
And at once I wasn't sitting at my desk anymore. I'm transported to my mother's Lexus on McNab Road in Tamarac, Florida, where I'm sweating despite the cranked AC, wiped out and dreading the days ahead, when the radio announcer tells me Roe is gone.
I was exactly as gobsmacked as I should've been, and also exactly too overloaded to process any of it.
I'd taken a last-minute red-eye the night before because my stepmother had died unexpectedly and my father -- who has dementia, who had COVID -- was alone at the house. I can never sleep on planes and had dozed maybe an hour at my mom's before hopping in her car and racing to my dad's to sort things out when Roe went down. In South Florida. In a red state. Surrounded, metaphorically, by the people who'd made it happen.
My father is a lifelong Republican, an avid Trump supporter. He doesn't have a problem with abortion so much as he loves bullies and loathes immigrants. His wife was the same, till her dying day, literally. And I was interrupting my life to manage theirs, seething with a rage I had no outlet for, because their votes, their beliefs, had caused this.
I thought about every conversation I'd had with them since 2016, when I started saying we were going to lose abortion access. The quiet eye rolls. The calm dismissal. Every single time.
_You 're catastrophizing, Dana.
Roe is settled law.
I can't imagine that ever happening._
If the past decade has taught me anything, it's that Americans have spectacularly shitty imaginations.
Then I drove to pick up my father in the wreckage of the thing he helped build, and I took care of him, and nobody apologized.
That's the part women never talk about enough -- not the being proven right, which is its own complicated thing, but the _afterward_. The way we absorb the consequences of being dismissed and then have to keep showing up anyway. Keep caregiving. Keep loving. Keep driving through South Florida on an hour of sleep while the country announces it's decided we matter even less than we thought.
They call us hysterical. They always have.
The word itself tells you everything. _Hysterical_ comes from the Greek _hystera_ -- uterus. The ancient diagnosis for women who wouldn't calm down, who felt too much, who saw things men didn't want to see. The language they invented to dismiss us was named after the organ they wanted to control.
This isn't a coincidence. This is a blueprint.
Women said Roe was going to fall. We were called hysterical. It fell. No one apologized. Women said the voting rights protections were fragile. We were called hysterical. The SAVE Act passed in the House and barely died in the Senate -- for now. No one apologized. Women said birth control was next. We were called hysterical. The quiet legislative pressure on contraception access has been building for three years. No one's apologized for that either.
The pattern isn't incidental. The pattern is the point.
The consistent thread running through it all? The United States hates women.
I know what you're thinking: there are countries where women are publicly executed for the crime of being assaulted. Where girls are mutilated, and aren't allowed an education. Where we aren't even a comparison point. And you're right. But the United States is supposed to be the proof that it could be different--the country where women were gaining ground, not losing it.
The fact that we're moving toward those countries instead of away from them isn't a defense. It's an indictment.

On the morning of September 16, 2024, [Emily Waldorf](https://substack.com/redirect/45f5bb6d-d608-44ac-b33e-a8b1e4b51f1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s preschooler found her curled on the bathroom floor. She was 17 weeks pregnant and bleeding. She and her husband rushed to Washington Regional Hospital in Fayetteville, Arkansas, where Waldorf worked as a physical therapist.
The pregnancy wasn't viable. She was miscarrying.
But there was still a fetal heartbeat. And because Arkansas has one of the strictest abortion bans in the country, that heartbeat -- even attached to a pregnancy that couldn't be saved -- mattered more than the woman carrying it.
Her doctor [told her](https://substack.com/redirect/45f5bb6d-d608-44ac-b33e-a8b1e4b51f1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): _" Our hands are tied behind our backs. Tell your friends to vote differently."_
She waited. Her cervix was dilated, her uterus exposed to bacteria. The risk of infection rose every hour. The hospital's risk-management team was consulted twice. Their answer didn't change: there's still a heartbeat, we can't proceed. The standard medical guideline -- induce within 12 to 24 hours to prevent infection -- didn't matter. Her life, her humanity, her choice, didn't matter. The law mattered.
On day four, her water broke, a three-inch blood clot bursting from her body, followed by a steady drip of amniotic fluid, draining out of her.
Still, her doomed baby's heart beat on.
It was a depraved race: either the heartbeat stopped on its own, or Emily's condition had to worsen to sepsis before anyone could act. There was no option in which the baby survived. There were plenty when Emily wouldn't, either. And yet, they waited.
_" Are they going to let me die?"_ Waldorf asked.
And they would have. I don't blame the hospital workers entirely -- they faced potential penalties of up to $100,000 in fines and 10 years in prison. That's a nearly impossible choice. But I blame the politicians who wrote those laws. And I blame every single person who voted for them, knowing this was the natural outcome. These people _are_ America right now. They're culpable. They would've rather let Emily die, left her toddler motherless, than grant her bodily autonomy and life-saving care.
Finally after five days and many battles, she rode four anxious, bumpy hours in an ambulance to Kansas, where the team promptly induced labor. She delivered her baby. Then post-delivery she hemorrhaged and nearly died. She made it -- barely. This almost certainly wouldn't have happened if she'd been induced five days earlier.
Emily Waldorf couldn't understand it. Raised Baptist in a Republican family, she kept asking: how could an abortion ban aimed at women who wanted to end their pregnancies keep doctors from helping a woman who desperately didn't?
I don't say what I'm about to say without compassion. But I want to name it: _how was she surprised by any of this?_
Women like me weren't surprised. We've been called hysterical for years for _not_ being surprised.
I don't know how Emily Waldorf voted. I have my suspicions: Baptist, Republican family, Fayetteville, Arkansas. We know what that combo typically means. She's now joined a lawsuit challenging the state's abortion ban, which is good. I'm glad she's fighting. But I keep turning over the same question: why did it have to happen to her first?
This is the empathy gap. A significant portion of white women voted for the politicians who wrote these laws -- not because they hate themselves, but because they couldn't imagine it landing _on them_. Abortion bans were for other women. Careless women. Unlucky women. Women who'd made choices they shouldn't have. Not women like Emily Waldorf, who wanted her baby, who'd named her, who worked at the hospital where she was left to bleed.
But pregnancy is a risky act. It always has been. It can go wrong in ways that have nothing to do with want or choice or virtue or how you voted. Your body doesn't check your ballot before it hemorrhages. Your placenta doesn't ask your political affiliation before it fails to detach, as Emily's did. The fetus you desperately want doesn't survive just because you believe life begins at conception.
We should be voting as if it could happen to any of us -- _because it can_. Because it does. Because the woman in the next hospital room, told to wait while her infection risk climbs, might have voted exactly the way you did and still ended up exactly where she is.
What do women need to go through before we stop voting against ourselves? What does it cost? How personal does it have to get? Emily Waldorf had to be strapped into an ambulance with a life-threatening condition and shipped four hours across state lines before she understood what the rest of us had been screaming about for years. What's the price of admission to believing women when we tell you what's coming?
Because we always tell you. And we're always right. And somehow it's never enough -- until it's you.
I have friends -- both lawyers, both smart, both people I love -- who ended a wanted pregnancy because of a genetic marker that made the fetus nonviable. Quietly, with excellent medical care. Then went right back to telling me I was catastrophizing about Roe. This was in 2016. I told them what I'd been telling everyone: the court seats, the long game, the fifty-year strategy the anti-abortion movement hadn't bothered to hide. Roe was finished, I said.
_You 're being hysterical. That would never happen._
They've never apologized. Never said: you were right, we were wrong.
And I think I understand why.
It's because on some level, they always knew they'd be fine. They're wealthy, educated, connected. If they needed an abortion tomorrow, they'd have one. The ban was always something that happened to other women. Women without options. Women who couldn't get a lawyer involved and a transfer arranged and an ambulance dispatched after five days of waiting to nearly die.
Emily Waldorf needed a lawyer to get an ambulance.
My friends would've chartered a jet.
The same country built both of those realities and called it pro-life. When in reality, they're not pro-life. They're anti-women.
They _hate_ women.

They're coming for no-fault divorce next.
Don't argue I'm being hysterical. [The](https://substack.com/redirect/b303b9c7-3eb8-4b1c-bf58-25a02e7cc07c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [evidence](https://substack.com/redirect/b619d3ce-4479-4a51-97b0-ecda1b7be2e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [is](https://substack.com/redirect/4fa9021a-5963-4f85-9ef4-7c24909c48a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [clear](https://substack.com/redirect/5d2fcac8-7aaa-4cf7-8b2f-53f612295b15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [I'm](https://substack.com/redirect/8ee9d38f-4413-47da-a17f-41def8551e87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [not](https://substack.com/redirect/395ebe8d-070c-4df6-afb1-1168caf0a3c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The argument in conservative legal circles is that no-fault divorce -- the ability to leave a marriage without proving abuse or adultery -- destroyed the family. That women were given too easy an exit. So their proposed solution is to make leaving harder. To justify cause, to require proof. They want you to stay until you can demonstrate, to a court's satisfaction, that you've earned the right to go.
Of course this is aimed squarely at women.
Women have every right to leave a marriage and they don't need to explain why. Life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness and all that. We're entitled to end a marriage if we're dissatisfied for any reason. The simple wish to longer to be romantically, legally, or financially linked to a husband should suffice.
Conservatives disagree.
Since women fought and won access to our own credit, mortgagee, and business loans, our dependence on men has evaporated. Now women file for divorce at significantly [higher rates](https://substack.com/redirect/d48e9d66-5635-4e11-a7c4-0224be18b389?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than men do. That's not because women are fickle or destructive. It's because women are, statistically, more likely to be unhappy in marriages -- more likely to be carrying the invisible labor, and more likely to have subordinated their careers, ambitions, and friendships. The no-fault exit was the minimum acknowledgment that a woman's desire to leave was reason enough.
Conservatives want to take that back.
And they're not stopping there.
Birth control -- actual contraception, the pill, the IUD -- is under [legislative pressure](https://substack.com/redirect/3f2fcb47-ed29-40d1-a8f3-6a0b0c5c0280?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in ways that weren't imaginable a decade ago. _Don 't be hysterical_, _no one 's coming for birth cont -- _SHUT UP. Seriously, just stop.
[THEY](https://substack.com/redirect/40e5e017-8b75-4976-b8ea-a619c21fe7cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [ARE](https://substack.com/redirect/b0dde676-6272-41a1-838f-286cd9855dd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [COMING](https://substack.com/redirect/53776849-33c6-4aeb-b2ef-3af39681b095?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [FOR](https://substack.com/redirect/850abf0d-0ebf-456a-b88e-6305fe4d480e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [BIRTH](https://substack.com/redirect/593684ae-b876-4d69-a476-290a22d9a272?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [CONTROL](https://substack.com/redirect/5cc53251-0fc8-42fc-8c84-1aa138cbf8b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [TOO](https://substack.com/redirect/47af3321-75d5-4de2-ac61-11c6072ac4b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The playbook doesn't change. Only the target does.
The logic isn't about families or faith or any of the things they say it's about. It's about access. It's about control. If they can't control the body through abortion law, they'll control the life through marriage law. If they can't control that, they'll control the contraception. Keep her contained. Keep her pregnant. Keep her from having the clean break that lets her rebuild. Keep her from having the agency that lets her leave in the first place.
They want to control us, because they hate us.
They just dress it up in the language of stability and tradition and family values, and they wait for us to stop paying attention.
We're not going to stop paying attention.
