Then there is Thomas Jefferson. Only thirty-three years old.
His draft of the Declaration already rests before Congress, yet the words are no longer his alone. They are questioned, revised, debated, defended. I cannot help but wonder whether he had any idea that children two and a half centuries later would memorize sentences he wrote in a small room in Philadelphia.
Roger Sherman is here.
John Witherspoon, the Presbyterian minister, is here.
Charles Thomson's quill never seems to stop moving. Someone must preserve every motion, every vote, every decision. History always needs a witness.
Richard Henry Lee's resolution declaring these colonies "are, and of right ought to be, free and independent States" hangs over every exchange, even though Lee himself has returned to Virginia because of illness in his family.
Outside, another wagon rattles down the street.
A merchant greets a customer.
A church bell marks another hour.
Life continues.
No one outside knows that inside this room the course of history is changing.
I wonder about the silence between the speeches.
Did Adams search the room for one more vote?
Did Jefferson quietly reread his own words?
Did Hancock look around the chamber and wonder how many of these men would still be alive a year from then?
I wonder whether any of them slept well that night.
They do not know they will become the Founding Fathers.
They do not know there will be a United States of America.
They do not know whether this experiment in liberty will survive even a single generation.
They know only this: if they fail, they will die as traitors.
One thing, however, is beyond debate. The rights they are defending do not come from Parliament. They do not come from King George III.
The document before them appeals to "the Laws of Nature and of Nature's God." It declares that all men "are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights." Before it is finished, it will place "a firm reliance on the protection of divine Providence."
Those are not ornamental words. They are the foundation beneath everything else.
The afternoon grows late. The debate pauses. The delegates gather their papers. Some leave together. Others walk quietly into the warm Philadelphia evening.
Tomorrow they will return. Tomorrow they will vote. Tomorrow history will ask them for an answer.
As I stand in Washington 250 years later, I am grateful that America's story did not begin with fireworks. It began in a stifling room filled with imperfect men who disagreed with one another, counted the cost, and anchored their hope in something higher than themselves.
Tomorrow my feet will walk these streets of Washington.
Tonight my heart remains in Philadelphia.
Before we celebrate America's birth, I wanted to spend one day with the men who did not yet know if America would be born at all.
On this July 1, I pray that the same God to whom they appealed for wisdom, courage, and divine Providence will once again grant our nation hearts humble enough to remember that freedom is never merely inherited. It must be guarded, cherished, and entrusted to every generation.
If you'll meet me here tomorrow, we'll walk back through that door together.

body:
We’re going to lower our tempo for a few days now, ahead of July Fourth and the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The work doesn’t stop, though.
#
Peter:
We emailed quite a bit in advance of our quarterly FEC deadline at midnight last night, but not without good reason.
The impact VoteVets has depends on the resources we’re able to raise well in advance of the elections this November. We pushed hard to hit our goals last night because every dollar we raise now we’re going to put into winning critical races, and taking back the House and Senate. That work doesn’t start in October, or November. It’s already months underway — and we can’t let up.
But thanks to the support of thousands of donors, giving an average of around $25 online, we not only hit our goals for Q2... we beat them. So, from all of us here at VoteVets, from the candidates we’re backing, and from the people they’ll go on to fight for in Congress: Thank you for sticking with us.

subject: Will the persecution EVER stop?
body:
We J6ers don’t usually get much good news, so when some came my way, I had to share it with you.
---
[View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e7250491/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvbUNDRHVWelFZSA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA3MDE/LbmNsYmdCU2xRRA/qP2hpZHM9bmM0WkxTUlplZllXOGFscw/gakWVRQ/s4r023cf54f)

| | |

[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
Patriot,

We J6ers don’t usually get much good news, so when some came my way, I had to share it with you.

The DOJ had two pages about me on their website. A guilty verdict page from March 2023 and a sentencing page from October 2023. When I search "Shane Jenkins DOJ," both show up on Google.

But when you click either link — THIS is what you get.

_**"Page not found."**_

Gone. Scrubbed. Erased. The Department of Justice is actively removing their own anti-J6 propaganda.

They built those pages to destroy our reputations. Now they're quietly deleting them.

_**But here’s the bad news...**_

**There are still people in our government who are weaponizing it against J6ers.**

The DOJ’s $1.8B “Anti-Weaponization Fund” just got paused by a federal judge. Other politicians are proposing a 100% tax on J6ers who receive money from the Anti-Weaponization Fund.

The J6 community doesn’t know what comes next, but here’s what I know for sure: We won’t lose hope. We’ll keep fighting. This isn’t over.

My organization, Stand in the Gap, exists to provide real, practical help, like rent money, job training, transportation, legal referrals, trauma counseling, and health insurance, to help these persecuted patriots move on with their lives.

**By supporting Stand in the Gap, you are helping a former J6 defendant find the help, hope, and healing they need to succeed in their second chance.**
[Give a J6er a Second Chance Today](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
There are hundreds of J6 defendants right now in need of help.

Even though they pardoned us and acknowledged the weaponization was REAL, there are still people in power who want to take every single dollar back that would help make us whole.

**Let that sink in...**

The last 5-plus years have been an absolute nightmare for J6ers. Still, some of the most powerful individuals in the country are trying to keep everyday, working-class Americans from receiving the compensation they need to get their lives together!

These patriots have been financially drained after over half a decade of brutal legal
battles, imprisonment, and persecution.

**Stand in the Gap was created for this moment: To resurrect their futures after being continuously attacked and defamed.**

But we can’t do it alone.

We need your help if we are ever going to help them get back on their feet.

[Will you help J6ers heal physically, mentally, emotionally, and spiritually by donating $10, $35, $50, or even $100 to Stand in the Gap today? >>](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate $10](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $35](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $100](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $1,000](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate Any Amount](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
In solidarity,

Shane Jenkins
Founder and Executive Director of Stand in the Gap

P.S. Stand in the Gap believes in second chances, providing support to individuals transitioning back into society after incarceration, and working towards a more forward-thinking and restorative prison system that sends non-violent offenders into the world better off than they were when they went in.

This isn’t about politics. **It’s about justice.**

These are real Americans — veterans, first responders, fathers, mothers, hard-working citizens — who exercised their First Amendment rights and were persecuted for their political beliefs.

_**If you won’t fight for our fellow patriots now, who will?**_

Every dollar helps Stand in the Gap provide relief, resources, and hope to Americans who have been put through hell simply for being on the wrong side of the political establishment. [Give a J6er a Second Chance Today](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

" Have you abandoned Trump?" " If you cared, you'd donate..." Those are just shameful. So, I recorded a personal message for you to say the two words that aren't said nearly enough in politics... THANK YOU. (please see my entire message below) Thank you for volunteering, for voting, for donating - thank you for all the blood, sweat, and tears you've poured into our Party. God knows you 've gone the extra mile. The idea that you've "given up" just because your voter file wasn't 100% complete and up to date is utter nonsense. Frankly, it's insulting. But I want you to know that some of us DO thank you for everything you've done. And if you have a moment, I'd sincerely appreciate it if you could verify your voter profile - because as of today, we are less than 149 days from Election Day. ... And I assure you - the Democrats' voter file is near-perfect right now. With less than 149 days on the clock, the single most critical step we can take to beat the Democrats is to make sure our file is 100% verified - and stays that way every week between now and November. So, I 'm humbly asking you to please verify your voter profile today, so we have every tool at our disposal to WIN the midterms. [[LINK]]() For God and Country, Sen. We just got some bad news, Friend.
**The Supreme Court just handed billionaire donors and special interests another major victory.**
In a 6-3 ruling, the Court struck down longstanding federal limits on how much political parties can spend in coordination with their candidates, **opening the door for even more money to flood our elections.**
Justice Elena Kagan warned in dissent that **this decision creates a _massive loophole_ that allows wealthy donors to effectively sidestep existing contribution limits.**
This is yet another example of the rules governing our democracy being rewritten in ways that benefit the powerful while making ordinary Americans' voices matter less.
As outside money pours into elections, Democratic Secretaries of State responsible for ensuring elections remain fair, transparent, and free from political interference are feeling the pressure on our election system continue to grow.
That's why DASS is working to elect Democratic Secretaries of State in the battleground states that will oversee the 2026 midterms and the 2028 presidential election.

Set the mood at your carne asada this weekend! | | | Hey Peter, what does our future sound like? This Fourth of July marks 250 years since our nation’s founding. For much of that time, working people have been cast out of the story of this country. Right now, millions of us are struggling to make ends meet, while the administration tries to tell us who gets to belong here. We’ve had enough of our lives being treated as disposable. Together, we’re ready to organize and make the next 250 years better for all of us. **And, we know that community will be the key to bringing our vision to life!** **Hanging out with your friends and neighbors this weekend?** 🪇🌴We just dropped THE Fourth of July playlist to stream at your next carne asada or BBQ with friends. Peter,

I know you probably get a lot of urgent emails like this from Republicans.

That's why I try to avoid contacting you unless it's truly necessary. When you see "Chairman Tim Scott" in your inbox, I want you to know it's something that's not just _important_ , but **[vital](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/FY1XavY0tUNTaskciFdzVOJmNJjxlEFJzAsjjQSbUqwNngRf8ghIlVO94TnXJBWkqw3dWWLDa4Hy_8A2HG6d-N4auilDbFGcrh7JIZkeoffvWcCywqCVmwUx4QFbPgwVb-bHA8L1f8pUnltiRze9-ov-i-TwKBvLI55bzryBiPmbxPItKliAWMGlTipSqGjTmKGpfmD347K2HI7Lrsyj32BItRci7MdoTufoA5Uk8X106sDuWHKfKv8q-bn51z62wjlZr03rMAnKYpOLxWqaW7ynT9-KqYlMAnrrkTHJ9Tl3CM8SafaqiKWq1-tHZxNLNOaJzAzzjqU8LUsolfLou6C9n37JxPDMt3mIESYn7Bk_2EUUA8e964oo1yqQSvDjFGA5-HFjamQEt-_Py7Af8AiJMB6S9VdkmhEVKTjVPGqrPtgN7OUZvuADiwC3yI7OyMFJ_oKHGPyF8Ug0ouvwuaQEbvJJyDLhDv6HrrtZ34o6v-zC71yHDDW58uyBeW9E_KckIBmwpxluBWPoXZiS2HYyjZwkUxrkibTyuLSPPdr8QrLD5ipeyMmjuQC1FGowRBAcU2oYIe_6H85da_N6X_dMwOtUMLHZUAGMsMqLctNAr7YRW-GPtQZw8BZwtw0p46PkNp6MPAqrfErywntZQm9qWCRf02ALKjlA9M83844npVwbSTQWitlikgbm-bB143pvi70y25rrYAFX8zdwg4WqTW8UDyShVc_2YMj1RfKRm-jGiaMZVotLTc_4E1wqXjyjGZNqEldNs6vnzpqQalH4KiXDTP12TqwDm-20QqN9_AwhrnyREa7erXFzRMzRVoxf8RM0_4e2H3YmxknDK3zNzl2EmgiXwDr4MhLm1naooN6Xg7hvnI9Ea1TABRu6YPFm69jIj4hZPB2eEQ_MA9Xd5BLh9Qux1qEl4OiyJ3A1deu3SHd6ExiH0RbLLlm4KnocSmjF7IbsqGN2DKycmHz_dPdNUrGMjl3LHmmMOHQxnYpTAR5p4ld9Qwez1ojcX_SzvDYFEVIjT3s24ULthDgfYAbydp_nCo5BvEtv_Tc31VwpBA/iLlgVp4KCdwPqHNPayfsiEb146Tb87EP/22)** to the success of our Party.

Well, what I'm about to tell you will make - _or break_ - our chances of defending the President's Senate Majority in the midterms.

**[As Chairman, I was just briefed on some extremely troubling polling numbers in both Texas and Georgia, where the latest data actually shows radical Democrat Senate candidates LEADING our Republican nominees.](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/5UU--sJy3cQC9BKRhtzlLKrrqX7oFddzeuH_pBMZN9PxUps_woRzmCQF7pei5YCV1_1Uhr58VuRifVPZ1gsk3UpYMeicsnH6u1csfH6X9QyOVEqNa3CV3Sca0b-r0PnjcuKFPMBoXqqYc7vI2sN3s2-5jMGW9bbdGUbfW6GQwfx_VNqJdRaCjbNilmTqEg6c_yAymXwoEgTZPTSpeK7jWivlspmd9BezPZh0L6tubT1OSmHIUf5nt5hc9ERheioH4w2FBxfb-ieZdPGVGgmbLBaMo9spl-Rymwk_4USJaXb_-EMbPIbTkNWL3__JX2hWlbrR7ff4htKTHOp4lYw6AimFSCFdxD9_rg2W-lH5Y4VPEHk2Fa0uShmLdWGzNDpMJWyFZZCnzDB1E9Hn9HXOy3MBoWz3j8S7t3t3QGJk8reaKr48YewAX1cnUiN7zenYe2UWlmcQqPOcxA51rNY7_xBlWQWzW-WkEw6OMJpsXJro2syJrdx2NBpMKn9MsYrpBVFo7vsmvAWnQ9PkygpOpjIxtMyH-o4TohezMhHKr8a_bckTFcWcgIMTbnOBkQOZ3BFxKeu7iOMrz013PjkXXtzp5TrILAJBnONMa_3Pi7EuS49RBaIoeVnzBRz4G85p0-1nuo050YPbtbht9C0WfY3-tpau6CtgPSfKlnPjNoJkyA4ypU4BYgfkvY9W4mXTkyUhktAmseO8acDKD-eC-pKWwkL8NKyX7Q_jub5czX9jgZLYKciAlQ4rNUg_5bgyYd78VhGUDZZWiMMu5vEWLcje5pUSgvpW_tEdZGAVBo-koQ3wMdI2PQ9xc3Hml7td3g5yxjyIyN5eFS5mVtsW_wtzx5sxsu2bqmnm-YOsJ64InZfnQMFgVpIm1A1fzsAXTs5XlP_tvOaGRxvt5U1W9jkYwekvmmIaMMTBua88aXS5jJl6hkqKTaOiulc04A3HB0HmoEk3OVsJxhQEPMC6NxCetSuHt9yTWeAWiLbJFdyZKTb9LKRHccil-iFa423cppnNh1p_8EKEcrv67FWpMXRAuxQrlmSnM0UgAyYYgEHT_HjPUw/AdxckvFqbPLWqjD0StNOGztahcSuspUb/22)**

If these trends hold, our conservative candidates could be in real danger!

And the same reason we're falling behind in these key states is the same problem we've been seeing for the last year: _Too many Republican voters are sitting on the sidelines!_

_Some politicians have resorted to criticizing GOP voters, even going as far as to accuse them of being "Democrats" because they don't feel motivated to cast a ballot._

I'm not going to do that. A vote has to be **[earned](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/3AtaJYizqjmjwqsz817I2ZFw1vnEUBEEAjbCv58hlNdB0KZupz49rXReFba3O-kvESb2Pp7jYRG8pAC3AJ1tUxere8gfHD-XFlHDhh3U4F3Um-N5C_yGAu9OsicP1_wC3pHQ4GAwgC2F3aLr0uQmvhDwLTyVpsRf8oESgecByxF13XjZYFb2NaWl75h0d8DQzgrlz_l8P9zr2brJZ-lYU_5RkogK2_mRThCkt5LYA4KeEfxyBrfhIpqsB7yKu8N6jlruxh-MMY30O-f6ls79lw96CoYY9z7TdDJ4vB3pIFgfKLhphwWYqeZMmHv8fhzK9sWT8Alh4NZ-r2pYCEbqXm82zh62Uq8KII1WZNM2czcNIZJIXgT51hhQgP_O9kvEeUCMC97VvQrC9Yd4GdWJTi_tFovCg3qjVokbVaX4fMBEgLZs6R15wURPMk3r1PsFOhf20N3c6GP95SoR4dBRHnuEe4aTZOwEXCAbez4Ya3hB_xmFSq0E2oUqmmr1IP_Hf7e378mEnEhHq_LLVWe7fgowl-P7i0GnFkhYhKVBM4cQvTT8QEY5-WRnmZ1FvPtWH0dS3PLys1Qen6l47lJwKfW1g3bI8FZSwZX9xzpMMlG5NXvKD0r9yaMkaudmL95Ye0BxTZEkKQYMY9T6WrKSqbxC_SHywvpPfWR7YDwKNvYP8ZR8MKDEP3pQflJ0IClhSX1AkA4L4BAv-EapYpeO-Un7tqv9VfminAsahJPckivnDvXrqBigdAS7F4v09Psai32gW7CpGcP8kvLRll-HGPCRhFJBxAzZXkozYdsVMly1L-XYNUUXlGgSOVklrXpr1NV89SBjyzWdviaJSOu0eondwuaApQpFfwTrUY1tswMaG2RCuE605_xc1a-TPLxab21y0wzT-AQEeWxicOErDAlhMOD9ymUyrEMBrQ7x61Y8E2SSIwO5Q6DNMsZZ6xltkLvNlsX3QD-bGvOS2Y5BF0iRImLtyLNeRuz5KvDp4_3lbnGwUJrvoJ9J_4xiC_TJvBf65kqoo7GwiWbmdGgxFrlLCnzodFOcsmLqLN8hbezcBfKTNw/7VNfFFyMA9qUZrHRG0woYOdVeClVkx-Y/22)**. We're not entitled to it!

If we want America First conservatives like you to show up and vote for us in November, then we need to make sure that we're fighting for _YOUR_ top priorities.

Oh, Andy. Sweet, perpetually triggered Andy O'Brien--the face of the Maine AFL-CIO, the man who most adores Graham Platner (but not in a gay way), and the guy who turned "labor spokesman" into a full-time gig as a leftist sh*tposter.
This week, our boy took one look at a perfectly reasonable Democratic strategist's column in _The Hill_ --written by Laurie Watkins, who had the unmitigated gall to say maybe her party shouldn't whitewash character concerns around alleged abuser Graham Platner just because he's carrying the D label--and fired off the rhetorical equivalent of loading a Mosin-Nagant.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..HhzS_4d3kBUhBCZyffgUilMo47b8l88__Cz5AzSCtYg?)
"First up against the wall when the revolution comes," he posted to Facebook, along with a screencap of Watkins' blog post.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ac49e7f0-e4a5-4402-8bda-995a3898ddb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In other words, this Democrat stooge--who counts among his closest allies luminaries like Troy Jackson, Shenna Bellows, and several publications that run his freelance ramblings--was calling for the executions by firing squad of political dissenters.
Charming stuff from a top surrogate and fanboy for Platner. Perhaps the two mama's boys are a good fit, considering Graham is the Senate candidate who, on his pre-deletion Reddit greatest-hits album, proudly declared he "got older and became a communist," hung with the Socialist Rifle Association crowd, and dropped gems about how an "armed working class" is a "requirement for economic justice" and that fighting fascism might require reading up on when violence is justified. Andy's been out there canvassing, Substack-defending, and generally simping harder than a teenager at a boy-band reunion for P-Hustle. Maybe what really brings them together, apart from a dysgenic love of communism, is the desire to murder the unbelievers.

Followers of Maine politics will not be surprised to learn that no Maine Democrats condemned O'Brien's call for political violence. No Democratic officials, at least. That's not their style. They would expect a pile-on from Republicans were the shoe on the other foot here, and Republicans would obsequiously oblige. But Maine's top Democratic officials and party leaders remained silent. Not even a performative "violence has no place" press release from the party that spent years treating every January 6 tourist as a budding Timothy McVeigh.
If this were a conservative spokesperson floating the same line about a NeverTrumper, we'd have hearings, cable-news panels, and a fresh "stochastic terrorism" white paper from every think tank with George Soros in the donor Rolodex. Indeed, O'Brien would be the screechiest of all the harpies howling about right-wing terrorism. But when it's a lefty union guy cheering on the guy with the communist Reddit receipts? Crickets from the likes of Gov. Janet Mills, Sen. Angus King, Rep. Chellie Pingree, and whichever dork is running the Maine Democrats these days.
The Maine Republican Party and even U.S. Sen. Susan Collins were the only ones with the moral courage to condemn the naked call for political violence.

When will Maine Democrats realize that their party has been totally hijacked by political extremists who fantasize about violence like Andy? The Democratic Party used to stand for economic equality. Now, Maine Democrats represent the wealthy lawyers, lobbyists, and the from-away coastal elite. The old sayings about equal opportunity have been total replaced by "equity" and equality of outcomes, which necessarily means tearing down the successful, the fortunate, and the beautiful. Maine Dems read about [Harrison Bergeron](https://substack.com/redirect/f98e6458-778a-4478-bd98-e2562236a3c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and imagine ways to implement that in public schools. Maine Democrats are now united by Jew hatred and a desire to abolish the only liberal democracy in the Middle East.
Andy O'Brien only gave voice to the threat that hangs over everyone who still calls themselves a Democrat: Obey, or else. And the "or else" is real. Refuse to toe the party line, you'll face economic ruin and silent slander. Democrat members who buck leaders at the State House leave caucuses crying. Remember Rep. Bruce White? But the threat from Democratic extremists is more than just career homicide. Just last week, a very wealthy Democratic donor expressed grave concerns about potential threats to her physical safety that might flow from the Platneristas. Simply put, Democrats are terrified of Platner and his bioleninist cabal of extremists.
Maybe O'Brien's post will be the straw that breaks the proverbial camel's back.
A few brave Democrats risked their reputations, as well as their personal safety, to condemn the AFL-CIO's bloodlust. Jill Barkley Roy, director of the far-left 501(c)(4) Emerge Action Fund, cynically lamented that nothing would be done about O'Brien's call for violence, but she added yet another dimension to the behavior of the AFL-CIO's keyboard samurai: "Nothing's ever going to be done here, but someone who's harassed Maine women up and down the state for MONTHS is now calling for the author of the op-ed I posted earlier to be EXECUTED," Roy posted.
"This is so beyond anything else he's said or done, and he's said and done a lot this cycle," she said.
Well, that's intriguing... If you're reading this, Jill, politics makes strange bedfellows, and you can always drop me an email.
Although Gov. Mills was too busy to issue a comment, another member of the Mills family did chime in.
"Seems like his threatening and bullying post should be reported to law enforcement, his employer, the Platner campaign, and everyone associated with Mr. O'Brien," said Dora Mills, the sister of Gov. Mills.
"I do not know him, but this is completely unacceptable," she said.
Andy, bless his revolutionary little heart, contrived the perfect defense: It was just a joke! From _The Hitchhiker 's Guide to the Galaxy_!
Specifically, the bit about the Sirius Cybernetics Corporation's marketing division being "a bunch of mindless jerks who'll be the first against the wall when the revolution comes." (And fun fact for the literary pedants: the future _Encyclopedia Galactica_ entry notes they were the first--past tense. The purge happened off-screen.) Speaking of O'Brien's obsession with harassing or putting to death his political enemies... He somehow never got around to acknowledging the Southern Poverty Law Center's starring role in the very ecosystem of inflated "hate group" labels, donor-fueled activism, and selective blindness that props up the divisive identity grift he claims to oppose. The SPLC was literally funding the Ku Klux Klan--and even sleeping with some of them. Funny how the SPLC gets a lifetime achievement award for "fighting hate" while its own scandals, mislabeling machine, and cozy relationships with the activist outfits Andy adores sail right past his outrage meter. By the way, has anyone heard from Andy's BFF Christopher Polhaus since USAID and the SPLC got shut down? Hmm... Real talk, Andy--you're a character. Union lifer cosplaying as a revolutionary intellectual while shilling for an oyster hobbyist ex-Marine with a communist origin story. It's almost endearing, like a toothless, mangy Boston terrier convinced he's a dire wolf. But when we're done laughing at your antics, the question remains: How does any of this help the handful of workers in Maine who are still paying dues to the AFL-CIO? Keep the tweets coming, champ. Keep the Substacks flowing. Keep calling us Nazis while stumping for Mr. Kik and his Totenkopf. We'll keep reporting, keep laughing, and keep handing you the rope--metaphorically, of course. I miss the days when you made funny Temp Tales cartoons. Those just might be your best contributions to Maine. We're left wondering where that Andy went. So long, Andy, and thanks for all the laughs. Okay, okay... One last thing. We here at the Maine Wire found O'Brien's Reddit burner account a few years ago. Like his Totenkopf'd Titan, Andy likes to anonymously post to the leftist chat site. He's so boring and has such terrible taste in music, that we mostly use it as an inside joke. But there's one post I just have to share... | | ---|---|--- Andy O'Brien, the very smart, very savvy and funny face of the AFL-CIO, once solicited advice from veterinarians on Reddit about whether his cats testicles could grow back "like salamanders." Imagine the events that led up to this post. Andy, petting his cat while dashing off nasty tweets about everyone who disagrees with him on tax policy or project labor agreements, started to feel some tufts around his feline's butthole. He felt them and felt them, and he inspected them closely. So mystified, he pulled out a flashlight and a magnifying glass. "What possible could these ball-shaped clumps be," he wondered. Unable to solve the mystery himself, he took his quandary to Reddit, professing to the world that these balls hanging off his cats add were "kind of blowing [his] mind..." Andy, my brother in Christ, those are dingleberries. Go wash your hands. ? | | | | ---|---|--- | Jun 26 | | | | | * ---|---|--- | Jun 30 | You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. Team: When nearly two out of every three Americans agree on something, it's probably a good idea to do it. When it comes to the Electoral College -- a system that isn't equipped to handle the stress tests that opponents of voting rights are giving it -- we need to end it and stop letting cynical candidates game the system to take power.
Fuel our efforts to support a popular vote standard that will end the Electoral College forever with $35 or whatever you can right now >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=070126_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Pew Research Center: Majority of Americans continue to favor moving away from Electoral College [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=070126_3&amount=25]
As has been the case for over 200 years, the Electoral College determines the outcome of U.S. presidential races. Yet most Americans have long supported moving away from this system.
More than six-in-ten Americans (63%) would instead prefer to see the winner of the presidential election be the person who wins the most votes nationally. Roughly a third (35%) favor retaining the Electoral College system, according to a Pew Research Center survey of 9,720 adults conducted last fall.
We're clearly all tired of a system where all our candidates and their campaigns care about is whether the margin of victory is close enough in the state to make it worthwhile to campaign there instead of speaking to real Americans with real challenges.
The people who tell you we can't get rid of the Electoral College are wrong. Chip in $35 or more to help us change to a popular vote system once and for all >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=070126_3&amount=35]

subject: I wanted to say thank you, Derek
body:
---
Derek, I wanted to say thank you. We know that times are hard right now. It feels more difficult than ever to afford stuff that you and your family need to live. **Thank you** for sticking with us and opening this email. Thank you for doing what you can. Thank you for helping us hit our end-of-quarter goal so that we can grow our opposition movement. Every little bit helps. 99.7% of our donations come from grassroots donors, so we truly can’t do this without you. I’ll be honest: The next four months are not going to be easy. Democrats need to flip **four** Republican seats to take control of the Senate this November. That will mean winning races in states like North Carolina, Ohio, Maine, and Alaska. We also need to flip at least three seats in the House to take away Mike Johnson’s gavel. **Derek, all of this will take a _massive_ amount of resources — especially now that the Supreme Court just opened the floodgates for billionaires to dump even more money into politics. name: States Win (Formerly Sister District)
subject: We can’t keep failing red states
body:
Flipping just 17 state legislative seats would break four Republican supermajorities.
#
Dear friend,
The old Democratic playbook is failing red states.
For years, Republicans have built dangerous supermajorities that let them push through an extreme agenda with little opposition. But in Ohio, Kansas, Indiana, and New Hampshire, we have a real opportunity to change that.
In all four states combined, flipping just 17 state legislative seats would break four GOP supermajorities and end unchecked one-party rule.
**[PLEDGE TO BREAK REPUBLICAN SUPERMAJORITIES ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22895?t=1&akid=1676%2E2118727%2EWYWn4K)**
Voters are frustrated with the MAGA agenda and hungry for leaders who will fight for their communities. We've identified races where our support could make the difference — but only if we act now.
**[Will you pledge to help break Republican supermajorities and build Democratic power in the states?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22895?t=2&akid=1676%2E2118727%2EWYWn4K)**
In solidarity,
– States Win

# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=5063%2E898137%2E2z5NJA)

Because of your support, we’ve built the biggest grassroots campaign in this primary, and all without a single dollar of corporate PAC money. Seriously, your help means the world to me.

Socialism On The March
The Democrats' leftward lurch reached deep-blue Denver this week. Twenty-nine-year-old DSA organizer Melat Kiros, endorsed by Bernie Sanders, [ousted 15-term](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFuwyAYBOCnsTcsICHYA0MXb-na0fqBHwcFgwV_4j5-5Up9gc4nnb67r_tyh5hiXj9hQ1MpLL74pRUXIcVGzZVMMb-Q4InljYvk8sa4ZlwsOS2i98Y7D8L1aIQe5aQ417p_GKXDVQg9haCUFIAjwKhGDWqy3Fqr-mjOKq65kBd1vejBcSsnEbj39ia10t2VQ8JKQ8X9ZVN0kAnaM5TqcHBl65N5EO2tu3x0cu7kfBzHEMp3xqOdeSfnvaRI0bVOzn-LNrYWbOzARsw3YBbcEz1zD0gJ84qVlVejxlLJK8UNmcetuArUV-P3I6YU2-20rRvE9Ougf9z2NvInAAD__7vNgCE) Rep. Diana DeGette in Colorado's 1st District primary. It marks the third socialist House upset in a week, following the Mamdani-backed [New York sweep](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFyhCAUheGnwQ4HUGEtKNLYbdqUzhWuemcRHGDX5O0zm0dIf-bMN__Xfb4DBYrbJxxoc11nn_xckiMIVGpxKVaKT6zwwPTCWQmluTBcyDmGWTbeeudBugatNDc1DkIY0-y2lwOOuDrtdY-InR-lFzd566VY9CixIfu-EkZI1Q19Z1onFjXKVXi_aGUGw3oBAXNtM57PJZCDWKE81pQdti4dTbB7rWdh3QdTE1PTdV3tBWWnuNUU8RsOipjfU6amiFdhaup1p0SnmZoODFD5g3Iq3OOKUAvf07Mg93gkl6FyTxCBe9ywVuQU-ZnpgPzD1NRk68-LQqCi39LtAAp_qvqPiC-rfgMAAP__8_KDKA). Kiros campaigned on abolishing ICE, Medicare for All, and an arms embargo on Israel -- a platform national Democrats increasingly own heading into the midterms. Republicans [wasted no time](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2O6yAQhZ8Gd0R4_ENcUNzGXW67pTUehmQUbCwgWeXtV95H2OY0Rzrn0_d1W24oUfb7f9zY5RoWn_xSEglGKbVQ2qvsL6745PTmBQyM2lht2mWPS9t458ljSw271l5hGoyxtnk4GNdhCuNkrqM1PIQQkAg629PI3AfbiDunjDUtdEPf2QuZFaY2GO_XEexgVW8wcq6XzMdrjUK4VyzPkDLxhdLWRPeo9Siq-6dgVjB7lPghjJHz2SuYzwcFs7FntArmjSNW_ZScivaCO2rPd66VNaWYMvqkH-lVWHveEmWsQvrIsmH-KJib7PzxLTFKGU-8-4YSf1HqH8y9HfwEAAD__5L0fgc) branding the party captive to its most radical wing. ★★★
GOP Plans Midterm Convention
President Trump announced on Truth Social that Republicans will [hold a convention](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2unDAQRp8GOiNjfny3cJGGbtOmRMN4WEZrbGQPS_L20W6K9Lf89ElHR-fXfb4DB46Pn7CTy7LOPvm5JGQIXKRgisLxJIEnpRfNRptRaat0O8cwt7V3Hj20WJNr7Ze5DVpbW28OwHb9qq3uvrSFgRaP_TigH3RPsMCtZvdGaatb0w19ZxvUi7m1q_Z-GY0dbNVrCJSlyXScS2CEKFCea8pIDaa9Dm4TOUrV_ajMVJnpuq5mTb8jXeX9V2Y6UmBhLJWZ_kPUAVn-qC0VURsXSZlR7eyF8q4wxRdF4RSVhxCgKMnnfiiIMZ0R6bNlU_8C1dn54-IQuIxv38cOHD5u8o2UL2f-BgAA___4J4jQ) in Dallas on September 9-10 -- the first-ever midterm party convention. RNC Chairman Joe Gruters is billing the two-day event as a [midterm 'Trumpapalooza'](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2unDAQxfGngc4rYz6cLVykobtpU6JhPF5G19jIHiDK00e7j5D6SEd__X5_LV_AkdPrF-zkioTFZ7_UjAyRq1TMSTidJPBN-aLFaDMpbZXulhSXrvXOo4cOW3Kd_WGeo9bWtpuzvfc44To-daCwjiv5NYxD0ADUDWhadu8rbXVn-nHo7QP1ap5d0N6vk7GjbQYNkYo8Ch3nGhkhCdTvkAvSA_PeRreJHLXpfzZmbsx83_cj5D-J7vreGzMfObIw1sbMJaHCDbioo5BnlKoClyqKLipqZy9UdoU5XZSEc1JylqQ8xAhVSTn3Aw6IOf8F9SEI_NqkLc4fN8fIdXr3vnbg-GmT_6C8nPkXAAD__4zOiHw) designed to mobilize low-propensity MAGA voters before November. Strategists see the gathering as a way to [nationalize elections](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLtu6zAQRL-G6iSQqwftgsVt1Pm2KYUVuZIX5kMgaSufH9hN-nRTDGYOztdtuSF7jvt_DGRy3RaX3FKSZfRcarEpVo5Pqvig9KIFJEyt1K1US_SLapxx1qGyDRmlL3AdpdS6uZsNaAWFuElN2wAkJ5SKLrZ363UESQ2b95TUUkE_Dr3urFzhqjbp3DqBHrUYJHrKtct0PFfPFmPF8thSttTZFBpv7rUeRfT_BMwC5vM8uxPLneNeU6RvDBwpv6sC5khnETBbDAfyHj85xT1TKZwiegHzMPVKaxAw1_wMR-vQeyzt730b2FXKobUpvihWTlHA3GTjjpO95zK9ofeA7D-A9Q8-XwZ-AgAA__-W4ogP) around the president's agenda and energize the base. Democrats, by contrast, have declined to stage a comparable event, betting instead on a quieter turnout operation. ★★★

| | Dear Peter,
My name is Joan Wright. I'm a member of Workers Strike Back and a queer activist in Seattle. This past weekend, we volunteered at Pride events in Seattle and throughout the district. We talked to voters and queer community members about the candidates in this race and why they should vote for Kshama as a fighter for LGBTQ+ people and for all working people.
---
|
---
| | **Kshama is the only candidate in this race for Washington's 9th Congressional District with a proven track record of fighting for trans rights and standing with LGBTQ+ people.** And we need a fighter for trans people in Congress in the face of the right-wing attacks on our community.
---
|
---
|
---
| | In 2026 alone, 44 anti-trans bills have already been passed in 15 Republican-dominated states. Trump's executive orders have targeted passports, banned trans girls from sports, stripped federal funding from schools, and cut healthcare for trans youth. **Just yesterday, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 to uphold state laws barring transgender athletes from sports, a decision that will affect athletes in 27 states, including Washington, where anti-trans ballot measures are already moving forward.**
And we cannot pretend Seattle is a safe haven for trans people — Juniper Blessing, a UW student, was murdered in our city while simply doing laundry. One in five trans people have been fired or denied a job for being trans. One in eight have been evicted or denied housing. One in five have experienced homelessness. It doesn't matter if a city is a sanctuary city if queer people can't afford to live there.
Kshama’s main opponent, Democrat Adam Smith, has spent nearly three decades voting to fund endless wars, cut Medicare and Medicaid, break the railroad workers' strike, create and fund ICE, and send tens of billions of dollars to fund the genocide in Gaza. Big Pharma, the war industry, and the Zionist lobby continue to fund his campaign because he delivers for them. You cannot separate LGBTQ+ rights from the economic conditions trans people depend on to survive. Smith has betrayed us and all working people countless times.
The other Democrat in the race, Melissa Chaudhry, claims to be a progressive alternative to Adam Smith, but her campaign tells an entirely different story. She does not call for an end to military aid to Israel, for free universal public healthcare, to stop the AI data centers and mass layoffs, or to shut down ICE. During a recent candidate interview, she admitted she deliberately avoids even mentioning LGBTQ+ rights on her campaign website because she doesn't want to offend a particular community. **She said this as scores of anti-trans ballot initiatives are being brought forward across the country and the Supreme Court is attacking trans people.** **You cannot be neutral on this. You cannot be silent. You are either on the side of working and oppressed people, or you are not.**
---
|
---
| | Chaudhry’s own words explain the rest. When speaking at a Democratic Party event she announced: "I am a team player," clearly signaling that she is prepared to tow the line of the Democratic establishment. About Adam Smith she said: "Our incumbent has done some great work on housing" and "In many fronts, we are aligned, honestly." And when asked what she would do in Congress: "I cannot change the makeup of 535 people right now. I cannot convince 535 people of anything, but I can become one of them. Right?"
Wrong. That's exactly the problem. **We cannot replace Adam Smith with just another cog in the Democratic Party machine that has abandoned LGBTQ+ people.**
Kshama Sawant was my city council member here in Seattle, and I saw firsthand what a fighter in elected office can actually win. The $15 minimum wage (now $21.30) and the Amazon Tax didn't just benefit workers in the abstract, they dramatically improved the lives of queer and trans people in Seattle, who are disproportionately low-income, disproportionately renters, and disproportionately one paycheck from homelessness. And those victories spread to many places across the country, positively impacting the lives of thousands of queer and trans people nationwide.
Kshama is also the only candidate in this race with an actual track record of fighting for and winning LGBTQ+ rights while in office. Her office partnered with the Gender Justice League on a landmark LGBTQ+ Hate Crimes Forum, passed Trans Pride Day proclamations in consecutive years, and won hundreds of thousands of dollars for an LGBTQ+ senior center on Capitol Hill and an LGBTQ+ wellness center at NOVA High School. Kshama has also endorsed the [No Hate in Washington State campaign](https://us.list-manage.com/12IR5E0Q1TV?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15), calling for a NO vote on two proposed anti-trans ballot measures threatening the rights of trans kids and all other children in Washington state.
Kshama calls for:
* An end to anti-trans attacks and all LGBTQ+ oppression
* Free healthcare for all by taxing the rich, including full gender-affirming and reproductive care
* The Equality Act
* Emergency housing for trans and queer people fleeing abuse and homelessness
* A public-sector living-wage jobs guarantee
* National rent control and a massive expansion of publicly-owned affordable housing
* End all military aid to Israel

If we want to win these demands, we need to go all out to fight to get Kshama elected to Congress. The Democratic Party and the Republican Party have both been coordinating to try to keep Kshama out of the general election. The August 4th primary is five weeks away.
I have donated $3,500, the maximum amount, to Kshama’s campaign and I will be out every week and weekend volunteering to get her elected.
But we need an army of volunteers to defeat Adam Smith. I need you to donate to Kshama’s campaign, volunteer in person or on the phones, and tell everyone you know to vote for Kshama Sawant by August 4th.
In solidarity,Joan Wright
---
